Constantly using the fragrance of the precepts to anoint and polish the body, Always wearing the robes of meditative concentration to sustain the person, The wondrous fruit of Bodhi serves as universal adornment; In whatever place one dwells, there is constant peace and joy.
The wondrous fruit of Bodhi universally adorns all; may the patron of offerings always abide in joy through their devotion.
The wondrous fruit of Bodhi universally adorns all; may those assembled at the maṇḍala always abide in joy.
The six directions provide protection with a firm foundation; the ten paths submit without end.
If one violates the true teachings of the Three Jewels, one’s head shall split into seven pieces like an *āmalaka* fruit.
That night, the ritual arena was solemnly purified and the boundaries were firmly established. First, the Three Jewels were invited to serve as witnesses;
next, all spirits were summoned, with the hope that they would descend to grace the assembly. The master of offerings, with sincere devotion, bowed his body respectfully and made his invocation.
Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gaofeng, Volume II;
Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gaofeng, Volume III;
Section on Rituals Concerning Sound and Speech.

I respectfully request that the Buddha be invited, for the site of practice has been extensively opened and the Dharma assembly grandly inaugurated. The monastics stand in rows like a flight of wild geese, while the lay donors stand upright like cranes to pay their respects.
The golden bells have ceased their striking, and the jade chimes are tapped slowly; their pure resonance rings out in harmony, blending with the *brahman* chants.

His voice resounds with majestic clarity. He possesses the thousand auspicious marks of a single wheel and the ten titles of the Ten-Thousand Heroic Honored Ones. Seated upright upon a lotus pedestal, his robes drape lightly like morning mists.
His topknot rises like the verdant green of a mountain; his eyes are as clear and bright as green water. His lips are as radiant as red peach blossoms; his eyebrows are parted like azure willows.
Upon his chest is the imprint of the *svastika*; his feet tread upon a thousand flowers. His nose is as prominent as refined gold; his teeth are as white as pearls.
White jade. It unfolds the two palms of the Goose-King (Brahmā); it manifests the full majesty of the Lion. Lofty as a single mountain upon the sea;
bright as the solitary moon among the stars. Bodhisattvas and Pratyekabuddhas attend and follow; Śrāvakas and Arhats accompany him.
Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings all arrive; the eight classes of devas and dragons gather together. Vajra...
Holding halberds, they stand as left and right attendants; jade boys scatter flowers, kneeling with bowed waists.
They revere the towering majesty of the Sage’s virtue—this is the ultimate in honor. Beholding his solemn countenance, one gazes upon him with awe-inspiring dignity.
Great indeed is the Heavenly among Heavens! Sublime is the Buddha among Buddhas! How gentle is his harmony that can be known; how vast is his boundlessness that nothing can equal it.

Thus it is named. Now, as this mindfulness is present here and now, you have come and taken up your station. Yet, though there may be a thousand varieties of words, they cannot praise even a single hair’s breadth of your merit.
The Dharma conch is blown and the Dharma drum resounds; celestial music echoes and heavenly flowers fall.
You sprinkle down the fine, misty rain of Dharma and fan the brisk, refreshing breeze of compassion. You open wide the kitchen of Fragrant Accumulation and universally offer the *sudhā* nectar.
Through this feast, the Perfectly Awakened, the Nearly Awakened, and the Śrāvakas of vast awakening all provide witness and testimony.

Avalokiteśvara’s wondrous voice and ocean-tide voice are all brought back to the True Dharma; the eighty thousand afflictions are swept away in a single stroke, and hundreds of thousands of merits manifest as the Three Vehicles.
It drenches the heart like nectar and consecrates the crown like clarified butter. Why seek further for Maitreya Buddha?

Here and now, one is fortunate to behold the Teacher Śākyamuni. Facing the Awakened Sovereign with reverence, I hum this Buddhist verse; the faithful layman, with sincere devotion, prostrates himself in worship.
The verse on the Buddha Jewel, the Great Sage Buddhaya, says:
The Buddhas of the ten directions are like the great void; A hundred billion transformation bodies appear simultaneously.
With myriad jade-like features, Their thousand-fathom golden countenances are magnificently adorned.
The breeze of compassion sweeps vast and great, auspicious clouds swirl around; The rain of Dharma falls in fine mist, and the air is thick with auspicious radiance.
Gazing afar toward the Western Pure Land, I extend this invocation: I pray that you will descend upon this Eastern land to witness our boundless devotion.

I reverently burn bright incense and prostrate myself before the Upādhyāya, single-mindedly inviting [the Buddhas of] the ten directions throughout the entirety of empty space and the three periods of time.
The Buddha Jewel of the past, present, and future is infinite. We reverently contemplate this Buddha Jewel: with the marks of honor from a hundred merits and a wondrous body of a thousand lights;

having fulfilled the fruit after three *asaṃkhyeya*-kalpas, his grace moistens the nine realms of existence. His virtue and Way pervade both the distant and the near; his majestic spirit manifests transformations among humans and devas.
He unfurls the light from the hair-tuft between his brows to illuminate the sublime affairs of the human world. We humbly pray that he may mount the clouds and arrive at this end.

The colorful canopies embrace auspicious lotuses; the fragrance of precepts and meditative concentration wafts through the ten directions. The rain of compassion falls upon the three realms. Light mists are drawn forth, and refreshing breezes fan gently.
Celestial maidens scatter flowers, and the deities of space play music. The ceremonial ranks of the east and west line up, their colors soaring toward the heavens;
the banners and streamers of the south and north are arrayed, their radiant brilliance outshining the sun as jeweled bells chime.
The sound followed the wind’s resonance; when the golden bell was struck, its melody vibrated like the roar of the sea.
White sandalwood incense rose from the heart of the burner, and red lotus flowers bloomed fragrant beneath the seat. Śrāvakas led the procession, and Bodhisattvas gazed upon them with devotion.

The stars shone forth, illuminating the eight directions, and the roads were level, making the four suburbs vast and open. Having received this sincere invitation, we pray that you descend to this site of practice. Do not...
Relinquishing compassion, one realizes the merit of the proof.
(In a long-drawn tone: May the Buddha’s compassion be vast and his wondrous power inconceivable; may he descend upon this site of practice.
(The assembly joins in: Realizing the merit of the proof. Requesting with incense and flowers. Requesting with incense and flowers.
The Great Sage’s Dharma Jewel Gāthā says:
"The wondrous Dharma of the Three Vehicles is truly immeasurable; A single thought of taking refuge disperses calamities and misfortunes.
Indra reveres it and offers worship within his grotto; The Dragon King gazes upon it with respect as it is treasured within the ocean."
The numinous texts of five thousand palm leaves are inscribed; The golden-mouthed verses are contained within twelve lapis lazuli cases.
I pray that you will lightly open this precious treasury, Descend upon this Dharma assembly, and radiate light from your brow.
I reverently burn bright incense. With prostrations and *vaṃdana*, I single-mindedly invite [the Buddhas] of the ten directions throughout the entirety of empty space and the three periods of time.

The inexhaustible Dharma-treasures of the past, present, and future. We reverently contemplate this Dharma-treasure: the words bequeathed by the Great Sage within the dragon palaces and oceanic repositories;
the texts of the *pūrṇa* script revealed among the crags; and the verses on contemplating flowers inscribed upon leaves.

Some were written with gold melted to adorn the pens, others with blood drawn to moisten the brushes. When unrolled, the sandalwood rollers abound with fragrance; when wrapped, the scarlet silk cords are fine and delicate. Thus was it written.

The transformation of the magpie was accomplished; the concealment [of the scripture] was like the turning of a phoenix. Upon hearing four lines, a thousand obstructions were dispelled; with the proclamation of a single verse, the six sense-objects were purified.

The Way was fulfilled for the youth by the crags; merit was achieved for the wild jackal at the well. From afar, I have always gazed upon the Terrace of Prajñā; I revere this establishment of the assembly of the trichiliocosm.
All this arose from the reverence for the Dharma, through which I first obtained the opportunity to hear the Sūtra. A half-verse is difficult to encounter...

An encounter [with this teaching] is rare even over a thousand lifetimes. We humbly pray that you will open the Dragon Treasury and bring forth the jade-bound volumes, scattering the luminous flowers of heaven and spreading the auspicious joy of the human realm.
Let banners and streamers lead the procession from front to back; let bells and conchs vibrate their tones high and low. As pearl ornaments jingle, pairs of sounds resound;
as incense seals are divided, clouds of smoke drift and disperse. Having received our sincere invitation today, we pray that—
Descend upon the site of enlightenment. Do not abandon compassion; bear witness to our meritorious virtues. (In a long-drawn tone:
We pray that the Great Compassion of the Dharma and its inconceivable wondrous power descend upon this site of enlightenment. (The assembly joins in: Bear witness to our meritorious virtues.
Invocation with incense and flowers. Invocation with incense and flowers.
The Great Sage’s verse on the Saṃgha Jewel states:
The Śrāvaka Saṃgha Jewel is most transcendent among all; Having forgotten both fame and profit, their Way surpasses the Honored One.
Amidst the muddy waters of Lake Anavatapta, Beneath coral trees, they recite the sacred texts.
Dragons descend within the bowl, swirling in mist; tigers crouch before the crags, gathering in dense clouds.
We pray that you grant us your compassionate presence at this Dharma assembly; may wind-chariots and cloud-mounts descend in profusion.

We reverently burn bright incense and prostrate with palms joined, single-mindedly inviting [the Honored Ones] from throughout the ten directions and the entire realm of empty space, across the three periods of time.

The Sangha-treasure of the past, present, and future is infinite. I reverently contemplate this Sangha-treasure: those of the three vehicles and five stages, possessing the ten grounds and six supernormal powers;

their precepts as pure as frost, their minds as clear as mirrors. Whether through the cultivation and realization of the four elements, or the refinement over three *kalpas*, they exercise supernatural powers such as floating a cup upon the sea, or travel through worlds while shaking their mendicant staffs in mid-air. Entering meditative concentration in the smoky outskirts, they dwell among the peaks.
I uphold this sutra. The Bodhi tree is lofty, rising ten thousand *ren* with spreading branches; the ocean of merit is deep, vast and boundless for a thousand *xin*.

A single gaze and a single prostration dissolve the dust and toil of kalpa after kalpa; a single praise and a single exaltation ensure the perpetual growth of blessings and wisdom throughout all births.

I humbly pray that you will briefly leave the secluded valley to descend for a time into the human realm. May you float across the sea in your physical form and tread through the void with your feet, shaking the six rings of the subduing tiger.
With golden tongs, you hold the five-fold jade basin that subdues dragons; you whirl light silks amidst snow-white waves and part heavy mists beyond the crimson heavens.
Suddenly, you leave behind needlework in a stone chamber, yet enable the thread to follow the shifting mountain.
We pray you open the jar of Louyao and hasten to this evening’s assembly. Accepting our sincere invitation, we pray you descend to this site of practice and never forsake your compassion.
Compassion. To bear witness to the merit. (In a long-drawn tone:
May the compassion of the Sangha be vast and its wondrous power inconceivable; may you descend upon this site of practice.
(The assembly joins in: To bear witness to the merit. Invocation with incense and flowers. Invocation with incense and flowers.
I reverently burn bright incense and with single-minded devotion invite: the Honored One of the Mahāsattva Realm, the Arhat; Venerable Daoming; the Great Discerning Elder;
the Dharma-protecting deities within the assembly of the Triple Gem; and the host of the Eight Great Vajrapāṇis and Guhyakas.
I pray that you will not unsheath your frost-like swords nor bend your moon-like bows, but descend upon this site of practice to accept our sublime offerings.

We reverently contemplate the Three Bodies of the Tamer of Men, whose four wisdoms are compassionate and benevolent; the Pratyekabuddhas with their five eyes, and the Arhats with their six supernormal powers.

Their radiance encompasses the myriad phenomena, and their grace protects the four modes of birth. Their physical forms manifest the majestic majesty of golden features, and their light flashes forth from the white tuft of hair, shining with brilliant clarity.
His body is adorned with a hundred jewels, and his seat is embraced by a thousand lotuses. Brahmā and Śakra intermingle as his retinue, while lion-kings and elephant-kings lead the procession.
Throughout the human and celestial realms, he benefits beings and assists all who encounter him; wherever he is invited, he is everywhere accessible.
Without specific vows, he remains majestically sovereign. His inconceivable power is beyond full praise. We respectfully pray that you will descend and bear witness to these meritorious deeds.
Recite the Mantra for the Peaceful Treasure Seat clearly and with devotion. When chanting this mantra,
one must further realize that the myriad phenomena of the universe are all but atoms of buddha-lands, and that the purity of the ten directions is nothing other than the realm of all Buddhas.

The Dharma-body, though described as profound stillness beyond naming, inevitably responds to every sincere invocation. How much more so when the collective will is focused and the site of practice is solemnly purified:
golden censers burn lightly as auspicious smoke drifts upward, and silver candles blaze high as radiant light shines forth.
As the Dharma conch is blown, pairs of sounds harmonize like the cries of phoenixes; when the Brahma-voice resounds, couples seem to dance together like kalaviṅka birds.
Before the jade carriage, the four Bodhisattvas welcome [the Buddha]; behind the crystal dais, the eight Vajrapāṇis provide protection.

The assembly of monastics exhausts themselves in sincerity of devotion, and the donors offer their utmost prayers of reverence. Thus they invite the True Reality of the ten directions. Ten thousand...

Accompanied by a hundred million gateways of *dhāraṇī*, the noble Saṅgha endowed with the six supernormal powers free from defilement, and the host of deities of the eight classes, we pray that your holy mind may look upon us from afar and your compassionate ears hear us from a distance.
May you not fail to respond to our power of aspiration by coming to us, fully answering the sincere prayers of this heart.

Furthermore, I prostrate to the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, numbering as many as the atoms within the oceans of Flower Treasury lands—the Dharma-body, the Reward-body, and the Transformation-body;

those who have awakened themselves and awakened others, and whose awakening is perfected; who manifest the perfect True and Responsive bodies upon the thousand-petaled lotus thrones, and reveal themselves amidst the light of myriad virtues.
Auspiciousness! The Three Names and Four Wisdoms discern the true capacity; the Five Eyes and Six Supernatural Powers observe the Dharma-realm.
Śākyamuni, the Great Compassionate Father; Maitreya, the True Guide. Full Moon and Lapis Lazuli Light; Amitāyus of Sukhāvatī.

Samantabhadra’s ocean of practices and vows; Mañjuśrī’s wisdom and dhāraṇīs. Avalokiteśvara rescues the four types of birth; Mahāsthāmaprāpta leads those in the three realms of existence. The Ten True [Vows] are immeasurable.

The Buddhas of the vast and great vows; the three stages of worthiness and the eight liberations of the *pratyekabuddhas*; the four fruits of the *arhats*; the dragons, devas, and the eight classes of beings;
those of the watery realms and the human world; the steadfast deities of this realm; the records of good and evil merit; the local lords of this land;
the deities who serve the incense and lamps; all the sages and worthies; and the multitudes who rejoice upon seeing or hearing—having heard this invocation, [may you all attend].
May all deities descend and grace us with their presence.
The general text for the six offerings:

May the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time all arrive; may the sages and worthies of the ten directions all shine forth their presence. Though it is said that one should focus the mind with single-minded purity...

I focus my mind solely on these few offerings. Is there anything that does not include the burning of five-part incense, the offering of spring flowers, the lamp as the cause for transmitting the Dharma, and the tea as the auspicious sign for defeating Māra?
The wondrous fruit of Bodhi and the noodles of the Fragrant Accumulation Heaven—by offering these precious things to the Buddha, the Buddha-fruit is perfected;
by serving the Awakened Sovereign, the flower of enlightenment blossoms. I reflect that there is nothing insufficient for this purpose.
Behold the intent! Only through ultimate sincerity can one move the divine. I shall now proclaim each point in turn; I pray only that you will look upon us with compassion and grant your protection.
Incense.
This incense has once offered blessings for the ten-thousand-year longevity of the Son of Heaven and perfumed the body of the Dharma-King of the Fivefold Teachings.
It occupies the preeminent rank within the sandalwood forest and dwells as the highest grade among the orchids and musk.
Now, as we honor the Buddhist rites and present this sublime fragrance, we only pray that Your Sacred Compassion will graciously deign to accept it. (Ring the bell.)
The *vāra* incense offering wafts and melts away; Yaśodharā faced peril within the imperial palace, yet at that moment of calamity, she was moved by divine response.
Incense was burned within the fire-pit, where she was transformed into a blue lotus as the red flames subsided. Anāthapiṇḍada burned sandalwood and offered it to her wondrous countenance.
Rā-sumi rā-muñja-ruha-dūpa (substitute this word *dūpa*) maṇḍaṃ ca ga-dūpa-vittana-mijika tañjana-mijika mahājinaṃ kalumi.

The flower is indeed a flower. Within the pool of the seven treasures, it displays the beauty of a national beauty; beneath the moon, its single branch claims the fragrance of heaven. The World-Honored One held it up to show all people;
Bodhidharma transmitted it so that the five petals might unfold. Now we honor the Buddhist rites and offer this brilliant flower upward. May it be so.
I pray that Your Holy Compassion will graciously look down and accept [this offering].

(Ringing the bell: This *vara* flower offering is as fragrant as the thick spring air; emerald green and azure red blooms open in a lush thicket. The Tathāgata of Radiant Conduct is named the Hero among Śākyas.

With this King of Precious Flowers, I present my wondrous countenance. Having attained the three types of knowledge (*trividyā*) and realized the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), Kāśyapa of old once...
Pick it up! The enlightened nature is pervasive. *Lā-sū-mi* (chanting and responding as before; change *Duō-bō* to *Pǔ-xī-bō*). The lamp is the lamp itself.
A single point, unshaken by the eight winds; a square inch of mind, eternally bright through kalpas. The Buddha of the Western Heaven...
The Patriarchs have transmitted this to one another; may it dispel the darkness for all sentient beings throughout the great earth. Now we honor the Buddha’s work by offering these bright lamps.
We only pray that through your sacred compassion, you will graciously look down upon us and accept them. (Ring the bell.)
The *vara-dīpa* offering shines through the vast expanse of space. Its crane-like flames flicker brightly, illuminating the deluded and obscured.
Amidst ten thousand *hu* of ghee for the Jade Emperor, Āniruddha, with his divine eye (*divyacakṣus*), illuminates the three evil realms within the five sufferings.
Śāriputra constantly kindles it to illuminate the Brahma palace. [Recite as before; change *duō-bō* to *ní-bō*. *Rā-Sumeru*.

This is tea, indeed tea. Silver waves surge within the jade-green bowl; snowflakes fly beside the golden millstone. Only when the nostrils reach toward the heavens can one first perceive its fragrance;
only with eyes that possess true vision can the tongue finally discern its flavor. Now, as we honor the Buddha’s work, we offer this sublime tea. May it be so.
I hope for the Sage’s compassion to look down and graciously accept me (ringing the bell, he says):
*Vāra-miṇḍa*. The spring buds and sprouts are fresh; the white jade flowers part, their flavor most exquisite. Plucking them from the spear and banner, they spread through the mists and clouds.
The wild man acts: to quell the demonic and the heterodox. Grinding the jade into dust, floating the snow-flakes. Three sips of Zhaozhou’s tea.
Tea. Coming and going. Ra-sū-mi (as before, chant and respond; change *duō-bō* to *shí-gōng-bō*). Truly it is the fruit.
Cultivated in this land of merit, it has now ripened; where the flower of the mind blooms, it naturally forms. Within this, one should...

Presiding over the spring in the Imperial Garden, may we together realize the fruit of Bodhisattvahood beneath this very tree. Now that we honor the Buddha’s work, we offer this *āmra* fruit as an offering.
We pray only for Your Sacred Compassion to look down upon us and graciously accept it. (Rings the bell.)
*Varāko ki*. The green forest is like a jade cascade; ten thousand kinds of fragrant and beautiful fruits hang high on the branches.
Wild cranes and monkeys all gather them to return home. Chewing red apricots, the crimson fruit is delicious; its flavor fills the belly, and its emerald luster clings to the teeth.
Through long cultivation and realization over *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, one attains the wondrous principle. *Rasumī* (chanting the preceding refrain and changing the *duo-po* to *po-lo*).
This is food, indeed food. May it cause all sentient beings to be fully satisfied, enabling them to escape hunger and emptiness for ten thousand kalpas.

May this exquisite flavor of *sūda* be offered to the various devas, and may this food from the Fragrant Accumulation (*Gandhavyuha*) above be presented to our Buddha. Now, in honoring the Buddhist rites, we offer these precious delicacies above. Only...
I pray that Your Sacred Compassion will look down and graciously accept [this offering] (ringing the bell).
*Vara-pūṭā*. The six flavors are harmoniously blended; the cowherd girl’s boiled porridge is offered to the Buddha. A hundred kinds of rare delicacies are called *dhyāna*.
This manifests sincerity, bringing forth even greater merit. It presents the three virtues and the six *pāramitās*. Śakra, Brahmā, and the gods of the Pure Abodes.
In the kitchen, one attains the wondrous fruit. *Rā* (chanting and responding as before; change *duōbō* to *wàlíng*). Universally offering this tribute, I praise that which is immeasurable.

I pray only that you will compassionately grant your protection, so that all members of my household, young and old alike, may enjoy peace and security, and that our merit and longevity may extend eternally.
(For the rite for the deceased: "I dedicate these provisions to aid the deceased in rebirth in heaven, and that the filial kin may obtain increased years.")
The general text for the seven offerings:

As the ritual banquet is illuminated and opened, the worthy sages descend. Although supreme sincerity alone is sufficient to move the divine, material offerings are nonetheless necessary to manifest one’s intent.
Thus, with reverence, a single incense stick is burned; its smoke drifts in billowing, auspicious clouds, while several slender branches are gently plucked.
The appearance of the form reveals fragrant and auspicious luster; a single drop sprinkled becomes nectar. The seven tiers shine like bright stars;

the Dragon Ball is ground and releases a wafting fragrance; brewed in "crab-eye" boiling water, it possesses a true flavor. The pervasive scent before one is nothing other than that of the Gandhavyūha kitchen;
the perfect clarity upon the seat is entirely the seed of Bodhi. These are offered as a tribute to express sincere devotion.
Fragrant jade axes have carved the mountain’s soaring peaks; golden incense burners rise with auspicious smoke thick and dense. All those whose nostrils reach toward heaven smell it from afar;
the fragrance of precepts, concentration, and wisdom perfumes the entire Dharma-realm.
The five-petaled flower blooms here in this land; a single branch of the *utpala* grows in the Western Heaven.
When the World-Honored One held it up to show all people, Kāśyapa broke his countenance with a smile.
The lamp illuminates the dark thoroughfare, dispelling the gloom; it increases the brilliance of the Buddha-sun, making it ever more distinct. From lamp to lamp the flame continues to this very day;
from patriarch to patriarch the fragrance is transmitted, its light never extinguished.

The waters of the Western River are sucked dry, yet they find no place to enter his mouth; as a cloth of nectar, they moisten all living beings. The nine dragons personally spout forth water to bathe the Golden Sage;
for ten thousand ages, Caoxi remains an inexhaustible green.
When Old Zhao drank tea, how direct it was! Mañjuśrī holding up the cup was all too clear. If you wish to know this flavor that surpasses Mount Ya, you must have eyes of your own upon your tongue.
Diligently plant the groves of the fruits of merit; cultivate them with the creative power of the mind. What is plucked up arises naturally from roots of goodness;
when offered, it is perfected as a fruit beyond reproach.

The entire great earth is transformed into the realm of Fragrant Accumulation; its exquisite flavors are of a single taste, such as the world has never known. With one’s whole body serving as a mouth, one partakes and tastes, remaining forever satiated throughout ten thousand kalpas and thousands of lifetimes.
The general text for the twelve offerings begins:
The ritual arena is opened; the dharma assembly is solemn and majestic. Since the ritual implements have been extensively arrayed, it is hoped that one’s sincere heart may be manifested.

The fragrance of precepts and the fragrance of meditative concentration rise like clouds and billow like mist; the torches of wisdom and the torches of insight shine like the moon and the stars. The udumbara...
Flowers bloom, trailing auspicious mists; the fruit of Bodhi ripens, condensing nectar. Within a bottle of azure lapis lazuli, snow floats as one sips Zhaozhou’s tea;
in a bowl of red agate, frost clears as a single drop of Caoxi’s water falls. Every kind of precious treasure is fully present; every divine pearl is perfectly radiant.
The hundred flavors of the ritual gruel are pure and clear; the five-scented offerings for the vegetarian feast are refined and immaculate.

The robes of dawn glow with brilliant colors; the medicinal herbs are fragrant. Now, I shall present each one individually to the Able and Benevolent One (Śākyamuni), hoping for the bestowal of compassion and equal acceptance.
As for the incense:
The value of agallochum and sandalwood is beyond compare; as soon as they are burned in the golden incense burner, auspicious clouds billow forth.

Their fragrant smoke pervades the three thousandfold world-system, serving as a portent of good fortune as it circles the World-Honored One. Now that we honor the Buddhist rites, we offer this bright incense (substituting other items as appropriate).
We only pray that Your Sacred Compassion will look down upon us and graciously accept it. (Recite the *Wang* [Gaze] verse in the *Nan* [Southern] melody.)
Incense is offered: aloeswood and sandalwood, their hundredfold blended fragrance pervading the Dharma-realm.
As auspicious omens and portents, they swirl around the Sacred Mountain, entreating the Buddha to descend into the human world.
The flower was once plucked by the World-Honored One’s golden hand; Kāśyapa joyfully transmitted its wondrous meaning. From this, at Vulture Peak, he attained sudden enlightenment;
with its five petals on a single branch, it benefits humans and devas.
Offering flowers: By whom were these five petals planted? They grow by the steps of the Tuṣita Heaven;
they bloom before the Buddha at the assembly on Vulture Peak. Kāśyapa has transmitted them here.
The lamps, their ancestral flames brilliant and glowing, are arrayed upon the jeweled platform. Long ago, the Venerable One brought them here, prodded forth with an arrow.
Who would have known that these ten-thousand-bushel seeds of red lotus would scatter across the site of enlightenment and blossom this very night?
The offering of lamps illuminates all beings. The Dharma transmitted personally by the Master divides into the jewel-flames;
lamp after lamp continues in succession without ceasing. From this, the dark barrier is shattered.
Tea is made from early spring buds ground by stone wheels; when brewed, they rise upon the bowl like scattering milk-foam. Having sipped it, a pure breeze arises beneath both armpits;
do not say that Old Zhao was merely fond of brewing tea.
The offering of tea is wondrous in its fragrance and flavor. In days past, Zhaozhou personally cultivated it;
tonight, a lay devotee offers it to the Muni. As it is brewed, snowflakes fly forth.
The fruit is fresh and plump, presented upon a golden platter; the Chan practitioners of the four seas raise their eyes to gaze. Two phoenixes bring it and personally offer it to the Buddha;
even the wild monkeys still strive with all their heart to reach for it.
The fruit is offered as an oblation; the green jade chews the red incense. Its sweet flavor fills the belly and its fragrance permeates the crown of the head.
Held forth upon a golden platter, the jade vessel contains its fragrant essence. It is worthy of being offered to the King of the Dharma.
When Brahmā Śikhin brought the fragrant rice porridge, he still accepted the jade-milk gruel from the palace maidens; had his crown not possessed the vajra-eye,
why would Mañjuśrī have needed to take a single spoonful?
Having made this offering of the vegetarian feast, one no longer envies the celestial *sudhā*. A hundred flavors of rare delicacies are worthy of being offered to the Buddha;
though the heavenly kitchen prepares them, they are never in excess. After the meal, one attains *dhyāna*.
The waters are vast and expansive, with azure waves reaching to the heavens; they constantly ferry great ships across the dark ocean.
In the past, when a hundred thousand troops descended upon Mount Gui, the Bodhisattva brought them down upon the tips of the willow branches.

The offering of water follows the shape of the vessel—square or round. Once upon a time, upon the willow branches of Guanyin, it was transformed into nectar to sprinkle throughout the three thousandfold world system;
flames were transmuted into red lotuses.
The ointment is a golden cup of *śrīkhaṇḍa* sandalwood, most profound and fragrant; it is the consecrated *amṛta*, a jade-like liquid nectar.
It can eliminate the feverish afflictions of sentient beings and further cause the ground of the mind to attain cool clarity (as before).
Anointing offerings: nectar, milk, and jade nectar. Upon the sacred stone of Potalaka on the shore of the sea, the various immortals dwell in great fragrance.
Held forth, it emits a radiant glow.
The "Treasure" is the red furnace where the ore is refined; with the upper tongs and hammer, the golden-maned lion cub is forged.
Cease your scrutiny, lest you become like Bian He weeping in vain over jade. Within this, is there anyone who knows? (As before...)
These precious offerings are truly marvelous and worthy of praise; white jade and yellow gold are most noble, while coral and agate are flawless in their purity.
They are offered to the Buddha at the Dragon Flower Assembly.

As for the jewel, two dragons struggle over it without ceasing; this, however, causes the foreign monk to smile and nod his head. Do you know that he has personally obtained it from the ocean-treasury?
Do not seek it outside the realm of the *maṇi* jewel. (The rest is the same as before.)
The pearl is offered; the dragon maiden holds the maṇi jewel. Having realized the fruit of the Southern Stage of Purity, she attains Bodhi at the side of the lotus pedestal.
All throughout the three realms know this from afar.
The robe consists of nine strips and five seams, made of deep-purple sandalwood cloth. It was transmitted from Huangmei at the hour of midnight;
it could not be lifted when held at the side of the stone on Mount Yuling. The heavy tower remains locked at Caoxi (as before).
The robe is offered as a tribute; its five-colored radiance shines brightly. It remains enshrined within the multi-storied pavilion as the ancestral essence.
When the secret transmission took place at midnight in Huangmei, it was worthy of being offered to the Buddha Muni.
Medicine is what the world calls the Great King of Physicians. It possesses its own formula for longevity and immortality, capable of rescuing sentient beings from all their ailments and sufferings,
instantly transforming their feverish afflictions into refreshing coolness (as before).

This medicine is offered; its wondrous efficacy is truly immeasurable. It delivers sentient beings from all their ailments and sufferings. Among the world’s medicines, it is difficult to distinguish such excellent and superior ingredients.
Only within the mind-ground does the true prescription reside.

All the offerings described above, which are able to bring benefit throughout the entirety of space, I now proclaim as these wondrous mantras; may the assembly of sages and worthies all graciously accept them.
*Namo sarvatathāgataduṣpaprasādani-padapāramitā* (Homage to the one who causes all Tathāgatas to be difficult to please).

*Om amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtaśīle amṛtasambhave amṛtavati amṛtavarṇe amṛtagarbhe amṛtakeśe amṛtāyur-dade amṛtodbhavodbhūte amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtavarṣaṇi amṛtakuṇḍali amṛtamūrti amṛtasaṃmaye hūṃ.* (Recite once) *Oṃ gagaṇasvabhāva vajra hoḥ.* (Recite twice) Thus, make the universal offering.
With twelve sublime causes and conditions, present this praise with focused devotion in due order. May auspiciousness be invited and blessings gathered to clear away all obscurations.
Karmic Obstructions. The Boundless Mirrors of All Sages.
Volume Three of the Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gaofeng.
Volume Four of the Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gaofeng.
Compiled by the junior disciple Ruying, Abbot of the Sixth Patriarch’s Monastery,
this work sings in verse praise of the Triple Refuge of the Buddha-dharma.
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Tathāgata Maitreya, who dwells upon the lotus pedestal within the inner court. May he swiftly descend to birth among humans;

may he then convene the three assemblies under the Dragon Flower tree. With songs, gongs, dances, and offerings of flowers, the five-clouded celestial hosts manifest as auspicious omens for the Jade Emperor.
Beholding his sublime marks, one realizes samādhi; beneath the shadow of the wondrous banner, one reverently serves the Compassionate One.
Venerable One, with ears attuned to the music of the *shao* flute and the chanting of hymns, one departs from the three realms.

From the Tuṣita Heaven, one prostrates a thousand times in person before the Dharma, taking refuge in the sacred texts of the jade-axle, the numinous writings, and the precious verses. The names bestowed by the Tang emperors are unalterable;

these inscribed upon golden tablets in fragrant water at the ritual altar remain enshrined within the palace of the Dragon King. Those ordinary beings who hear the distinct teachings on form and emptiness shall immediately ascend to the Ten Stages.
The Ten Stages (Daśabhūmi) sport within the Flower Treasury Ocean (Kusumagarbha-sāgara). Golden trays filled with fragrant winds blow;
returning here, they scatter celestial flowers as an offering to the present Emperor, his imperial sons, and grandsons—may they live for a thousand autumns and ten thousand years!

I take refuge in the Sangha: the Śrāvakas and noble sages of Perfect Enlightenment who dwell on Mount Nanyue and Tiantai. At Mount Zhurong and Fangguang, they are far removed from the dust of the world;

entering meditative concentration, they contemplate emptiness without obscuration. They abide in profound stillness where tigers submit and dragons descend. How marvelous is this lofty Way! How marvelous is this Way!
They widely deploy the six supernatural powers with sovereign mastery, constantly responding to offerings throughout the ten directions, reaching those who call upon them in an instant.
At that time, this land and other realms were without obstruction; worthy of reliance, they guided all living beings so that they might all transcend the realm of the Buddhas.
Ancient Yangguan bows his head in refuge to the Buddha. When he was first born in the Lumbinī Garden, at nineteen he left the city and headed toward the snow mountains.
He practiced austerities on the mountain peaks; as the sprouts of reeds grew through his knees, he consumed only one grain of hemp and one grain of wheat morning and evening.

Having completed six years of ascetic practice, he realized Great Enlightenment Bodhi. Out of compassion, our Buddha emitted light from between his brows, illuminating the three evil realms so that beings might leave behind suffering and delusion.

Śakra, Brahmā, and the various devas turned toward him in devotion; the three realms looked up to him for refuge. Within the Dragon Flower Assembly, he personally bestowed predictions of enlightenment upon all sentient beings.
Discoursing upon the wondrous Dharma, inconceivable; when invited to descend, there is no refusal.

I prostrate and take refuge in the Dharma. The Bodhisattva asked about the causes and conditions a million times, and the Buddha expounded the true exposition in his vast golden mouth, personally proclaiming it.
Within the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury, may he constantly turn the Wheel of Dharma to deliver those with karmic affinity. Truly secret, it is inexhaustible.

Exhausted [is suffering]; the vessel for crossing to the other shore. Through faith and single-minded devotion, one departs from a thousand calamities; auspiciousness descends, and blessings and longevity are extended.

On this evening, incense and flowers are arrayed, and the music of the Dharma fills the heavens. Through compassion and skillful means, all classes of beings offer their sincere devotion as a field of merit.
I now prostrate; do not fail your vow. We invite you to descend to this feast.
Bowing my head, I take refuge in the Sangha. You dwell in the world at Fangguang and Tiantai, and atop the towering, dust-free summit of Mount Nanyue Zhurong.
Having personally received the Buddha’s entrustment, you respond to this land from other realms or the heavens; sometimes subduing tigers, you reside among the cliffs.

On the mountain slopes, sometimes shaking his staff or floating his bowl, he rests idly amidst piles of white clouds. Startled awake by the cries of divine birds, he wanders before the crags and enters meditative concentration;
he awakens to the blossoming of tree flowers. Beneath the coral trees, he further plants green pines under the moon.
Truly elegant and carefree, with no other concerns. At this invitation to descend, come to the Qiaogu Temple to take refuge in the Buddha.
Śākyamuni is the true compassionate father; manifesting his physical form, he departs from the stage of the "Remaining One" (Anāgāmin) and rides upon the white elephant.

The clouds dispersed; he then sought refuge in the imperial palace and took shelter with Māyā. Nine dragons spouted water to bathe him in a golden basin, and he attained the true golden form sixteen feet tall.
He was then invited away by Pāpīyas.
I take refuge in the Dharma. The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* is the marrow within the sūtras. Furthermore, I have expounded the *Avataṃsaka*, the *Ratnakūṭa*, and the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
I have taught the birth of Maitreya upon the Vajra Throne, the *Yogatantra*, the *Mayūravidyārajñī*, and all the various sūtra scrolls from within the Dragon Palace treasury;
scroll by scroll, they are the inconceivable wisdom of the Buddha.

I take refuge in the Sangha. The Sangha is that which has reached its fulfillment through conditions cultivated over successive kalpas. By imperial decree and the grace of the Emperor, my person remains unaltered;
I don the three robes of the Tathāgata to serve as a field of merit for those in the human realm. Holding a khakkhara staff in hand, I subdue dragons and tigers;
beneath trees in the forest, I settle into the seat of dhyāna. I pay no heed to the affairs of the red dust of the world.
Having completed the Three Refuges, he offered this benediction: "May the Emperor now reign ten thousand years, forever as he is today.
May his merit and longevity equal the mountains and rivers. May the Crown Prince and high ministers be exalted; may the people be at peace and the state prosperous, singing in joy.
May all neighboring states cease their strife, and from the eight directions, all come to pay homage to the Emperor."

Willows embrace the mist as the Buddha-treasure’s praise is inexhaustible. Success was achieved throughout immeasurable kalpas; towering is his sixteen-foot body of purple-gold. He awakened to the Way at the peak of the Snow Mountains.
From between his brows, the jade-white light shines brilliantly, illuminating and dispelling the darkness and delusion of the six realms. At the three assemblies of the Dragon Flower...
May we meet and expound the True Principle of the Dharma.
This Jewel of the Dharma is truly immeasurable, proclaimed from the golden mouth of the Tathāgata. From the dragon palaces and ocean treasuries, celestial fragrances are dispersed;

the Awakened One recites it with resonant clarity. Upon jade rollers bound with crimson silk, characters are inscribed in gold, appearing like rows of autumn geese in flight. It is all because of the Tripiṭaka.
Please come to Tang! For a thousand ages you shall spread [the Dharma].

The Jewel of the Sangha is inconceivable; your body is draped in the threefold cloud-robes. Floating upon a cup and shaking your staff, in the space of a single moment you respond to conditions and manifest according to the capacities of beings.
You are worthy to serve as a Master of Merit for the human realm. Firmly upholding the precepts without transgression—I now prostrate before you.
May you know this from afar. Holding my monk’s staff, I am like a crane soaring toward the heavens;
I bow my head to the Benevolent Sage. Your majestic features are peerlessly sublime. For ten months within your mother’s womb, you rested in peace. It was just at the beginning—
On the festival of Zhuming at the summer solstice, amidst the blooming of celestial flowers beneath the trees of the Aśoka grove, the Holy Mother grasped a branch as the Crown Prince was born.
His compassionate heart is vast and great; with devotion, he bows to the Unconditioned Joy. He extensively proclaims the secret words of the Three Vehicles. At the Dragon Flower [Assembly]...

He points out the path for humans and devas, nourishing and penetrating all; with cool clarity, he removes the heat of affliction. Like the moon’s serene radiance, his sixteen-foot golden form is pure and bright;
majestic and unshakable, the light from his brow-pores spreads forth intensely, illuminating the great trichiliocosm to save living beings and extinguish suffering. Now I praise him...

Praise and prostration to the Original Teacher, whose face is like the full moon; the Muni who expounds vast compassion. I make this vow of refuge, hoping to lead all sentient beings to transcendence and liberation. (Praise to Śākyamuni)

Qianqiushi: With a sincere heart, I pay homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. He is the Teacher of the Three Realms and the Father of the Four Modes of Birth. From between his brows, the jade-like light appears;
from his golden mouth, he speaks wondrous words. He nourishes all living beings as withered wood is moistened by sweet dew. His eighty secondary marks manifest through transformation.
Endowed with the thirty-two marks, manifesting compassion to rescue all from suffering—I now prostrate in homage; may you graciously grant your protection.
In a future age, having left this transient life in Jambudvīpa, [may we be born] in the Pure Land. (In praise of Śākyamuni:
With sincere devotion, I take refuge in and pay homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Manifesting the aspect of compassion, the Sage is pure and radiant; his eyebrows curve like emerald.

The willows: His face is round like the full moon; he manifests transformations throughout the lands of the ten directions according to the needs of sentient beings. Beholding him in worship disperses calamities; hearing his name extinguishes transgressions.
He appears amidst assemblies of incense and flowers arranged like stars; the music of Dharma descends in continuous waves from heaven. The sounds of strings and flutes are harmonious and pleasing.
I pray that you may dispel my sincerity and grant your compassionate acceptance, beholding my earnest devotion. (Praise of Avalokiteśvara)

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the Buddha of Fixed Light (Dīpaṃkara) at Nan’an. Appearing in the guise of a layman before the Golden Gate, he was personally venerated by Emperor Renzong, whereby calamities throughout the realm were extinguished.
The Emperor bestowed upon him a purple robe and a posthumous title in an imperial calligraphy that remains inscribed on a stone monument to this day.
Master Poli said: "Since the Dharma-hall was established five hundred kalpas ago, clouds of incense and flowers have gathered in dense profusion.
Devotees have cultivated caves and grottoes, constantly making offerings to the Great Bodhisattva, the Perfectly Responsive Teacher, who praises the Light of Samādhi."

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the Tathāgata Blazing Radiance (*Jvalanaprabha*). Manifested within the realm of the Sovereign Devas (*Īśvara*), he possesses great majesty, virtue, and supernormal transformations.
Upon a crimson lotus pedestal, his countenance is of purple-gold. Flashing fire-wheels and tongues of flame traverse the Milky Way; he wanders through all twelve palaces of the zodiac.
As he travels everywhere, malevolent planets and demonic stars gradually dissipate. For the sake of our families and nations, he eliminates all calamities and hardships.
When the planets Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn approach, one should simply make vows before the golden countenance [of the Buddha], which will transform them into goodness.
One must know that compassion provides the skillful means for salvation (praising the Buddha Blazing Light).
The Five Blessings descend from the midst of heaven;
we reverently take refuge and pay homage with a sincere heart. Śākyamuni first manifested his transformation body; Māyā was moved by a most extraordinary dream.
When the moon was full, he was born in the Lumbinī Garden; as he took his first steps, lotuses followed the movement of his feet. Brahmā, Śakra, and all the devas beheld this auspicious omen.

Śuddhodana marveled at this rare wonder. Gradually he grew up, becoming fully accomplished in both civil and military arts; he frequented the four gates to study the three ends and six arts. There, he beheld the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death;

moved by these pressing sorrows, he sighed and turned back. Abiding in stillness amidst the void, he was informed [of the time]; at midnight, he leaped over the city walls and gradually ascended the snowy peaks.
He departed for the mountain peaks to practice his cultivation.
He sent a secret letter back to inform his father-king that there was no need for sorrow, as he would achieve the Way in the future and return to appear before the Emperor.
After six years of diligent effort, his practice was fulfilled; at that time, he received the milk-gruel from the cowherd girl and bathed in the mud-born lotus of the Vajra-treasure.

As he sat there realizing Bodhi, the celestial Māra and his retinue became envious of the Teacher. Evil thoughts arose within them, and they summoned their demonic soldiers and ghostly generals, each displaying their formidable prowess.

As they drew near with clashing swords, blades, and halberds, the World-Honored One was seated upon a red lotus. Witnessing this supernatural power, the Māra immediately turned his mind toward repentance.
They returned to take refuge.

Once the demons and adversaries had retreated, he gathered at the Deer Park; there, he proclaimed the Four Noble Truths through the Three Turnings of the Wheel. Subsequently, he spread the sublime teachings to widely deliver the deluded masses.
I now offer praise and prayers that the sovereign’s reign may endure forever and the imperial foundation remain firm. May all sentient beings together ascend to the realization of the Right Way.
The Principle of Non-arising (In Praise of Śākyamuni).
Linjiang Xian:
For three great kalpas, he cultivated the practice of Avalokiteśvara; now, having attained the fruit of time, he has realized Bodhi. Upon Mount Potalaka, his seated form is majestic and towering.

Holding the water of ambrosia in hand, with a robe of six *zhu* hanging from the body, he possesses an inexhaustible intent to rescue and deliver sentient beings. His light from the *ūrṇā* hair shines universally upon the masses of the deluded;
his dignified majesty arises from the awakening of compassion. He is constantly worshipped throughout the ten directions, and all within the four seas take refuge in him.

(Praise to Avalokiteśvara) The Great Benevolent One, Kṣitigarbha, possesses vast and far-reaching vows; his compassion is tireless as he responds to the capacities of beings. In hand he carries a golden staff, shaking through the Avīci Hell;

the entire heavens are brilliantly illuminated, and throughout the earth all voices chant his name. He delivers sentient beings until the very end, his single hair-tip radiating light that shines everywhere.
In the remote regions of Qí, the three evil paths and eight difficulties have ceased their delusions; sentient beings transcend to the other shore, and there is nowhere they do not take refuge.
(Praise to Kṣitigarbha) — Southern Sacred Court.

Amitābha Buddha is truly worthy of admiration; his marks and signs are dignified and radiant. A light from the hair-treasure illuminates the great trichiliocosm, within which appear śrāvakas and arhats.
Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra both offer praise. Possessing the four great vows, he guides all sentient beings to realize non-arising.
Having perfected the fruit of Bodhi, he is fully accomplished.
The Pure Land of the West appears, soaring through the void. Latticed towers of pearls and jade palaces stand; within the lapis lazuli ponds, auspicious lotuses bloom.
Drawing forth layers of auspicious clouds, the Buddha’s vast compassion extends skillful means to guide all beings toward the ten wholesome deeds.
Upon the nine grades of lotus pedestals, they realize the eternal and true; he delivers sentient beings without weariness.

Tonight, the filial practitioner prepares fragrant offerings with utmost sincerity and solemnity, following the instructions of the hermitage. The monks burn incense, chant, and recite the sublime scriptures to clear grievances and absolve transgressions.
May the three evil paths and eight difficulties be entirely extinguished, and may they awaken to True Suchness.
By virtue of these meritorious offerings, may the souls of the deceased be delivered to the Inner Court of Sukhāvatī. (In praise of Amitābha)
The Five Thunder Disciples:
*Namo Buddhāya*. Great Compassionate Father of the Three Realms, you provide a vessel for the sea of suffering.

For those drifting through the six realms of existence, you manifest a thousand billion transformation bodies to rescue us sentient beings from their pain. O Source of Compassion, receive these deceased spirits and lead them to rebirth in the Pure Land.
Homage to the Dharma. Within the yellow scrolls of the Dragon Palace lies the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra; therein four lines remain as the true exposition of the twelve divisions of scripture.
Every word is the Buddha’s speech, written in the script of the Five Heavens, to guide deceased spirits toward rebirth in the Pure Land.

Homage to the Saṃgha. His six supernormal powers are transmitted through the ages; he carries a golden staff in his hand. Having subdued dragons and tamed tigers, his body is draped in robes of purple sandalwood.
Taking up his alms bowl, he wanders according to conditions as a master of transformation, guiding deceased spirits toward rebirth in the Pure Land.
(Recommending the Deceased to the Triple Gem) Skillfully played upon the zither is Śākyamuni Buddha.
Initially, due to the conditions of his causal ground, he took form within Māyā. Beneath the branches of the Aśoka tree, nine dragons spat forth fragrant incense.

Water. With a golden basin, he bathed and washed, as the Prince descended from the imperial palace. When the Father King learned of this, he provided lotus petals for his feet and a halo of light enveloped his body;
the consorts joyfully cradled the Prince and returned him to the inner palace. As time passed swiftly and imperceptibly, nineteen years slipped away.
Then, having gone out through the four gates to wander and briefly observe the floating world, he encountered [an old man] at the western gate.
"Death! A monk from the North Gate, carrying his alms bowl and staff, was teaching and transforming beings with every step, saying, 'Give according to your conditions;
cease your folly, cease your folly! Do not be attached to luxury or wealth; turn back your heads and reflect early! Upon hearing these words, the Prince felt joy in his heart."
When the time for departure arrived, he passed beyond the city walls. He practiced austerities in the Snowy Mountains; for his morning meal, he sustained himself on hemp and wheat to fill his hunger.

The Heavenly King offered him venison, a magpie nested upon his head as he performed the consecration, and reed sprouts pierced through his knees. Through such arduous practice—arduous practice—for six years, he realized the *pāramitās*.
His towering marks and golden body are beyond compare. Within the Dragon Flower Assembly at the Twin Trees where he preached the Dharma, he is the Many-Jeweled Tathāgata.
Samantabhadra, Maitreya, Pratyekabuddhas, and Arhats all take refuge together. Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra—our Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma is boundless and limitless.

The meaning of the sutras, the meaning of the sutras: the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* in seven fascicles is the very marrow of the scriptures. Emperor Wu of Liang performed repentance rites to eliminate calamities and transgressions.
May the Human King, the Peacock-Sovereign, and Maitreya hold him in their mindfulness to ensure his peace and security.
Seeking merit and blessings, the king shall repay the grace of Heaven by inviting the Saṃgha to return the offerings. (Praise to Śākyamuni) Furthermore:
Praising the Bodhisattva’s initial causal origination in the stage of the ground, his physical form was manifested within the kingdom of King Wondrous Adornment. Devas and nāgas gave rise to joy;

the princess descended into the world entirely through the power of her vows. A transformation body of great compassion appeared in person, with eyes as radiant as blue lotuses and a body as glowing as red peaches.
Her beauty was peerless; she did not seek a prince consort as a fine husband, but resolved in every thought to seek [the Bodhisattva] for deliverance.

Departing from worldly existence, he went directly to Mount Gandhamādana, having no attachment to honor or nobility. Sitting upright, he practiced by himself; casting aside the imperial palace, he turned his light inward and realized the *pāramitās*.
With his Dharma-body fully perfected, he rescues those in suffering upon hearing their cries. His self-sacrifice is most extraordinary—extraordinary indeed!
With a thousand hands and a thousand eyes, his divine powers were cultivated through countless *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas. This was due to his past...
When Avalokiteśvara appeared in the world, he instructed me at that time to cultivate the stage of samādhi. Through hearing and reflection, I attained awakening to the True Dharma from the ear.
The Tathāgata bestowed a prophecy upon me: "By means of the Vajra-samādhi, you shall universally deliver all beings. With great vows, great vows, you adorn your sacred form with the thirty-two marks.
Clad in white robes and draped with pearls and emeralds, you are exquisitely beautiful atop Mount Potalaka in the Lapis Lazuli Garden.
Within [the hall], the vase of ambrosia manifests; willow branches are sprinkled with water. The *Lengyan* assembly proceeds through its standard sequence. Fearlessness is universally bestowed.

Those who preach the Dharma attain deliverance, and humans and devas take refuge. This inconceivable Great Compassionate Divine Mantra extinguishes all transgressions. Extinguishes all transgressions! Great Compassion! Divine Mantra! Inconceivable!
The wondrous meaning of the *Dhāraṇī* of the Universal Gate Chapter brings forth and guides sentient beings so that they may together realize Bodhi; may all their vows be perfectly fulfilled.
Now I prostrate with single-minded concentration and address Avalokiteśvara: may all increase in merit and wisdom. (Praise to Avalokiteśvara) Hail to the Sacred Court!
The Tathāgata rescues sentient beings from suffering; he is the compassionate father of the four modes of birth. All living beings are enabled to leave behind their collective delusions.
He manifests transformation bodies in a thousand places. Pāpīyān and the non-Buddhists give rise to anger and malice;
driven by jealousy, they compel him to enter nirvana, leading him toward the extinction at the twin śāla trees.
At that time, Pāṭalī ascended the path of the clouds and went to the celestial palace to inform his mother. His mother said, "I was only just beginning to be startled from my dream;
I grieve that sentient beings have no protector. Then Māyā, hearing these words, shed tears that fell like rain.
Leading her retinue and riding upon auspicious clouds, she arrived at the Twin Trees to behold him in person.
Circumambulating the coffin three times, he wailed in bitter grief, saying: "Siddhārtha, my son! You have now abandoned me to enter Nirvāṇa.
I pray that you, Master, leave behind four verses; let the Tathāgata speak words of truth from within his coffin, so that I may be freed from sorrow and my suffering may cease.
All worldly things are utterly impermanent; only the Dharma-body is eternally firm. (In Praise of the Buddha’s Nirvāṇa)
*Man Ting Fang*:
I bow my head in refuge to the Great Sage named Guanyin upon Mount Potalaka. You constantly assist those in the eight difficulties and respond to the myriad conditions of sentient beings.

Your white tuft of hair radiates brilliance; with ten billion willow branches, you sprinkle the bitter sea as rain. May all weary beings throughout the realms as numerous as motes of dust and grains of sand pay you their respects.
I look up: in a single thought, one is spared from drifting and sinking. Upon the towering lotus throne, his body is adorned with flowered canopies and necklaces, as radiant as silver.

Around his neck he wears a net of pearl threads, his form graced by a hundred jewels. Everywhere he seeks out voices to save those in suffering; at every turn he reveals himself to receive all beings.
Manifesting his form as a true compassionate father, amidst the swirling incense smoke of the burner, I gaze afar, hoping you will witness my sincere heart. (In praise of Avalokiteśvara)
Furthermore, we, with sincere and single-minded devotion, take refuge in and pay homage to the Compassionate and Benevolent Kṣitigarbha. His great compassion pervades heaven and earth;

we everywhere seek refuge in you. We pray that you will deliver us from the suffering of the three miserable realms and the eight difficulties, and grant us your grace. Tonight, all living beings gaze upon you...

I look up to you with all my heart, striving with utmost diligence. The Great Compassionate Honored One’s vow is profound and weighty; I pray that you will release light from the hair-tuft between your brows to illuminate the dark realms of suffering.
May the lords of hell be transformed to pardon the prisoners’ sins and cease their torment, so that sentient beings may be liberated from their grievances and enmities.
From this day forward, let them no longer wail in sorrow. Relying upon the Buddha’s power, may all conscious beings together attain complete transcendence. (In praise of Kṣitigarbha)

Furthermore, the Triple Gem is worthy of reliance, and all living beings turn toward it for refuge. Within the site of enlightenment, an unobstructed feast is spread; the resonance of a single toll of the bell pervades as many worlds as grains of sand in the Ganges.
The master of offerings prostrates with sincere devotion, arranging pure offerings and displaying banners and flowers. Burning incense, he invites the deities of the celestial and terrestrial realms.
The water-trinity descended in cloud-chariots; all the dragon deities of the human palaces and temples descended as well.

Along the shores and to the ends of the earth, they listened to the Tathāgata’s secret liberation maṇḍala, universally rescuing sunken souls and lingering spirits so that they might leave hell and proceed to the abode of the immortals.
Tonight’s ritual has reached its full fruition. I prostrate to the Buddha!
(Praise to the Three Realms) A song in the Shuǐdiào mode extolling the Teacher of the Three Realms, Śākyamuni Buddha. He then called for Ānanda, Pūrṇa, and Śāriputra.
"O Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Aniruddha, Maitreya Bodhisattva, Jālinīprabha, and Subhūti, I command you all:
you must know that you should go quickly to the city of Vaiśālī. Vimalakīrti is currently afflicted by illness;
inquire after his well-being and report back to me exactly how he fares. At that time, the devas and bodhisattvas wished to depart, yet they hesitated.
They all bowed their heads in grief and addressed the Buddha, saying: "The Venerable Mañjuśrī has now gone to the layman Vimalakīrti.
His wisdom is vast and boundless beyond compare, and he preaches the Dharma like a flowing stream. It would be difficult for us to approach this superior man to engage him in discourse."

The Buddha said, "I know your intention. You once encountered him in the past. He then summoned Mañjuśrī and the assembly of celestial and divine beings, commanding them to go quickly to Vimalakīrti’s dwelling.
At that time, the various Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas all wished to accompany them.
Mañjuśrī rode upon a lion, manifesting his full majesty. A fragrant breeze dispersed, and extraordinary celestial flowers fell in profusion;
from the vast sky, the rain of Dharma fell in fine drizzle. He proceeded directly to the chamber of Vimalakīrti, where he respectfully bowed his head in prostration and paid homage.
"I have come by the compassionate command of the Buddha to inquire about the causes and conditions of your illness, O Householder—from whence did it arise?"
The layman suffered from an ailment and leaned alone against a support. He thanked you for coming to express your concern. Now, I too am afflicted by the illness of sentient beings;
out of compassion for all who are deluded, I feel as a parent would when their own child is ill.
The inconceivable responses of the various bodhisattvas flowed like a stream. The layman once again recited five verses, expounding upon the gates of the Dharma of suffering and emptiness;
in every gate he spoke without deviation, viewing the body as dew, lightning, and a shadow, thereby transforming the masses of deluded beings.
The fourfold assembly, as well as the asuras and gandharva kings, were all filled with joy. They praised the Tathāgata’s skillful means and his excellent understanding and realization.
"Through my own delusion, I have explained the principle of *tathatā* (suchness). I now bow my head in prostration and worship, taking refuge in you completely.
(Praise to Vimalakīrti)

Praise for the Subduing of Māra: Homage to the Great Sage, the Muni! Descending from Tuṣita, he responds to the three thousandfold world system. Mounting a dragon and riding an elephant, he dreams of penetrating the clear heavens.
Departing for the Garden of Lumbinī, beneath the Aśoka tree, he descends with his right side downward. Colorful clouds connect; nine dragons spout warm springs as he bathes—how marvelous!
How extraordinary and fresh—how enviable! At every step, red lotuses serve as his footstool. He performs music to inform the King, delighting the Dragon’s countenance.

For a long time, he has been inclined toward wandering through the four gates; there, he personally beholds old age, sickness, and death, and realizes that this floating life is neither long-lasting nor firm.

Furthermore, he encounters a field of merit and thus desires to transcend mundane conditions. He ascends to the presence of his royal father; suddenly, upon hearing these words, the music of strings and pipes increases once more.

The clamor of sounds; within the void of the Pure Abodes, the words of the response are bewildering. Cease your greedy attachment to the realms of the five desires; practice cultivation early and learn the dhyāna of peace.
At midnight, he mounted his crimson steed and leaped over the city walls; on the Snowy Peaks, his resolve remained firm for six years.

With a bird’s nest upon his head and sprouts of reeds growing from his knees, he remained unmoving in tranquil composure with palms joined. With the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, the Golden Immortal transformed thousands and hundreds.
The *Bodhicitta* unfolds the true dharma; the vow is to deliver all sentient beings, infinite and boundless.

At that time, the demonic armies were greatly incensed; leading their monstrous troops, they fought the Golden Immortal (the Buddha). They brandished spears and brandished swords, swarming about; smoke flew and they went mad with frenzy.
They set a thousand-jin crossbow, commanded the divine generals, and issued a proclamation with steel hooks, swords, halberds, and broad blades.
Swords were crowded together as they vied for the front; furthermore, wind-cannons were discharged, striking in chaos. The roar of "Kill! shook the three thousand worlds;

sand was blown and stones were driven along, with cries and clamor reaching to the heavens. The demonic armies employed a thousand methods, fiercely displaying their ferocity to intimidate the compassionate countenance.

Thunder and lightning flashed across the void, and the heavens and earth were struck with alarm. Yet, amidst this, the One of Central Heaven remained serene through compassion, kindness, joy, and equanimity, adorned with myriads of virtues.

Boundless! Whenever he raised his spear or sword, they were transformed into red lotuses. When the demonic armies beheld such divine power, they turned their hearts back and repented of their past transgressions.
They vowed with faith to become disciples of the Tathāgata and forever seek refuge before the Buddha at Jetavana. At once, they bowed their heads in prostration and took refuge in him;

they received and upheld the precepts with single-minded devotion. Those in the world who were foolish and sought to form auspicious karmic connections were universally exhorted to return with sincere resolve.
Relying on the authentic exposition of the World-Honored Buddha, I pray for the Sage and Enlightened Sovereign that his sagacious life-span may endure for ten million years.

Looking toward the Southland, I take refuge in the Buddha, who is most honored throughout the three realms; having cultivated practice over successive kalpas, he attained Perfect Enlightenment and constantly raises the rain of Dharma to sprinkle all beings.
Heaven and Earth—nowhere is His grace not felt. For ten million years, His wondrous form delivers all of humanity. May He, in His compassion, grant His protection;
may the people be at peace and the nation prosperous, spreading the clouds of Yao, and may the Buddha-sun endure forever.

I take refuge in the Dharma. The royal axis is inscribed with refined golden script; when the palm leaves unfold, its light shines brilliantly. Where the lapis lazuli caskets are recited, auspicious clouds arise.
Spoken from the golden mouth of Śākyamuni, the volumes are truly immeasurable. They remain enshrined in the Dragon Palace as a treasure for the world;
as a field of merit, they deliver all those with whom they have a karmic connection, transforming the lost at the ferry-crossing for long eons.

I take refuge in the Sangha. Your true countenance is majestic and imposing; your body is draped in purple robes, yet your mind is like a mirror. Responding to conditions as they arise, you answer the needs of all sentient beings, like the moon illuminating a clear pool.
You constantly provide offerings to those in the sea of suffering, rescuing those who have sunk and perished. With sincere resolve, we prostrate ourselves before you.
We pray that we may meet Maitreya as he descends from the celestial palace, hear the Dharma, and awaken to the state of non-arising.
Incense and flowers escort the Buddhas as they sit upon precious lotuses; celestial music comes from the sky to welcome them.
The resonance of gongs, cymbals, bells, and drums fills the heavens. Processions surround the Golden Immortals (Buddhas), along with hosts of Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas.
These various hymns in Sanskrit and Chinese are able to forge auspicious karmic ties for the world, ensuring that the Buddha-Dharma flows on forever. (Song □)
The assembly at the site of enlightenment joins their palms to escort the Golden Immortal. May all sentient beings receive benefit and joy.
May we form auspicious karmic bonds this evening at this assembly. May those in the world awaken to the true teaching. To the various holy ones of the site of enlightenment:
Prajñāpāramitā! Mahāprajñāpāramitā! Gambhīraprajñāpāramitā! May the merit and blessings be forever inexhaustible. (Escort of the Buddha)

Throughout the night, the Dharma assembly proceeded with the chanting of the *Śaṅkhaśvāsa* (Sound-Slow) Sutra. We were graced by the descent of the holy assembly. Our offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments—made with our ordinary, mundane minds—were exceedingly meager.

Behold, as the night draws to a close and the moon fades into darkness, the golden bird of the sun gradually emerges from the east, faintly visible. I offer praise and prostrations, looking toward our Buddha.

May your compassion graciously behold this sincere devotion. As the secret mantras of the Tripitaka are empowered and the music gradually fades into the profound depths, the patron remains devoutly earnest, gazing upward in hope that blessings and grace may be bestowed.
May the donors increase in merit and longevity, and may the three evil realms forever find rest.
The deluded mind awakens to the principle of wisdom. Through the vows of the three assemblies at the Dragon Flower, may we behold the Golden Body.
(Farewell to the Buddha) Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Gaofeng Longquan Monastery, Compiled by Jixian, Volume Four.
Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Gaofeng Longquan Monastery, Compiled by Jixian, Volume Five.
I humbly pray that my family members may live in this sagely age;
though I am but a member of the human race, I am indebted for the grace of the stars’ illuminating gaze and for the life-giving kindness of my parents. I offer my thanks.

Regarding these virtues, I have fortunately encountered this auspicious day, coinciding with the very moment of Your birth. Unable to repay my private feelings of veneration, I employ this as a means to express my sincere devotion.
I humbly pray that the Imperial Vault of Heaven may favor the virtuous and the Supreme Deity may augment Your humility.

May the Mount of Longevity rise ever higher, and the Ocean of Blessings flow ever more far-reaching. May the Sages of the Cinnabar Terrace record Your eternal years, and the True Immortals of the Purple Palace...
May you forever receive boundless blessings.
In life, contemplate with sevenfold mindfulness that the body is an illusion and the world is not solid. If one were to cultivate causes for the sake of what lies beyond this life, why not do so now?
Exert yourself with diligence hereafter to honor the fruit of Buddhahood and prepare the bridge and raft in advance. I humbly pray that your meritorious achievements may shine forth brightly;
let this be a longevity register for the present life. How great is this circular proclamation! May it serve forever as a protective talisman for future generations.
May Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva act as witness, and may Kṣitigarbha, the Benevolent One, graciously grant his seal of approval.
Having received the seeds of birth and obtained their fruit, one now manifests as a present body. To acknowledge kindness and repay it, the teaching on receiving birth is thus expounded.
Since it was previously said that [the debt] was borrowed, it must now be repaid. We look up in prayer to your sagely and divine power, and look down upon us...

Examining one’s true heart and sincere intent, once the bridge of salvation has been established, karmic obstructions will subtly vanish. May the ocean of merit and the mountain of longevity be further deepened and solidified in years to come;
may the spring breeze and harmonious qi always remain as serene and dignified as they are this day.
The Blood-Basin Mother nurtured me; having fully bestowed the grace of her upbringing, a child’s love for their parent must repay the virtue of her arduous toil.

Thus, I venerate the highest goodness to look up and answer the debt of my birth-giver. I humbly pray that my mother may enjoy long-lasting blessings throughout a thousand lifetimes and that all ten evil deeds be extinguished.

May the basin of blood be transformed into a lotus basin; may the ocean of karma be turned into the ocean of Dharma. In this life and this world, may calamitous stars be shifted to become auspicious stars;
on other days and at other times, may one return from the path of humanity to the path of the Buddha. May the Benevolent One, Kṣitigarbha, pray grant witness;
may the Master, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, look upon us with compassion.

Born among the lower realms, my destiny belongs to the supreme firmament above. Fearing that ill fortune may descend upon me and apprehensive that malefic stars may not be rectified, I exhaust my humble sincerity to look upward and appeal to Your Celestial Wisdom.
I pray that you may dispel these groundless calamities and grant me the great bestowal of abundant blessings.
Ill fortune is transformed into auspicious fortune; malefic stars are turned into benefic stars. The Cinnabar Terrace records years of agelessness;

the Purple Palace inscribes characters for increased sustenance. Rāhu and the Moon-asterism shall forever be free from the peril of invasion; the Courser (Yimǎ) and the Saddle-clasp (Pān'ān) are constantly graced by their illuminating virtue.
The Five Elements converge like spokes; the Four Pillars are securely established. This is entirely due to the Great Descent of the High Transcendents.
Miyu: I return my vows to the divine powers above, earnestly seeking their grace of protection. Now that the years have passed, I am indeed sustained by the power of their guidance.
Having already received your silent grace, how could I dare betray my original resolve? I now exhaust the sincerity of this day to specifically fulfill the vow of former times.
I pray that the names of "pending cases" may be erased from the ledgers of the Six Ministries, and that the characters for "repayment" may be inscribed upon the registers of the Three Realms.
May you grant the great blessing of beginning and end, so that the merit already accomplished may reach full completion.

May the spirit of Mount Song descend to grant a son who shall become a worthy minister; may prayers offered at Mount Niqiu result in the birth of a sage. Though the hearing of Heaven is lofty, the sentiments of human beings may reach it.
Consider me, a lowly member of the common class like weeds and brush, a mere life among plants and trees, who has long been in harmony with the sound of the zither and the lute.

Before any omens of dreams of bears or tigers have appeared, I hereby exhaust my humble sincerity to trouble Your Majesty’s sagacious hearing, hoping to give birth to a son endowed with wisdom and intelligence,
so that this auspicious vow may be fulfilled at an early date.
I, the man surnamed Xie, address Your Sacred Majesty. May my wishes accord with the heart of the falcon descending upon the swallow; indeed, my humble desires have been fulfilled.

In silent resonance with the omen of the bear in the dream, may there be a succession of worthy sons and a lineage of noble lords. Thus, I know that the way of our family will surely flourish and the ancestral spirit shall not decline.
Truly relying upon your support and assistance, I venture to offer my sincere thanks.

Regarding the protection of the fetus, I, [Name], reflect that while I carry this child within my womb, sustained by the virtue of Heaven and Earth, there may be some uncertainty at the time of childbirth.

In these times of hardship, one must rely upon the power of the Sage to bestow great hidden merit (*guṇa*). May you protect her for ten months with ease and guard her during this period so that no calamity befalls her.
