May the Holy Mother be overseen by the Sage to have her transgressions diminished and partially absolved; may the divine infant be protected and granted the blessings of great auspiciousness.
May she dream of the bear and the cubs, and may the bow and arrows be displayed at her door—may the omen of giving birth early to a male child be fulfilled, so that he shall succeed to the lineage.
As descendants of the patriarchs' tradition,
we pray for wealth and honor bestowed from Heaven, which cannot be achieved by human effort alone; yet where blessings and auspiciousness reside, they can be sought through the fruits of goodness.
Recently, when my compassionate mother conceived this excellence and while she was cherishing her young child, there was no door upon which to rely and no Buddha to whom we could turn for refuge.
Entrusting ourselves to the power of the Sage for protection and support, and relying upon his spiritual essence for guardianship, both mother and child were joyfully spared from misfortune;
wife and children attained safety and well-being. The birth was indeed a celebration of auspiciousness, and the carrying and sending forth truly depended upon the Śākya clan.
There are vows that must be fulfilled. Knowing one's debt of gratitude, how could one ever forget it?

I earnestly pray for [Name], who has endured many misfortunes over several years and has suffered from illness for a long time. I fear that malevolent stars may cast their influence upon his destiny, thereby bringing about calamity.
Calamities entwine us from without; there is no door through which to extend the methods of averting and deliverance. May the Sage act as our Lord to whom we may turn for refuge.
We humbly pray that the calamitous stars shall withdraw their influence, eliminating present misfortunes, and that the auspicious luminaries shall descend, bestowing great blessings upon the future.

The Celestial Physician’s Messengers shall protect the vital energy so that it endures forever; the King of the Treasury of Peace and Bliss shall sweep away the winds of evil so that they cease eternally.
The five spirits shall be tranquil and the hundred vessels harmonious. The field of the body shall be as firm as pine and cypress trees; one’s allotted lifespan shall be as solid as a mountain ridge.
I pray that,
as the current year’s cyclical signs are unfavorable and my destiny is beset by many calamities, resulting in illnesses that cling to me and medicines that fail to heal,

I may rely upon your compassion to perform rites of averting and deliverance. I humbly entreat you to harmonize through your refined intention and that the assembly of True Beings grant their sincere protection.
Unforeseen faults shall be dissolved; past transgressions shall be pardoned and erased. Auspicious stars shine upon one so that destiny becomes radiant;
malevolent planets vanish so that the physical constitution is secure and peaceful. The five elements flow harmoniously, free from the peril of mutual conflict or clash.
The six pulses are balanced and regulated, removing the suffering of agitation, constriction, sinking, or floating. Dragon deities provide protection; the will of Heaven offers support.

In praying for the averting of calamities, I reflect that though I have been born in a prosperous age, my nature is fundamentally dull and ignorant. I am indebted to the grace of Heaven and Earth for their encompassing support, and I bear the virtue of the Sun and Moon for their illuminating presence.
I am deeply concerned that disasters may arise unexpectedly; since man prizes the value of preemptive protection, we shall collectively gather our family resources to reverently perform this rite.
Buddhist Service. We humbly pray that through these virtuous causes, calamities may be averted; that malevolent stars may be transformed into auspicious stars;

that the power of the Sages may provide protection; and that demonic vapors may be changed into auspicious mists. May every place become a land of peace and happiness, and every household consist of people living in tranquility.

May yin and yang be in harmony, and may wind and rain fall in their proper seasons. May disasters not arise and chaos not be stirred. May the four classes of society delight in their vocations, and [may] the eight members of each family...

There was no hunger; granaries were full and treasuries were abundant. Thieves and bandits declined, while litigation and disputes ceased. Each fulfilled their heart’s wish, and all bathed in the sage’s grace.
Thus the fire was averted.
Although the heavens are distant, they are fundamentally connected to one’s own mind; though blessings are boundless, they are all brought about by human effort.

We deeply fear that the wandering planet Mars may send down calamity upon the people of this ward. While the public sentiment has no means to offer thanks for past transgressions, we take refuge in our Buddha to offer this prayer.

I look upward in prayer to the Celestial Backbone and look downward with compassion upon the sentiments of the common folk. May calamities and transgressions be transformed into auspiciousness; may portents of misfortune be changed into prosperity.

May the celestial bodies follow their proper courses, and may the various regions be free from anxiety. May the divine spirits dissolve their traces within their native lands, and may the Fire Deity turn his radiance back toward the immortal palaces.

May the four classes of people remain tranquil and the ten thousand households enjoy peace and security. May wind and rain be harmonious, and the fields and gardens yield abundant harvests. This all depends entirely upon [your grace].
The arrival of Your Great Virtue has brought immense solace to the hearts of the masses.

Yet, the accumulated rains have exceeded the norm, and the lingering yin has become a calamity; failing to fulfill its natural function of flowing downward, it has resulted in this widespread inundation, threatening the crops in the great fields.

The people of neighboring houses, all farmers, sighed in lamentation. They urgently turned to the Buddhist scriptures to dispel the celestial calamity, looking upward to pray for the compassion of the World-Protectors and looking downward to rescue those suffering from pestilence.
He dispersed the white tuft of hair from his crown, chasing away all stubborn gloom;
he swallowed the vast ocean within the tip of a single hair, transforming it while seated into fertile fields. The Benevolent One universally observes; we rely upon his great protection.

To protect the seedlings from the *lang* and *you* weeds, one indeed relies on the suitability of the land; yet for the ears to be square and the stalks to be thick, one further depends on the excellence of the seasons.

Reflecting that while agricultural labor has already commenced in the southern fields, the full measure of the year’s achievement cannot be reckoned until the autumn harvest, I hereby pour forth my sincere devotion.

I look up and cast myself upon Imperial Enlightenment. I humbly pray that the golden years of plenty may respond in harmony and the jade lamps of the seasons may be evenly regulated. May winter not suffer from excessive heat, and summer not suffer from hidden cold;
may the wind not whistle through the branches, and the rain not break the clods of earth. May locusts suddenly cease and weeds of the field not grow.

May the High Heaven manifest the auspicious sign of the overturned Dipper, and the lower realm be moved by the omen of the dream-fish. May the common people rejoice in the blessing of overflowing granaries, and throughout the four [directions]...
Now that I am able to indulge in the leisure of nourishing my belly, it is entirely due to the sagely repose of Your Majesty. My silent aspirations have been fulfilled;

though I preserve the life of a silkworm and maintain the nature of a woman, I am unworthily situated within the inner chambers. To fully fulfill the way of a wife without deficiency, there is nothing more urgent than sericulture.

Although we rely on human effort, it is truly dependent upon the conditions of the Buddha. We prostrate ourselves with the humble wish that the King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra) may transform the non-existent into the existent, and that the Great Being Aśvaghoṣa may transform the meager into the abundant. May the cocoons be as bright as frost and the silk as vast as mountain ranges;
may there not be even a hair’s breadth of waste, but rather that tenfold the full harvest be gathered in.

In the construction of dwellings (wherein one speaks of joyful labor and peaceful dwelling) and the excavation of burial mounds (wherein one speaks of digging the earth to establish a tomb), one must necessarily rely on the power of management. When commencing work and disturbing the soil, how could there not be the apprehension of transgressing [the spirits]?

We specially rely upon your compassion to briefly extend us consolation. We prostrate ourselves, praying that the Five Dragons may take their stations and the Eight Generals may return to their abodes.
The four classes of malevolent spirits retreat and hide; by relying on the mediating power of sages and saints, a hundred evils are forever dispelled.
By drawing upon the transformative efficacy of Heaven and Earth, a thousand calamities are extinguished within the household and a hundred blessings are welcomed at the door.
In resolving karmic knots, how could there not be the enmity of countless past lives? In this present life and birth, there must surely be the defilements of sins committed in the past.
Fortunately, the Buddhas have widely opened the path of great compassion and permitted sentient beings to express their hearts of repentance. Thus, relying upon...
The great cessation of the knots is attained; may it cleanse boundless dark karma. With each knot untied, the ten evils and the five heinous crimes are entirely eliminated.
With each praise and each extolling, beings of the six realms and three miserable paths are all liberated.
Evil fruits are transformed into wholesome fruits, and the roots of sin are turned into roots of merit. Thus, one accumulates excellent causes and fulfills virtuous vows.

The rain-praying fields have their crops about to flourish, yet the drenching rains do not nourish them. Should there be any lapse before the High Heaven, then there will be no hope for their final emergence.

Looking up to Your Sacred Creation, I pray that You will behold my humble sincerity. I wish to rely upon this single offering of incense and beseech You to grant the grace of continuous night-long showers at an early date.
May the people’s hopes find some measure of recovery, so that they may equally partake in the blessings of Heaven.

After the rains have ceased for a long time and the weather has been clear, I fear the crops will wither and dry up; yet through the power of Your Holiness, such can be sought. Now the year’s rains fall in torrential deluges.
As the great earth revives through the labors of spring, all under heaven looks up with gratitude for the harvest of autumn. I hereby extend my humble sincerity to slightly express my thanks;
I further pray for the gift of continued prosperity and that this year may immediately become one of abundant grain.

Prolonged gloom has brought calamity to the prayers for clear skies, and the transgression of incessant rain persists. As the new grain has not yet ripened, we fear losing the hope for an autumn harvest.

Thus, with sincere devotion, we look upward to叩 (invoke) Your Sacred Intelligence. We humbly pray that You will emit the light of the white tuft of hair for the duration of a single thought-moment, shattering this stubborn [darkness].
Shading the four quarters and illuminating the nine heavens with brilliant splendor, we forever rely upon your protection and preservation; our resolve for *pariṇāmanā* grows ever firmer.
Recently, as torrential rains caused widespread disaster and dense clouds accumulated, I humbly approached you to appeal to your compassionate benevolence. Indeed, I have received [your response].

The emptiness of the Six Perfections has already allayed the afflictions of the three farming seasons; now that the shade of the Dharma has been extended, the rituals of the Brahmans are being enacted.
We celebrate our taking refuge with even greater joy, hoping thereby to express our gratitude and repayment.

I pray that the Buddha’s fruition may be like the power of the *pūrṇa-maṇi*, equal and impartial. Although there is nothing sought that is not obtained, it must be moved by resonance before the response is communicated.

Venturing to exhaust my sincere heart, I humbly implore Your compassionate illumination. At present, the winter darkness is not yet firm and the seasonal snow has long been overdue; [the harvest] is on the verge of being ruined.

Regarding the calamity of scorching drought, I am deeply concerned about the outbreak of pestilence. I prostrate myself and pray that you will not forsake your original vow to deliver sentient beings.
May the three white clouds of the flying deities swirl like soft goose feathers, and may the six-flowered snow cover the earth, lingering like the circling shadows of cranes.
It suppresses the demonic vapors across ten thousand *li* and brings forth auspicious blessings for the three farming seasons.

We offer thanks that the snow, which previously failed to fall despite six attempts, has finally descended; we are moved by the compassionate regard for all things shown through its hidden merit, as it transforms the harsh northern winds.

Welcoming the cold, flowers fly across the four fields and cotton-like clouds part across the thousand mountains. From this point on, the great earth shall receive profound bounty; from this day forth, all under heaven shall celebrate peace and prosperity.
Truly we are indebted for the Buddha’s compassion, and thus we humbly exhaust our expressions of gratitude.
Through various verses of praise, we extol the Buddha:

the weather is pure and harmonious, belonging to the season of Zhuming (Summer). This is precisely the anniversary of the Tathāgata’s birth. Ten thousand sages incline their hearts to gaze upon the Treasure.

The signs: Nine dragons spout water to bathe the golden body; the royal palace disregards the beauty of the jade flowers. On the snowy peaks you diligently cultivated the Way until the fruit was perfected.
With this vow, I pray further from this aspiration: may all the Sages grace us with their presence as we reach out to welcome them.

The Gate of Vows of the Medicine Master, Teacher of Medicine, has opened; he delivers all living beings from the calamities of ten thousand kalpas. The fragrance of the lotus blossoms perfumes the universe;
within the lapis lazuli light, pavilions and terraces overflow. The wondrous teaching of his single voice reaches the three realms; the seven-tiered silver lamps shine forth.
The Nine Heavens. Tonight, after fulfilling my vows through faith, auspicious light and auspicious qi shall come crowding at my door.
Amitābha! Amitābha!

The teachings of the Dharma have vibrated throughout the Western Land; the wondrous means by which you deliver all living beings are immeasurable. May the lotus pedestals of the nine grades descend to receive me.
Leading the way, seven tiers of precious trees stand in rows, fragrant and sublime. His towering golden form is majestic and beautiful; his brilliant silver hair emits a radiant light.
If faithful devotees can diligently praise and mindfully recollect him, they will instantly transcend to the Pure Land and realize the eternal truth.
The Buddha Blazing King of Śāla manifests his majestic supernormal powers, gathering the deities of the twelve palaces. His feet tread upon a golden wheel of brilliant radiance;
his body is draped in precious robes, auspicious and shimmering. Beyond the infinite accomplishment of auspiciousness, all calamities and misfortunes are eliminated.
In the midst of measurement, if you wish to know the place where the Golden Dawn receives blessings, the auspicious air at the gate and courtyard is lush and vibrant.
O Perfectly Penetrating One, O Great Compassionate Holy Lord! Your vows are vast and profound, beyond all discourse. The red lotus flower blooms under the moon.
The face is like a cascade of azure lapis lazuli water with ripples; the drifting rain of Dharma dispels the mists of heterodoxy, and the vast wind of compassion extinguishes the clouds of hindrance.
May your compassion increase our merit and virtue; may all be auspicious and as you wish, and may your life endure for a thousand springs.
The Subtle and Ineffable Discourse of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha of the Netherworld. His manifested true countenance appears everywhere;

those in the six realms and three paths hear the wondrous Dharma, and all beings of the four births and ten classes bathe in his compassionate grace. The precious jewel illuminates the path to heaven, and the golden staff knocks open the gates of hell.
At the gates of hell, that night the departed spirits were received by the Guide; upon the lotus pedestal, they paid homage to the Compassionate Honored One.

Maudgalyāyana, O Maudgalyāyana, the Venerable One, exercised his supernormal powers; casting his almsbowl into the air, he leaped through space in an instant. When his golden staff shook, the earth opened.

In the prison of the underworld, the pearl upon his brow illuminates all the way through to empty space. Desiring to cause his compassionate mother to be reborn in the heavenly realms, he repeatedly opened his sincere heart to inquire about the merits of the Buddha.
He reverently established the *Lanpen* (Ullambana) rites and lit the torch of wisdom; its influence shall flow down through ten thousand generations, forever without end.
Sizhou, Sizhou, the Bodhisattva named Saṃgha! I take refuge in you who dispels calamities and nurtures the sprouts of goodness. You bring refreshing grace to the Jetavana Grove like rain and dew;

your towering jeweled stupa pierces the clouds and mists. You open the teachings of the Six Perfections to drive away pestilence; your virtue saves all living beings. May you distinguish [the path] for us.
Right and wrong. I pray that you will depart from the Lotus Palace to attend this Dharma assembly; may great blessings be bestowed upon you, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

The Buddha Dingguang, the ancestral Buddha, halted at Tingzhou; having fulfilled the fruit of his true potential through cultivation over myriad kalpas, he struck the mountain with his staff and the spring gushed forth.

Commentary: The verse says: "The stream divides as it flows past the ancient bank; for those seeking sons or daughters, they appear according to one's heart. For prayers for rain or for clear skies, they grant rewards following one's intent.
May you depart from Nan Yan and attend this Dharma assembly; from now on, believe in the good and bathe in extraordinary blessings."

The Sixth Patriarch, the ancestral teacher, realized the profound mystery of true emptiness. His wisdom penetrates the numinous power of Prajñā; the bright mirror is not a stand, yet its light manifests transformation;

the Bodhi tree does not exist, yet the fruit’s fullness is all-encompassing. The robe was transmitted from the Western Land to clarify the Master’s intent; the Dharma was propagated in the Southern School to lead [beings].
Imperial Seal: The stream of the Caoxi lineage flows on inexhaustibly for ten thousand ages; the lamps continue their flames forever without end.

The Sangha at Unju is a supreme realm that crowns all quarters; the Sangha of Ryongji has established a site for the Way, where the majestic spirit of Seonyeo Mountain constantly provides its protection.

Protector! Your numinous manifestation on Mount Hu is most brilliant and far-reaching; the ten directions take refuge in you to dispel calamities and obstacles, and the four seas revere you to bring down auspiciousness.
We humbly pray that you will look upon this Dharma assembly with compassion, as we reverently burn this single offering of incense.
Kālaṃ Kālaṃ was originally the Honored Anāthapiṇḍada. He made vows and practiced to stabilize the Dharma-gate;

above, he blessed the Tathāgata so he might return to the Right Path, and below, he brought peace to the sons of Śākya so they might extinguish the roots of evil. He caused the precious monastery to flourish for a thousand years, and protected the vihāra for ten thousand [ages].
Ancient remains endure. This night, through the power of praise and offerings, the Dharma assembly early on bathes in Imperial grace.

The sacred altar of the King of the Community, its ancient traces, anchors the mountains and rivers; the local people’s prayers receive many responsive manifestations. The Sage’s majestic virtue bestows blessings from on high.

His majesty’s manifest traces have eradicated demons and malevolent spirits; we rely on his auspicious bounty to take refuge in the Triple Gem and depend upon the Six Principles of Harmony to repay his gracious kindness.
From this day forth, our villages shall be ever peaceful and secure; may the life-span of every person rise as high and majestic as a mountain peak.

In anticipation of the inevitable aging of skin like chicken-skin and hair like crane-feathers, one busily burns bright incense before the Buddha. The auspicious candles glow, outshining the night moon;
the precious banners flutter, chasing the cold winds. This is the path of manifest truth beneath the mountain of the field of merit, a bridge spanning the heart of the sea of suffering.
The Bridge of Dharma: How wonderful that this is the day of returning home for a hundred years! With unswerving ease, one ascends to the vermilion heavens.
This Daoist nun has prepared herself in advance;
standing solitary amidst the cold of winter, her acts of worshipping stupas and upholding sutras are beyond measure. She advances further within the grove of merit.

Step forward; on the path to Bodhi, it is best to gather your achievements. Seven-tiered silver candles support the Emperor of the Netherworld; four volumes of lapis lazuli scriptures answer the Sage’s sagacity.
If you wish to know where the preliminary cultivation reaches fulfillment, look at the single bright moon shining clearly across the vast sky.

Beholding the *Avataṃsaka*, one turns the mind toward goodness; reciting the *Avataṃsaka*, the realization of nature becomes clear and is no longer ordinary. Having read through the Tripitaka, one returns to the Treasure Store;
invited by fellow monks, one observes the Eight Precepts within the monastery. Gazing up at the Buddha-lands of the three thousandfold world-system, one repeatedly expounds the numinous texts.
Two Volumes. To recognize the place where the wondrous cause is perfected: A single wheel of bright moon reflects upon a cold pond.

Repenting the Blood Basin, one recalls the years of one’s compassionate mother’s childbirth; the myriad hardships and sufferings are not easy to describe—ten months of carrying the burden, difficult to repay.

Virtue! For three years she maintained a vegetarian fast, vowing to repay her debt of gratitude. The Blood Basin was transformed into a pool of red lotuses; hell was overturned into a gate to the Pure Land.
That she subsequently attained wealth, nobility, and splendor was truly due to her practice of filial piety, which moved both Heaven and Earth.

Returning the lamps, I fulfill my vow from years past, when I knelt to pray to the Golden Immortal. Tonight, to repay his grace, I establish this Dharma feast. Seven-tiered lapis lazuli towers burn the torches of wisdom;
a single incense burner wafts auspicious smoke of *campaka* flowers. Where silver lamps shimmer, calamities and obstacles are dispelled; as the golden chime strikes, [all afflictions] are cleansed.
Transgressions and faults are cleared away; this is the place where merit is perfected and the mind is fulfilled. May the blessings of the entire family and its kin be continuous and enduring.

By erecting lamps, performing repentance rites at the stupa, and celebrating the faith and goodness of the household, they exhaust their sincerity. Upon completing the prostrations at the pagoda, all vows are fulfilled, and within the radiance of the *śarīra*, ten thousand blessings are contained.

The Image: Within the reflection of True Suchness, a thousand bodies appear; the public case of the Tathāgata honors sublime blessings. With blazing stars and radiant flames, one establishes wondrous causes;
the confession is complete and perfect, protected by all Buddhas. May glory, flowers, and wealth ensure a thousand springs.

The assembly of faithful believers repent before the stupa; their hearts turn toward it with individual sincerity and devotion. They sweep the streets and alleys to gather roots of goodness. Incense burns upon the mountain-like incense burner as they chant jade-like verses;

they gaze upon the stupa of Aśoka and pay homage to the Golden Immortal. Person by person, lightning-swept, a thousand calamities are extinguished; household by household, clouds arrive in fivefold abundance.
May all blessings be complete. From this day forth, may the people be at peace and the state prosperous; may the sovereign’s sacred life endure for ten thousand years.

We pray for rain, lamenting that the tortoise-shell cracks are broken and the fields lie fallow. The fire-sun scorches the sky and the waters cease to flow; how great is the calamity wrought by the drought-demon!

How bitter! The dancing of the *śarabha* has ceased, yet true cause for concern remains. The people’s hearts are so earnest that their pleas find no outlet. May our Buddha, in his great compassion, respond to these prayers:
I pray that a sweet rain may pour down to revive all things, causing the crops to flourish and the autumn harvest to be bountiful.

Praying for Clear Skies: The Jade Incense in the Golden Furnace Unfolds in Swirling Vapor. The Lay Practitioner Prays for Clear Skies with Diligent Resolve. When the Buddha’s Name is Chanted, the Thousand Sages Assemble;
Where the Sound of the Dharma Resounds, the Nine Heavens Hear It. A Pure Breeze Blows Away the Mists of a Thousand Mountains; The Crimson Sun Burns Open Ten Thousand Clouds.
Li Yun: May the Sage’s merit descend in response, so that no more heavy rains fall in profusion.
These scattered flowers originally required no planting or nurturing; thank you, O skilled artisan, for your clever cutting and shaping. A thousand varieties of brocade display their elegance.

Their appearance is like five-colored silks, utterly free from even a speck of dust. Their growth does not depend on the power of the springtime warmth; how could they be worried about being withered by wind or rain?
Holding them up before the Buddha to offer this auspicious verse, I pray that blessings and prosperity may come together every day.

The Brahma-voice that unties the knots is as clear and resonant as the tide; it circles the silver lamps through the deep of midnight. With the seventy-seven vows, the cultivation of merit is complete;
with the thirty-three knots untied, transgressions subside. May every sound enter the path of True Suchness, and may every thought remain forever without retreat.
Transform the mind. May the faithful be protected as they depart from here; may the vast ocean of blessings swell ten thousand fathoms.
Repent for killing:
in this fleeting life, one is busily ensnared within the cage of existence, binding oneself in endless cycles of enmity and resentment. Pray to the spirits and deities to seek blessings.
With vigor, one welcomes guests to display the family tradition: feathers and down are minced upon the cutting board and knife, while scales and shells are boiled and roasted within the cauldron.
As the assembly of faithful kindle lamps and extend their repentance, they all transcend at once to walk through the celestial palaces.

The divine banners are raised; five-colored streamers stand tall in the vast sky. Invoking faith between the realms of the seen and unseen, we hope for a spiritual resonance. Upon the hundred-foot pole, the colored phoenix soars;

amidst the clouds of the nine heavens, the flying dragon appears. May those wandering in the six paths be summoned back to the true limit, and may those in the three miserable realms be guided to enter [the Way].
The Main Ritual: During the two hours of the Dog and Pig (7–9 p.m.), extend the invitation: May the sages and worthies descend to this Dharma assembly.

Having perfected the pure precepts of releasing life for the winged and scaly creatures, may the sounds of Dharma music shatter the darkness of karmic obscurations; may the birds soar toward the azure sky and become phoenixes.

Departing, the fish swims through the deep marshes and transforms into a dragon; with its feathers and mane fully brushed, it returns to the Cinnabar Grotto. Its head and horns lightly shake as it passes through the Gate of Yu.
From this point on, the Buddha’s merit shall aid in its growth and transformation; in time, its blessings and rewards will surely acknowledge the kindness of man.
Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Gao Feng Longquan Monastery, Compiled by Ji Xian,
Scroll Five Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Gao Feng Longquan Monastery, Compiled by Ji Xian,
Scroll Six Section on Verses and Praises for the Dedication of the Deceased
In offering this for the deceased, we reflect that human life is as fragile as dew upon a leek; it is truly difficult to prolong.

Departure is like a solitary boat chasing the current of a rushing stream—the light of a hundred-year span has now come to an end, and the dark paths to the ninefold underworld are vast and bewildering.
Spreading mats for jade delicacies provided by the celestial kitchen, Incense burns in golden censers, its smoke reaching the shores of the sea.
One should listen well to the power of these virtuous causes and merits, As one travels far and straight to the Tuṣita Heaven.
Accumulating merit and virtue, his nature was mild and gentle; The jade-like descendants stood solemnly in rows within the courtyard.
Before even a hundred years had passed, his physical form became but a dream; He has already returned to the single path of the Nirvana Gate.
A lamp is lit at the seven-tiered pagoda to aid his posthumous blessings; The sutras unfold three topics to mourn the departed soul.
With a snap of the fingers, one directly hastens toward the stainless realm; transcending the mundane and entering the sacred, one accords with the true source.
Furthermore, even the blue sky and the bright moon are still subject to waning and waxing; how could anything in the human world ever be perfectly complete?
Originally it was thought that for a hundred years you would enjoy the five blessings; Who would have expected that in a single day you would return to the deep springs?
The hearts and entrails of the children and grandchildren in the hall are broken; The kinsmen and relatives of the entire clan shed a continuous stream of tears.
I look up with hope that your honored spirit may receive the power of the Buddha, And within the light of the white tuft of hair, pay homage to the Golden Immortal.
This lady possesses a refined virtue free from even the slightest flaw; she has returned to wed into a family that has accumulated goodness for generations.
In her lineage, orchids and lilies flourish upon the steps, and within her halls, gold and jade abound to provide for her life’s journey.
May your lifespan be as long as that of a tortoise; how could it be said that your soul follows the distant dream of a butterfly?
By burning lamps to honor the Buddha and support your transformation, may we meet at the Dragon Flower Assembly together from this life through all future generations, O Elder.
Health, peace, wealth, and longevity are all fully possessed; He is worthy to be an immortal youth among men.
His fragrance spreads far, and all rise in reverence; His descendants flourish in excellence, all esteemed as virtuous.
We have already seen one phoenix soar beyond the clouds; Yet we have not yet beheld two dragons transform before our eyes.
Relying on the Buddha’s compassion, I extend this memorial for your deliverance; may your heroic spirit soar to the Tuṣita Heaven.
I memorialize you, Master Xingjia: your accumulated karma is truly pitiable; having vanished in the west, you have risen in the east, like the setting sun.
The spirit has departed upon the journey through the clouds; now there is a path. The filial grandson sheds tears of grief that soak his robes.
Though you were of great longevity and had no cause for regret, how can we bear that your humble heart has suddenly lost its reliance?
May the Buddha’s compassion guide and receive you, that you may follow the single sandalwood shoe back to the West.
Lady Jianpo possessed virtuous conduct worthy of her station; through diligence and frugality, she was honored by all in the household.
Though looking up, one might say there was not a single son, yet beholding her countenance, one rejoices in having many grandsons.
May their lifespans be as firm as the celestial cypress; who would have thought their bodies would follow the rushing waters?
Tonight, this filial descendant honors the sublime fruit, vowing to follow my Buddha through the gates of heaven to his parents.
The Sublime and Difficult Treatise on the Empowerment of Bhaiṣajyaguru;

Relying upon your compassion, you offer for the two souls the Dharma rain that washes away the obstacles of karmic resentment; May the lamp of wisdom illuminate and shatter the gates of birth and death.
In years past, I already bore the debt of your tireless labor; On this night, how can I repay the kindness of my parents?
I humbly pray that my parents may ascend the sublime lotus pedestal of goodness to pay homage to the Compassionate Honored One in the highest grade;
That my late father’s single dream of ripened yellow millet has ended, leaving his path shrouded in gloomy mist and sorrowful clouds as he departs into the vast unknown.
Facing the scenery, my eyes of double tears have withered; Before the wind, my ninefold bowels knot in vain.
My writings shall remain for a thousand ages in this pure world; My soul and spirit tonight return to my native land.
Ascending the heights, I lament and aspire to the sublime fruit; I vow to follow our Buddha to the Western Land.
Furthermore, the sorrowful clouds darken as tears fill my cheeks; I recall my late father, having ascended Mount Hu nearly seven times.
Raising a sigh at the sight of the mountain, the person is not seen; Entrusting my lamentation to the "Liao Yi" ode, the matter is truly pitiable.
In the Hall of Pure Brilliance, who knows where you have gone? Within the white silk curtains, you cannot be summoned back.
Relying solely on the power of merit from this night, May your compassion guide you to walk upon the lotus pedestal to offer sustenance for your mother.
In the past, I severed my loom to seek a fragrant neighbor; once parted, voice and countenance can no longer be sought.
I cannot bear to see the grain harvested from the fields and hear with sorrow the maple leaves falling across the plains.
Time and again I gaze upon the clouds, longing for my parents' faces; weeping over bamboo shoots, there is no way to manifest my filial heart.
A special vegetarian feast was prepared as an offering, And throughout the great trichiliocosm, the Buddha-lands resounded with the roar of thunder.
Again three years passed, my tears of blood drenched the crimson earth; The care she gave me in raising me was like a dream.

Ceasing the communal rites, I harbor the old resentment of years past; Feeling moved by the lingering customs of my neighbor today, I recall how I once hoped for a long life as enduring as the *chun* tree. Who would have thought that the hall of my mother would now be so silent and empty?
I pray that through the power of Maudgalyāyana’s filial piety, My compassionate parent may from this day forth ascend to the celestial palace.

At the minor anniversary of my mother’s passing, I accumulated merit and cultivated practice, spreading filial piety through my three generations of kin. By following her will and honoring her countenance, I brought the way of filiality to its conclusion.
Though the day lily withered at the end of her twilight years, the peach blossoms bloom once more, smiling in the spring breeze.
White clouds stretch to the horizon, separated by distant passes and mountains; the green birds return, yet no news is conveyed.
Worshiping the Buddha to cultivate roots of merit in requital for boundless kindness, she ascends on high to tread upon the nine lotus palaces—on the Great Auspicious Anniversary of her Mother.
First, you followed one dream back to Penglai; Your departed soul flowed away, never to return.
First you pursued white clouds to the grotto-palaces, Then followed green birds across the jade terraces.
Ever since we parted as the *huanyu* grass withered, I have thrice witnessed the plum blossoms betraying their opening.
The grieving son Chongyin extends the way of filial piety, Having long ago followed Maitreya to descend into birth;
He offers this memorial for his husband with a thousand acts of blood and tears that would shatter the city walls— Yet he does not see the man who once tied the hair-knots of marriage.
On this seat, new laughter and speech are hard to hear; From the tip of the brush, only the old spirit is written.
A phoenix soars in the mirror—alas for its solitary shadow; A peacock stands upon the hairpin—regret for being alone.
In bowing to the Buddha and practicing cultivation, one’s merit is great; Turning back toward the karma-mirror, not even a speck of dust remains.
Furthermore, we originally vowed to grow old together for a hundred years; who would have thought that my husband’s life would suddenly end so soon?
The one who once shared a brow with me is no more; today, the vow of our tied hair has become empty.
To transcend the deep and vast ocean of suffering, one must rely on the merit of the compassionate boat for deliverance.
How can I repay the sorrowful kindness of the stone that rose [in response]? May the seven-tiered lamp of grace shine with the crimson glow of lotuses, as an offering for my wife.
Husband and wife originally hoped for a hundred years together; Who would have thought that their affection would not last long?
The embroidered chambers are desolate and no one is seen; The dressing table is cold and the mirror lacks its luster.
The broken strings, in bitter sorrow, can never be mended again; The deep bond of marriage from the tying of hair is truly a cause for grief.
May these auspicious causes lead you back to the Inner Court; with six-zhu robes and sashes, brush away the celestial fragrance.
Yet as the clouds return to the desolate scenery of the immortal isles, the strings of the lute break, leaving even those who hear them with hearts broken.
The old matter of beating the basin invites derisive laughter from others; The new sorrow of binding the hair in marriage is truly heart-wrenching.
At dawn, the dew is cold upon the phoenix-mirror stand; At midnight, the wind extinguishes the incense in the phoenix-pavilion.
I pray you lend the power of the Buddha’s skillful means To support this noble spirit and ascend to the heavenly realm.
My wife passed away while giving birth;
her lifelong virtuous character has left behind a fragrant legacy. In a single moment, we suddenly heard she had perished in the painted hall;
that the flower should wither before its fruit is truly lamentable. That the oyster should shatter for the sake of the pearl is indeed a cause for deep sorrow.
Where are those within the Sandalwood Pavilion of the Moon? The mist is bleak and the path through the dark gates grows ever longer.
I imagine your soul has returned to the Wu Gorges; May you soon return to Tuṣita to pay homage to the King of Physicians and offer prayers for your brother.
Sharing branches and the same breath, we have been graced by the light of your benevolence; Suddenly, in an instant, we are startled by the injury of our own kin.
The *jiji* birds upon the plain cannot aid one another in their urgency; The wild geese amidst the clouds fail to form a single flight.
In the places where we once roamed among the bamboo groves, there is only sorrowful weeping; Beneath the shade of the *tángdì* trees, my heart feels as if it would break.
I only pray that my deceased elder brother, by the power of the Buddha, May ascend the nine grades of the lotus pedestal to the Western Land.
My brother has newly passed the imperial examination;
though he died at the thorny gate, He high broke the cassia branch, his fragrance still lingering. Having triumphantly ascended the yellow dragon robe, his fame spreads far and wide.
In governing the state, he never accepted triple emoluments; Having bid farewell to his kin, he suddenly returned to the realm of the Nine Springs.
Upon the *jilíng* plain, he grieves for being without companions; Amidst the clouds, like wild geese, he suffers the pain of a broken flight.
On this auspicious night, a vegetarian feast is prepared to repay his profound virtue; May his spirit enter the Hall of Universal Radiance.
When my younger brother was sent forth, he lagged behind while I vied for the lead; now that I go and he comes, our roles are reversed and topsy-turvy.
Like wild geese who have lost their flock, we grieve under the night moon; like *jiji* birds with no companion, we weep amidst the morning mist.
If you wish to assist the departing spirit in transcending to rebirth, You must rely upon the compassionate proclamation of the Secret [Teachings].
Diligently honor Amitābha and return to Sukhāvatī; Be born early in the Highest Grade, treading upon the red lotus.
I, your brother, have received this exhortation.
Having achieved victory in the literary arena, you stand preeminent among the multitude of talents; how much more so as your brilliance has blossomed in your youth!
The *tángdì* (plum and pear trees) were originally expected to flourish together in splendor, yet who would have anticipated that half of the *tíngjīng* (thorn bushes) would wither away?
Like wild geese crying out in unison when separated from their flock, you and your brother now fly and call to one another like *jílíng* birds.
How can one repay the old kindness of hands and feet? I specially venerate the Buddha-fruit to honor his heroic spirit.
For his son, every ordinary cough and spittle became pearls; His outstanding and elegant brilliance was beyond what could be captured by brush.
The White Jade Tower is completed; the summons to depart is urgent. The Yellow Millet Dream has ended, suddenly becoming empty.
Your parents shed tears that fill their eyes in vain; Ten thousand scrolls of books remain full upon the desk.
It is best to return directly to Tuṣita Heaven; There is no need to turn back and long for Penglai or Fúhú.
Furthermore, the phoenix chick suddenly returns to the crimson heavens; In the vast distance, clouds grieve as the path ahead stretches far.
The bright pearl within the hall is known to have vanished in darkness; The jade tree before the steps feels its fragrance fade away.
Who shall inherit the ancestral legacy? The gate of loyalty and filial piety lies in silent desolation.
May you rely upon the fruits of the Buddhas present before you, and aspire to transcend the three realms of saṃsāra.
[Dedication for the deceased] (Qin, Qi, Shu, Hua).
An outstanding and spirited youth from your noble house, In his youth, his fame has spread across the four seas.
At the Go board, who dares to rival him as he refines the stones? His vigorous brush, capable of lifting a thousand *jin*, is praised by all.
His mastery of painting rivals that of Wang Moqie; In his appreciation of mountains and waters, he finds a true *Ziqi*.
It is a pity that the wise man withered so quickly; facing the wind, there are none whose tears do not fall in pairs.
You passed away young, in the prime of life, your spirit as steadfast as a rainbow; who would have thought your natural lifespan would thus end so abruptly?
A lifetime flows like water, a passing horse through a crevice; worldly affairs are like floating clouds, lightning flashing across the sky.
Having been born with the precepts of the fragrant bag, one should, upon death, return to the Treasure Moon Palace.
If you awaken to the Dharma-body free from all hindrance, you shall joyfully mount the cloud-chariot and traverse perfect penetration.
Furthermore, no longer seeing that child before my knees, I suddenly cause my parents' tears to fall like rain.
The orchid leaves have now fallen from their branches; where can the phoenix chick go once it has left its nest?
Deeply lamenting, who shall continue the legacy of the *jīqiú* (archery and robes)? Unconsciously, I feel only a growing sorrow for my kin.
Relying solely on the power of the Buddha-vehicle to assist in the memorial offerings, may the pearl return to Hepu and shine upon the court. Memorial Offering for the Daughter.
The virtue of orchids and calamus, the spirit of jade; A graceful, crystalline beauty far beyond compare.
Her skill in weaving rivals the celestial maidens; Her artistry in cutting excels that of those in the mortal world.
The mirror stand lies empty, locking away the luster of the autumn moon; The curtained bed is still, where only the motes of dust dance.
Regretfully, her flower-like countenance cannot be retained; I pray that by the power of the Buddha she may awaken to the noble cause.
Furthermore, the fragrant orchids have withered and failed to form a grove; the kindness of her former nurturing is now entirely void.
The Jade Maidens see her return to the realm of Penglao; The Moon Goddess now returns to the Palace of Guanghan.
The willow-like brows remain green through the three springs; The lotus-like face retains its crimson through the nine summers.
By the power of the Buddha, she is pointed toward her destination: Amidst fragrant clouds, her feet are supported within the Nine Heavens.
Furthermore, the parents' eyes were brimming with tears; Because they had lost their elegant daughter from the inner chambers, The phoenix departed from the Qin tower, adding to old regrets;
The flowers withered in the Kunlun garden, giving rise to new sorrow.
Already you have hurried the fragrant banners back to the immortal isle; In vain we imagine your lovely countenance returning to the hall of celebration.
I only pray that your noble spirit may ride upon the wondrous fruit, Attending the Buddha-Mother to realize the True Constant.
Her natural, virtuous character was far beyond the ordinary; In a single moment, we suddenly heard she had perished in the painted hall.
The鹊桥 (Qiao Bridge) in the heavens can no longer be crossed; The flower-lamp wedding in the human world has not yet been shared.
Clouds obscure the Wu Gorges as her returning soul vanishes; The moon grows cold at Quan Pass as her path forward becomes vast and lost.
May we be companions to Avalokiteśvara, soaring freely upon Mount Potalaka;
sisters sharing a branch as kin for how long, until suddenly returning to the spring pass, we lost our refuge.
I recall how we once received instruction together in our mother’s hall; who would have expected that we, like geese in a row, would now fly apart?
A mournful wind blows through the fragrant chambers all day long, and tears fall like rain upon the emerald curtains through the lingering night.
Where shall your noble spirit find its transformation? May the Moon Goddess and her immortals lead you back to your original home.
The father-in-law and mother-in-law, one pillow’s dream beneath the southern locust tree; Facing this scene, I recall them with tears even more bitter.
In the blink of an eye, I am suddenly startled by the collapse of the ridgepole; With a broken heart, I can only sigh as Mount Tai crumbles away.
Sighing in deep anguish, tears flow like rain without end;
With a sorrowful brow locked fast in grief, how can this half-son repay such profound kindness? May your heroic soul behold the Tathāgata.
Her crystalline purity and dignified bearing were worthy of emulation; now that the Fairy has returned to the netherworld, she will not come back again.
Just as we rejoiced that the son-in-law on the eastern couch was a fitting match, who would have expected Mount Tai to suddenly crumble?
The outer family harbors lingering resentment as the clouds bury their traces; the daughter-in-law grieves for her kindness as tears sweep across her cheeks.
Tonight, may you well avail yourself of the power of this memorial service, And follow Maitreya down to his birth in the world.
When the mother-in-law and the paternal aunt suddenly perish in the high hall, The mist darkens and the wind laments, shaking the white poplars.
Regrettably, his true soul has returned to the Northern Lord’s realm; In vain remains the lingering affection for this "eastern couch" (the successor).
In sorrow, there are but a thousand lines of tears; To repay his virtue, one must rely on a single incense offering.
Furthermore, listen to the three topics of true Prajñāpāramitā; May you well ride upon the wondrous fruit to the Western Land.
Furthermore, from birth to death there is no reliance; the gates of the netherworld are shrouded in mystery across tens of thousands of leagues.
Not having expected that a close relative would now pass away, this grief causes the half-son’s sorrowful feelings to redouble.
In the northern hall, one can only bear to see the darkening clouds; from the eastern terrace, one hears in vain the rain of tears filling the void.
May you grant the aid of hidden merit to assist in the ancestral offerings, so that she may soon ascend to Penglai and Yingzhou with the Queen Mother, as the bride of the King of the West.
The cycle of birth and death is most pitiable; Upon hearing news of misfortune, tears stain one’s robes.
That man who once rode the dragon is no longer seen; Where has his trace returned this morning?
I hear not of my son-in-law returning to my sight; How can I bear to see the eastern chamber silent as the door is closed?
The Bodhisattva leads the way to the Tuṣita realm; his golden countenance is magnificent and sublime.
Those who gather around the bier find human life like a dream within the soul; the four elements are all cast aside as nothing but emptiness.
Six pieces of wood encircle the perimeter, Encompassing the entire trichiliocosm.
From now on, one is freed from the tethering halter of profit and fame; The cage of karmic offenses shall never be encountered again.
Circling this at a fine hour while extending ten recitations, One suddenly transcends the tainted realms and proceeds to the Western Palace.
Burying my father, my tears flowed so profusely that my eyes have hardly ever dried; I always lamented that my late lord would not return.
For several years I stayed at the Tiger-Taming Hermitage, yet by tomorrow morning I shall have returned to Sleeping Dragon Mountain.
The verdant tomb is envied by all; the soaring *huabiao* pillar stands tall where cranes roam in leisure.
Beholding the burning of yellow papers beneath the palace gates, the grandsons fill the hall as they line up for the court assembly. — *Cangmu* (Burial of the Mother)
As soon as the sound of the dirges is heard, The filial son’s grief for his parent pours like rain.
The crimson banner flutters as it meets the white hearse; The dark pines grow dense, enclosing the noble tomb.
The soul departs from the festive hall as the clouds darken; The spirit travels to the Jade Palace to accompany the moon’s radiance.
Take heed, O true spirit, and mount the fruit of Buddhahood; the path leading back to Tuṣita Heaven is now pointed out.
The funeral rites are completed and the burial fresh;
once parted in life and death, reunion will be difficult. As I recall your voice and countenance, my tears do not cease to flow.
The eyes turn toward the azure mountains where the clouds darken; The wind scatters yellow leaves as the dew falls thickly.
Though the funeral carriage halted long ago, The crimson banner has now found its rest through divination.
May the Buddha’s light further grant guidance, So that turning one's head, the body stands amidst the purple clouds.
The relocation and burial at this peaceful tomb: years ago the site was divined as a "returning dragon.
Today it has been moved here, surrounded by waters that encircle it and facing a winding stream. The couch-mountain rises in layered tiers, towering into the cold sky.
The source of prosperity flows on through a thousand generations; Ennobling edicts descend in rapid succession from the Nine Palaces.
Respectfully establishing lotus lanterns within the imperial tomb precincts, His descendants shall enjoy blessings forever without end.
I offer this new congratulation to my friend upon his recent advancement.
His spirit was as clear and pure as ice in a jade pitcher; his fame and renown spread throughout the imperial capital.
Yet, who would have thought that the summons from the Jade Tower would hasten his passing, suddenly causing his name on the golden list to remain in vain?
Though he donned the azure robes in a hollow ceremony, the imperial grace bestowed upon him remains heavy; his friends in the orchid circle can only increase their tears in profusion.
Recalling our former travels with deep bonds of affection, I have specially prepared these wondrous fruits to assist you on your journey through the clouds.
I offer this tribute for the deceased official, whose integrity was vast and whose demeanor ever dignified; he did not crave the ten thousand bells of emolument during his lifetime.
Magnanimous, he ever maintained the integrity of a high-minded scholar; Carefree, he truly captured the spirit of the ancients.
When the cycles of this world’s era were exhausted, All the literary talent within his breast became as empty air.
May the torch of wisdom be erected to offer solemn praise and lamentation; May he take refuge in the lofty abode of the Nine Lotus Palaces.
The elder official is eighty years of age, his virtue ever more sublime; In his later years he has received imperial grace, casting off his green robes.
Fortune and nobility rest with Heaven and are not easily attained; Life and death depend on fate and are truly difficult to evade.
A solitary man weeps blood, shedding teardrops like pearls; A widowed woman honors the causal conditions and bows before the Jade Radiance.
With a snap of the fingers, they go straight to the Land of Peaceful Nurturing; There is no need to turn back and long for the Peach of the Immortals, O Military Official.
Rare indeed is one as prosperous and noble as you; your vast spirit drifts like a ten-thousand-foot rainbow.
Sitting, you point toward the weapons of war to bring peace to the village; bestowed with rank and emolument, you strengthen the heroic.
I had hoped you would enjoy a long life like that of a tortoise; how could it be that you have so suddenly ended like a butterfly’s dream?
The departing spirit has returned to the stainless ground; who in this sagely court shall sweep away the lingering attachments?
This aged Confucian’s breast is rich with the books of five carts; a towering and heroic talent, a great scholar indeed.
Extremely great and extremely firm, he preserved his integrity; Possessing both kindness and bounty toward his village and neighbors.
Suddenly turning his head, he awoke from the dream of Zhuang Zhou; His diligent devotion was merely the surplus of Dong Yu’s efforts.
I still look toward your honored soul as it now attains liberation; With an empty mind, you have passed the imperial examination and walk the celestial thoroughfare.
A young Confucian scholar, in the prime of youth, has mastered a wealth of learning beyond compare; yet in a single moment, his fame and office have ended and all affairs have ceased.
With books remaining upon the desk while the person is no longer seen, his kinsmen and relatives are broken-hearted as their tears flow in vain.
Return early to the Buddha-land of the three thousandfold world; Cease longing for the twelve towers of the immortals' abode.
Form is emptiness, and emptiness is form; Clearly, it is but a single bubble upon the great ocean.
Proceeding on the Path, one transcends death.
With a jade whip he points afar toward the imperial capital; The spring examination roster awaits him as he strives to rank first.
Who would have thought that upon leaving his gate his body would transform, Just as he was about to break the cassia branch, his quest must cease?
This riverside is not the return to the Penglai Isles; Heaven above surely shall remember him in the Jade Towers.
Lamenting that the waters from the source of Wuling Pavilion continue to flow for you to this day through a thousand years;
there, a scholar drowned—
his talent and brilliance preeminent among the multitude of worthies— would have been ranked as the foremost immortal of Longmen.
Breaking the cassia branch, one follows the moon beneath the waves; Riding the raft, one mistakenly drifts through the sky upon the water.
To return to the source, one must reach the shore of Bodhi; To escape drowning, one must rely on the boat of Prajñā.
Where does the fragrant soul wander as it drifts? Beside the sands of the Golden Pond, one treads upon red lotuses.
The compassionate and wondrous virtue of the recommended monk is truly manifest; Never forgetting for a moment to recite the Buddha’s name or uphold the sutras,
He has utterly cast off the world of men, And returns as before to the Buddha’s homeland.
The mind of meditation is pure and bright as the moon; The observance of precepts is refined and strict, clean as frost.
If you wish to know where the Ultimate Truth has gone, The lunar orb reveals its clear light within the void.
Nirvāṇa—gone, gone, all conditions stilled; The central vase hung high, the journey already complete.
When returning with but a single shoe, the coffin is left behind in vain; Once the flower has fallen, the scenery can no longer be retained.
Who can rebuild the pillars and beams of the Dharma-gate? The vessel for crossing the sea of suffering shall no longer sail.
He cannot remain within the ranks of the Triple Gem; The waters of the eastern river flow on for a thousand ages.
Among physicians and monks, who can equal his lifelong dignity and frugality? His three robes of patched rags are worn through, yet he sews them back together again.
Constantly taking divine elixirs to heal the ailments of the multitude, Ever using palm leaves to investigate the True Doctrine;
His physical form resembles a thousand-year-old crane, And his integrity is like a ten-thousand-foot pine.
Once his body fell apart upon entering parinirvāṇa, Only the traces of his morning and evening meditation remain.
As Dharma-kinsmen we prostrated before our teacher to study the Way, fortunate as branches joined together; Suddenly, we heard that he had returned in his single shoe.
The Dharma-hall is now empty and bitterly mournful; Like geese in flight amidst the clouds, we lament our parting.
May you transcend the cool realm of the ten stages, And suddenly awaken to the potential for liberation through the three vehicles.
I dedicate this slight merit to repay your virtue; I further pray that we may meet again forever as fellow practitioners of the Way.
The waters of eight virtues reflect the void; In the palaces of the Pure Land, nine grades of lotuses bloom.
Śrīmālā sets forth a bridge to welcome the Buddha’s sons; Avalokiteśvara extends his hand to receive the celestial youths.
The melodic calls of sacred birds proclaim the Three Truths of emptiness; The clamor of precious music praises the six supernormal powers.
I do not know where your heroic soul has received this offering of mourning; in which flower does that single spirit now dwell?
The monk offers this memorial for his late mother, yet the Great Lady is no longer seen in the hall; suddenly, a thousand streams of tears fill my breast.
Coming like a fragment of cloud rising in a late-autumn valley, Departing like the solitary moon sinking behind a cold peak.
Turning back, the fruit of realization is fully attained; Counting on one's fingers, the time has come for the fifth and seventh days.
How shall the sons of Śākya repay the grace they have received? They light lamps upon the seven-tiered pagoda to manifest their sincere hearts.
I cultivate the fields to repay my benefactor, yet in a single day that benefactor has suddenly passed away. Moved by grief and sighing with sorrow, I stir the hearts of these farmers;
I have not heard of new grain being offered, but in reviewing the fields, I recall only the traces of his former footsteps.
In the orchid courtyard, tears fall as the cold wind blows; within the fragrant curtains, dust gathers as the gloomy mist thickens.
Having long enjoyed your protection, how can I repay it? I pray that, riding upon the Buddha’s power, you may ascend to the celestial palace to offer prayers for your master.
The Master of Mount Lu came to the human realm to study the Dharma, Never ceasing for a moment in his salvation of all living beings.
With his *juǎn* and *dòu* talismans, he overturned the world of spirits; With his numinous talismans, he secured and severed the gates of the ghosts.
He claimed his own body would never grow old, Yet how was it that through *shijie* (corpse-liberation) he departed and did not return?
A single blast of the horn sounds as it departs beyond the heavens; I imagine you have returned once more to Mount Lu.
At twenty-eight years of age, this courtesan is in the prime of her youth; her price for a single smile is not to be calculated even at a thousand pieces of gold.
In the hall of strings and pipes, the white days are spent; Within silken curtains and gauze canopies, the yellow dusk passes.
If one could command the love of a thousand people while alive, How could there not be a trace of gratitude after death?
Only the sentimental moon in the heavens Shines long upon this solitary grave through the clear nights.
A courtesan was murdered;
like a lotus emerging from the water, she was in full bloom. In an instant, her delicate form suddenly perished.
Her body lies upon the vast, desolate yellow sands, while her soul follows the white blade into the boundless void.
Before life ends, emotional consciousness sheds twin tears; for those who know one well, every inch of the gut is severed.
Mounting this impure, leaking body for the funeral rite, I pay homage to the King of Physicians within the light of the white tuft.
[Strangled to death.]
Throughout his life he flowed eastward like a great hero; In his view, death was no different from a dream.
Step by step he could not tread upon solid ground; At every turn he sought to collide with the void.
His manifested body entered directly into the realm of non-existence; With hands cast loose, he returned to the Palace of Joy.
I only pray that the Buddha’s compassion will extend its guidance, As colored clouds cradle his feet as I pay homage to his golden countenance.
The fire has burned out and the night is deep; the six windows are finally locked, And the monkey is no more; the man wanders within the dream of Zhuang Zhou.
In a daze, this body returns to the Great Illusion; In a panic, there is no way to descend from the upper story.
After the third watch, as the wind shifts and the fire turns, The smoke is extinguished, the ashes fly, and all affairs cease.
Mother and child need not harbor frequent regrets; Within the Samādhi of the Fire-Flame, wander freely at will.
