Section on Various Buddhist Rituals.
*Fadao wen* (This is for use when encountering a recent death; it is recited by those who summon the deceased soul to be reborn in the Buddha-land and to comfort the spirit-seat).

(Chant in unison): The World of Ultimate Bliss (All chant in unison) Amitābha Buddha (Four tones) Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (All chant in unison) Mahāsattva (Four tones) Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva (All chant in unison) Mahāsattva (Four tones) Ocean Assembly of Bodhisattvas (All chant in unison) Mahāsattva (Four tones)
I consider the physical body to be like a dream and this floating world to be insubstantial. Its birth is like a spark from a flint or a flash of lightning;
its death is like waves subsiding and water becoming clear. On this very day, [Name], your worldly ties have come to an end, and with the passing of life, you return to emptiness.
I still fear that the arrangement of the coffin and outer casket, and the wrapping of the garments and headdress, have not yet attained purity and are subject to various impurities.
Now, relying upon the Dharma-water to sprinkle these funerary preparations, may they all be rendered pure and entirely cleansed.
(Pure Water) Recite the following according to the instructions. (Gāthā)
The Buddha possesses *argha* water; Sprinkling it upon all afflictions (*kleśa*), All impurities are completely removed, Causing everything to be utterly pure.
(The Mantra of Pure Water): *Oṃ vajraśānti hūṃ hūṃ* (three times).
I reverently hear that human life is finite; it is wasted as one pursues fleeting appearances. Worldly affairs are rootless; they are as swift as drifting leaves.

Even if one possessed the nine-fold elixir of immortality or were granted a thousand vessels of wine, even if one fought alone and rose alone until committing suicide at the Wu River, or were captured and released seven times while sighing over remaining solitary and empty—Xu Yin’s poetic lament speaks of not dying.
To what can one turn? Emperor Wu’s poem says: "Seeking longevity, I see none; a skilled slayer of dragons, a butcher of beasts.
Unaware that the single nature is perfectly luminous, they vainly display the greed and desire of the six sense organs for fame and profit. All that overcomes the world is but a single great dream."

Wealth and nobility may startle the world, yet they cannot avoid the two characters of *anicca* (impermanence). Like thunder rising and lightning vanishing, or the moon waning and flowers withering, how many heroes have been worn away by the mountains and rivers?
When wind and fire disperse, there is neither old nor young; in a single day, there are the new and the ancient.

[Name] has today bid farewell to the human world and passed away into the realm of the spring. Fearing that he may encounter stagnation upon his journey through the underworld, I now offer this praise for him.
The Holy Name points out the way through the mazes of delusion; its resonance strikes the great bell, shaking open the dark recesses of the earth.

Relying upon the assembly of the Dharma, we reverently pray that Amitābha shall receive this newly departed soul and cause it to ascend to the Land of Bliss. (At this point, move the ritual implements and chant the hymns:
We only pray that [Name], whether new or old, may have the souls of those who have passed away from the underworld received and led upward to adorn the celestial realms.

Considering all things, none is better than the Great Hero (Mahāvīra) for applying the vessel of compassion to the sea of suffering; none is more effective than the Tamer (Vināyaka) for holding the torch of wisdom in the dark alleys of the world.
In the past, the great python was freed from suffering because of hearing the names of the Buddhas' offerings;

in days of yore, the parched fish ascended to heaven because of the flowing water chanting the name of the Victorious One (Ratnaśrī). These seven Great Tathāgatas are the compassionate fathers of the four modes of birth.
With vast and great vows, they rescue and deliver beings from birth and death; by reciting their name even once, ten thousand offenses are extinguished together.
Because there is such benefit, I proclaim this. I humbly hope that your venerable spirits will listen with sincere resolve.
I only pray that you will receive and guide the departed souls of both the new and old [the deceased], [namely] so-and-so, so that they may ascend to the celestial realms.
A hundred-year lifespan is but a mere instant; how could this illusory body composed of the four elements endure forever?

Even if one were to pile gold like a stupa, it cannot purchase eternal life at the end of one's term; even if one were to accumulate jade like a mountain, what can be done when one’s limit has been reached?

Yanshou: Do you not see that the young lord of the southern neighbor has his green hair changed to white, and that in the wealthy households of the northern quarter, there is song today but weeping yesterday?
Human life is like a candle before the wind; this floating existence is like ice within a fire.
Even the Master, who was the teacher of the six states, has returned to the road to the spring; even the World-Honored One, the sovereign of the three realms, is likewise...
Alas, beneath the twin *śāla* trees, one must sigh at how neither the sages of antiquity nor the worthies of today could avoid the cycle of birth and death.

On this very day, [the name of] such-and-such person, both former and present, has reached the end of their allotted lifespan and returned to emptiness through the transformations of illusion. Within the mourning curtains, we extend our sincere prayers for their deliverance;

the assembly of monastics offers their utmost devotion and earnest supplications. We recite verses on non-arising and strike the bell of impermanence. May they be bathed in these extraordinary merits and transcend to the blissful realms.
[Chant] (In the Kingdom): All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; they are the nature of arising and ceasing. When arising and ceasing have ceased, nirvana is bliss.
The Tathāgata has realized nirvana and forever severed birth and death. May the deceased listen with a sincere heart.
May immeasurable bliss be attained (recite three times for each).

We pray that you will receive and guide the deceased souls of [Name] and others, both new and old, so that their spirits may descend to the underworld and their lives may be adorned in the realm of rebirth. (At this point, strike the bell once more, three times.)
(Chanting: The first toll of the bell ascends to the Heaven of the Thirty-three. The second toll of the bell descends to the eighteen realms.
The third toll of the bell receives and guides the deceased, [Name], upward to adorn the realm of birth. (Phat!)
The deceased has already been confined within the coffin and outer casket; their spirit truly returns to emptiness.
Now, as the sounds of the Dharma music resound, they proceed directly to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
(Recite the Amitābha Dhāraṇī. By virtue of this dhāraṇī, may the deceased soul be reborn in the celestial realms. (Chorus: Reborn in the Celestial Realm.
[Chant] All with reverence and faith, we pay homage (Response: To the eternally abiding Triple Gem). [Recite the Buddha’s name].

With countenances adorned in purple-gold and white jade-like hair-tufts streaming forth, with a thousand spirals swirling upon the crown of the head and a body composed of ten billion parts, we reverently offer this bright incense.

With the utmost reverence, I respectfully address the Buddha Jewel, Dharma Jewel, and Sangha Jewel—all infinite throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions and across the three periods of past, present, and future;
all responsive spirits of the myriad beings; the Celestial, Earthly, and Aquatic Officials; the Four Rectifying Gonggao who report matters to the Three Realms;
the Great Deities of the Five Paths of the Netherworld; the Messengers who summon and escort the two souls; and those of the Yellow Robes and the Path of Karma.
O Divine Lord! O Messengers who cross the river! O tutelary deities of the ancestral dwellings of my former lineage!

I pray only that you descend to this Dharma assembly and witness these sincere petitions. I, Yang Daoxiao [Name], residing at [Village/Township/County] in [Month] of the Great Yuan Dynasty, submit this:
for the deceased [Name], aged [Number] years, on the [Day] of this month...
As he turned his face toward the end of his worldly life and suddenly passed away to the realm of the spring, we have ordered monks to sound the bells at our home to proclaim the Way.

Yet, fearing that people coming and going might tread upon the residence, and that the striking of drums and the tolling of bells, along with various forms of wailing, might offend the household deities and cause them alarm, we now rely on the scriptural teachings to uphold the Dharma in practice. We have cleared away the spirits and deities of the entire house and established prohibitions around its perimeter.
I humbly entreat all the deities to stand suspended in the void; once the funeral carriage has passed, please return to your respective quarters.
Recite these secret and wondrous words according to the instructions.
(Gāthā) The Buddha possesses the water of *āgata*; may the conscious spirit know this from afar. If but a single drop slightly moistens it, a hundred evils shall have no place to abide.
Aversion. (The Mantra for Purifying Water and Removing Impurities is:
Oṃ vighnāntaka mahāpracaṇḍa kha kha khāhi khāhi vikaṭavikarāla grāsani grāsani huṃ huṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ.

Having completed the recitation of the *vidyā-mantra* of the majestic traces from above the Sahā world and the sprinkling of the *āgata* perfumed water to dismiss the household deities (*gṛhadevatā*),

one should immediately prepare silver coins and first offer them to the Great Deity of the Five Paths of the Netherworld (*pāralaukika*) and the messengers who pursue and restrain the two souls (*ātman*).
Yellow-Robed Deity of Karmic Paths, Envoy for Crossing the River, we humbly entreat you to graciously accept this offering.
Thereafter, please wait for the moment when I strike the drum. We pray that all the divine hosts will guide the deceased, so-and-so, both new and old, to transcend and ascend to the Land of Bliss.
Recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* (strike the cymbals and proceed to the coffin; chant "Western Land of Ultimate Bliss" in unison).
Amitābha Buddha.
(Mantra) Recite the Amitābha Pure Land Mantra three times. (Leader) May the deceased souls receive this mantra. (Congregation in unison) Be reborn in the celestial realms.
I maintain that the single truth of profound stillness is fundamentally without going and without coming, whereas the myriad phenomena of floating splendor are subject to birth and extinction.
Thus, even our Great Sage Confucius had his final dream at the two pillars, and the Patriarch Bodhidharma still returned to the West with but a single sandal.
Among all the sages and worthies of past and present, none have escaped the cycle of birth and death. On this day...
There is now a certain deceased person who has newly entered the path of the netherworld and hopes to hear the Buddha-dharma.
We now extol the Triple Gem for the sake of their soul, so that the six sense objects may be instantly refreshed. We humbly entreat you to listen with a sincere mind;
listen with a sincere mind and receive it. (Recite: Namo Buddhāya. Namo Dharmāya. Namo Saṃghāya.
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Unsurpassed Honored One. I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One Free from Desire. I take refuge in the Saṅgha, the Honored One Among the Assembly.
Having completed taking refuge in the Buddha. Having completed taking refuge in the Dharma. Having completed taking refuge in the Saṅgha. (Recite together once.
Those who take refuge in the Buddha do not fall into hell. Those who take refuge in the Dharma do not fall among the hungry ghosts. Those who take refuge in the Saṅgha...
May they not fall among the animals. From this day forward, we take the Buddha as our teacher, the Dharma as our teacher, and the Sangha as our teacher.
Never again shall you take refuge in demons, malevolent spirits, or heterodox paths. We pray that the Triple Gem will compassionately accept and protect us.

Now, for the sake of the deceased’s fragrant soul, I shall further recite the names of the Seven Great Tathāgatas to offer them as a spiritual support. May they transcend to the pure realms. We humbly entreat the deceased spirit to focus their mind with single-minded devotion.
Listen attentively. Listen with a sincere mind and receive these teachings. (Recite the names of the Seven Jeweled Tathāgatas, harmonizing the voice each time.
(Gāthā: Unaware of the nature of True Suchness, one follows conditions to become defiled by dust. Having committed boundless sins, I now seek repentance with a sincere mind.
Repentance.
(The mantra says: Oṃ samayasattva (raise), Buddha-lokottara-bodhisattva (assembly in unison), mahāsattva.
I have heard that in the past, when the Buddha dwelt in the world, he brought benefit and joy for forty-nine years; his teachings circulated for two million years after his parinirvāṇa.
He who does not arise has no departure from the West, and he who does not cease has no coming to this Eastern land.
Having ceased, he may be a sage or an ordinary person; having arisen, there is neither increase nor decrease. On such-and-such a day, someone passed away; their worldly ties having been severed—
Fulfilled. The fruits of past karma have reached their consummation; the *śāla* tree of awakening has blossomed its flowers, and the music of the Dharma plays the melody of non-arising (*anutpāda*).
There are none who do not grieve for their kin at the eastern gate of filial piety. Yet, the Buddhas possess a subtle essence that ensures sentient beings never lose their fundamental source.
O Great Assembly, if the Dharma were forever exhausted and ceased to arise, even contemplating it would be insufficient to bring clarity; yet it constantly arises.

Extinction! Fearing death, where shall you turn? You should contemplate impermanence. Listen as I recite this verse. May the deceased listen with a sincere heart and attend closely (reciting the *Nirvāṇa* verses here).
I consider that in the Western Quarter there is a Buddha named Amitābha. The trees, groves, water, and birds proclaim the sound of the Dharma;

this resonance opens the ears and vibrates through the body within the Sahā world. His golden countenance and lotus-palms extend compassion, manifesting to deliver deceased spirits from the river of craving.
The assembly gathered before us, with one voice and in unison, chants the names of the ten Buddhas in harmony to assist the departing spirit in ascending to the pure realm.
The deceased, with a sincere mind, should listen attentively (here, recite the ten invocations of Amitābha’s name).
The preceding eulogy of the merit of the ten recitations is now complete. We respectfully dedicate this for the deceased, [Name].

For your soul that has departed upon the dark path from the beginning to the end of life, we pray that you may transcend to the Pure Land. We humbly beseech that lotus pedestals, banners, and canopies shall come to welcome you from the void;
that jade carriages and golden pennants shall ascend to receive and guide you. We prostrate ourselves in respectful farewell. (The assembly joins in: Homage to the Holy Assembly!

I consider that the souls in the netherworld are shrouded in profound obscurity, with no prospect of being seen again; the paths to the spring are vast and boundless, where surely there can be no day of returning once more.
Reflecting deeply upon this parting from the living at the spring, I rely upon these meager offerings to express my sorrowful farewells.

I look upward in hope that your spirit will look downward and graciously accept these three libations. I humbly request that the filial relatives, with sincere devotion, open the jar and pour the wine (set to the tune of "Willows Containing Smoke").
First libation: The first cup is poured. Alas! How bitter is the pain in the hearts of men. From now on, once parted, we fear it will be hard to find you again.

Unawares, tears flow down my breast. Second libation: The portion is increased. The deceased soul takes up the cup as it circulates. The six kinds of kinsmen and relatives shed tears profusely. From...
This marks another thousand springs [of years].
With two full cups of gold for the libation, relatives and kin choke with sobs of grief. Relying upon the Sangha, we briefly offer this dedication for the netherworld.

We pray that you may soon attain rebirth in the Pure Land. (At this point, strike the *ghaṇṭā* and bell three times; as the sound fades, chant the sacred name of Amitābha. Conclude by saying: "We only pray that you will receive and guide the deceased soul upward to adorn the realm of birth."
[The Preface to the Ritual for Offering Food to the Spirits].
(The opening of the memorial text may be composed at will; begin by invoking the Buddha.
We have heard that the Great Perfect Wisdom swiftly realizes the gateway of *dhāraṇī*, and that the treasury of the Tang dynasty radiates its brilliance, widely disseminating the secret teachings.
The traces of these [deceased] truly possess inconceivable virtues and the merit of the Unsurpassed Way.

By reverently observing the discipline of the Precious Seal and performing the memorial rites for the Golden Benevolence, we hope to rely upon the power of the subtle and wondrous, so that they may partake of this sacrificial banquet.

Facing the sacred curtains with reverence, we proclaim the holy teachings; we humbly pray that their honored spirits remain as if present, quietly listening to the true mantras and being fully satiated by the Dharma-food.
To forever satisfy hunger and thirst, I reverently uphold and recite this *Dhāraṇī for the King of Nectar’s Adorned Feast Offering*.
With filial devotion, the family offers incense and prostrates. *Namo sarvatathāgatānām arhatām samyaksaṃbuddhānām | Oṃ mara mara*.
SAMA RA SAMA YE HŪṂ (three times) NAMO SURUPAYE TATHĀGATĀYA TADYATHĀ OṂ SURU VA RA SURU VA RA SURU SVĀHĀ (three times)
When the Mantras are recited, mournful clouds darken the vast sky; when the Holy Name is proclaimed, the mists of sorrow swirl throughout the long day.
At this very moment, the filial kin [Name] humbly acts on behalf of the deceased [Name], whose soul has returned to Mount Dai and whose spirit has suddenly entered the gate of the spring.
The filial daughter grieves so that the nine clans lament, and the orphaned son sorrows so that the six relations choke with sobs. This is...

With exceptional solemnity, the memorial offerings were presented; the spirit-table was reverently set forth to bid farewell to the honored soul and to provide sustenance for the departing consciousness.
The filial relatives offered their gifts with earnest prostrations, while the monastics specifically chanted praises: (Sing: Great Sage, King of Ambrosia Bodhisattva.
The dream of Nanke cannot be recalled; With humble sincerity, I offer this special expression of grief.
Incense of agalloch and sandalwood is burned, perfuming the precious burner; Fine wine is poured from golden cups.
Bitter sounds and bitter resentments entwine within my breast; In sorrowful remembrance and longing, tears fill my cheeks.
I only pray that your heroic spirit will graciously accept this offering; I specially rely upon these sublime verses to recommend you to the realm of the netherworld.

For it is a fact that the realms of the unseen and the seen are far apart and life and death are separated; yet during your lifetime, as you were a close relative, you always bestowed your compassionate care upon me.

Since there would be no ritual of offering after death to manifest the transition from beginning to end, I, in my humble capacity, exhaust my sincere devotion to prepare these simple vegetarian foods.

A single melody of Dharma-sound is presented as one offering; the elegant strains of the Three Vehicles are offered to the three souls. This is specifically to repay the sentiments of those who possess virtue and to answer the principle of non-deviation.

I prostrate myself, praying that your honored spirit will not be obscured and will graciously partake of this sincere heart. May you, in your filial service, cease your grief and remain reverently respectful.
Libation (set to the tune of *Duànlìnzǐ*): First, pour the libation.
Holding the vessel, I draw the wine. May the deceased soul not remain oblivious, but discern and partake of this offering. Please rise; this is the first circuit of the cups.
Second libation: Filled with fragrant incense, the sacrificial offerings are arranged in rows before the spirit; may the soul and consciousness graciously partake. Third libation:
Full to the brim, the soul’s awareness is not obscured and it beholds as if still present; through this rite, we receive the Compassionate Honored One.
I briefly extend these three libations to specially manifest my singular sincerity; I have now composed this sacrificial text to be read before the spirit.
The preceding memorial has been fully proclaimed. I humbly beseech that your honored soul may graciously accept and behold this offering.

I pray that for the filial descendant [Name], who respectfully attends the door of mourning, the dream of the funeral rite shall dispel calamities and misfortunes shall scatter with the passing of time, as he returns to his home.

Casting off robes to welcome auspiciousness, may you gather blessings and fortune so that prosperity increases day by day. May your kin be peaceful and secure, and may your household and lineage be illustrious.
We look up to your sacred seat and pray for universal protection and sustenance. We respectfully bid farewell at the Hall of Filial Piety; we pray you take care of yourself. (Chant:
Transcendent Buddha-realm Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Eulogy for the Sacrificial Offering (Opening with the Invocation of Amitābha Buddha):

We have heard that when the Tathāgata manifested his transformative teachings, the light from his brow-pore pervaded heaven and earth; and when the Bodhisattvas cultivated their causal practices, their great vows encompassed all lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Since such majestic virtue has already ascended to the heights, how could it fail to deliver those souls in the netherworld? The path to the underworld is vast and profound...
With resources so scarce, the road to the underworld stretches vast and boundless—upon what can one rely? At the gate of death, the pain is profound;

without offerings, how can one see them off at their final end? For the deepest affection of kinsmen, if there were no libations, how could one manifest the rites? We prepare the six harmonious delicacies and refine the three virtues upon the platters and tables;
we rely solely upon the chanting of the *bānzhà* and depend upon the secret mantras (*mantra*) to transform ordinary food into jade-like feasts and rare delicacies.
Transforming dark wealth into silver, iron, gold, and ingots, one offers them to the honored spirits so they may obtain the joy of full satiation;

moistening the souls of the netherworld with abundance and glory. By reciting the *Amṛtakuṇḍalī Bhojana-dāraṇī* and sprinkling *argha* water, milk, and pouring offerings over the wicks and the savory foods, one can cause the consciousnesses of the departed to partake and enjoy them all as nectar (*amṛta*), ensuring that the deceased receive these offerings in their entirety.
The Supreme Essence (Amṛta) proclaims the True Mantra, spreading it throughout the assembly. The deceased, with a sincere mind, should listen attentively.
[Recite the mantra as before.]
In this memorial text,

we earnestly reflect that while the golden words have been proclaimed and the sacrificial offerings have been prepared in abundance, and the resonant ringing of the precious bells has assisted the souls in partaking of the feast,
although the virtue of satiation has been attained, the merit of transcendent deliverance has yet to be heard of; we fear that the nature-heaven remains dim and obscured.
Fearing that the mind-ground has become obscured and clouded, it is difficult to rely on guidance to achieve mastery.

Fortunately, the Buddhas possess the path of compassion, permitting all sentient beings to come and accomplish the merit of purification. These seven and six Tathāgatas are the compassionate fathers of the four modes of birth.
To recite their names even once allows one to leave suffering behind for ten thousand kalpas. In the past, the Elder Jalavāhana proclaimed the holy name to ten thousand wandering fish;
at that time, they later took rebirth as ten thousand devaputras upon death, attaining boundless lifespans.
Thus, one knows that these benefits are truly worthy of praise. Those who have passed away should listen with a sincere mind. (Recite: The Tathāgata Saptaratna.
The Holy Name:
Establishing substance while dwelling in the dusty world, making a vow to encounter Brahmā, with a pure mind I fully proclaim and with a sincere heart seek repentance.
Hā hūṃ oṃ samantamukhe svāhā (three times). May all enmity and karmic obstacles be extinguished;
May diligence arise to awaken at the site of enlightenment; May the wondrous, immeasurable wisdom of the Buddha-seeds be perfected;
May the suchness of reality be attained, realizing the eternal truth.
Há hūṃ oṃ yid te lü ni svāhā (three times). By hearing and reciting this true and profound mantra, blessings increase and calamities are dispelled.
By listening to and proclaiming these secret and wondrous words, enemies are transcended and transgressions are extinguished.
It is my earnest wish that the soul(s), receiving this sacrificial offering, may always experience a sense of fullness and forever be severed from hunger and emptiness.

His marks are far-reaching and sovereign, transcending the Three Heavens; his clarity is carefree, surpassing the Ten Stages. His three *hún* souls are not obscured, and his seven *pò* spirits remain solemn.
We humbly pray that you will honor this invitation to your journey through the clouds; we beseech you to take care of yourself. (Leader) Born in the Celestial Realm, Bodhisattva; (Chorus) Mahāsattva.
Invoking the Deceased (Appendix:
Ritual for the Laity) I reflect that the path to the underworld is profound and dark, and the road to the spring is vast and boundless. Where the wind of sorrow blows, it whistles coldly;
where the yin energy presses upon us, it is chilling and piercing. Since the deceased soul cast off its form, it has been as if in a dream. All the myriad schemes and endeavors of their lifetime—
After death, there is nothing to attend one; the seven *po* spirits do not know where they have gone, and the three *hun* souls have no certainty as to their place of rebirth.

Without relying on the compassionate mercy of our Buddha, it is difficult to enable the soul to attain liberation. Now, I am especially concerned that the spirit remains stagnant in the netherworld and has not yet descended.
I rely solely upon the golden bell to shake open the dark realm. Now, according to the sacred scriptures, there is the *Mantra for Breaking Hell*.
One should then recite: *Oṃ khara khara taye svāhā*.
Having completed the recitation of the mantra for opening the hells above, I pray that by the power of this incantation, you may hasten your journey. I look forward to...
May the officials of the underworld briefly extend their compassion; relying upon their messengers, may they graciously grant skillful means.

Accepting this present earnest invitation, please escort the deceased souls to descend to this place of practice, so that they may receive and partake of these merits. (Recite the gāthā, then chant the Universal Summoning Mantra three times.)
Shaking this bell to extend the invitation, may the departed souls, without being oblivious, hear it from afar.
May they receive the empowerment of the Three Jewels’ power and descend at this very moment tonight.
(Recite the Universal Invitation Mantra.)

That night, the Milky Way’s waves were clear and the jade water-clock hurried its toll. The stars in the sky shone with mutual brilliance, and the wheels and hooves outside the gate momentarily ceased their clamor.
It was precisely at this juncture of wandering between the realms of darkness, when people hear the recommendation for the deceased and offer their lamentations.
As incense of somber fragrance burned upon the altar, the Sanskrit chants raised the cadence of compassion. To summon a single spirit to descend and arrive, one must rely upon—

I make this earnest request three times. I humbly hope that all of you, out of your great compassion, will join your voices in entreaty and with single-minded devotion invite the Soul-Guiding Messengers of the Netherworld Authority, the Local Deities, and the Orthodox Spirits of this realm.

I pray that you, though burdened by these humble petitions, will take pity on the sentiments of ordinary beings and lead forth the fragrant soul of the deceased, [Name]. I further pray that their spirit remains clear and unclouded.

Your pure spirit remains as if present; by the power of the Buddha, you have come to this place. Guided by the divine banner, you arrive at this site where the One Truth is brilliant and pure, and the Five Blessings are serene and clear.
(Chorus: Having descended upon this ritual ground, may you accept these offerings for your lamentation.
With single-minded devotion, I again entreat the Soul-Inducing Messengers and the Local Deity of the Land. I pray that your divine power may be moved and your sacred virtue leave nothing unfulfilled.
I hereby invite the honored soul of the deceased, [Name]. I humbly pray that their soul may remain as if they were alive, and their spirit as if it were during their lifetime.

Relying on the vast and profound power of the Dharma, and sustained by the Buddha’s compassion to guide us across, may the three miserable realms forever cease and the six destinies be transcended together.
Having descended to this site of practice (and), we receive this offering for the deceased.
With single-minded devotion, I make this triple request to the Messengers Who Guide Souls from the Underworld, and to the Local Earth Deity of this realm:
I pray that your divine radiance may offer its praise and that your sacred traces may manifest spiritual power, so as to invite and escort the soul of the deceased [Name].

I humbly pray that, by means of these Dharma waters, their body and mind may be cleansed; that all myriad anxieties may suddenly become void, and that not a single speck of dust may defile them, so that the three souls may—
Present! The seven *pò* spirits, as if alive, descend upon this ritual site. (In harmony: Accept these offerings of mourning. Incense and flowers are offered; incense and flowers are offered.
Above, we reverently invoke Your divine majesty, which does not fail our petition. We lead forth the deceased, [Name]; may your heroic spirit remain unclouded.
The descent has been attained. We humbly entreat you to solemnly adjust your countenance and deportment, proceed to the assembly, pay homage to the Triple Gem, and gaze upon the myriad spirits.
Thereafter, take your seat in tranquility and graciously accept this sincere offering of mourning. Lead the way with the sounding of the *ghaṇṭā* and the recitation of mantras.
(If a deceased person is present, omit the following phrase "one fear. If no deceased person is present, proceed directly from here to lead them in to pay homage to the Buddha.)
Hitherto, relying upon the power of all Buddhas, we have summoned the deceased souls. Now that they have graciously descended, we invite them to enter the fragrant bath.
Here, the fragrant incense is prepared and the nature-fire is brought forth to boil; they are immersed in the exquisite jade-pool of the seven treasures, perfected by the water of eight virtues.
Thus shall the defilements of a thousand lifetimes be washed away, and the obscurations of ten thousand kalpas be cleansed, so that they no longer follow the cycle of the six realms.
[The water] returns, revealing alone the one true, pure reality. Although the essence of phenomena is inherently stainless, even the sages still cleanse their minds.
In the past, King Śuddhodana once bathed Prince Śākyamuni; for if there were so much as a speck of impurity, it would be difficult to draw near to the Compassionate Honored One of the Triple Gem.
Relying solely upon the empowerment of mantra power, may your body and mind both be purified. This is the teaching of our Buddha.
Within this [rite] is the Mantra for Bathing; I shall now reverently recite it:
*Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ vighnāntakṛte svāhā* (three times). To reach the far shore, one must rely on the compassionate boat;
to emerge from the river of birth and death, one must depend upon the power of wisdom. For the sake of the deceased souls...
Long cast out from the human world, they dwell for a long time upon the dark paths. In a state of frantic haste, they are compared to those in the royal court;

in a state of turbid stagnation, they are detained and confined within the underworld. Consequently, their garments are tattered and worn; their decorum and rites are neglected and lax; their bodies are exposed, foul-smelling, and putrid.

Tonight, as we perform this rite of merit, if our sincere hearts are not refined and solemn enough to welcome their spirits, we fear that our own bodies may be defiled by the presence of the sages and worthies.
Having committed an offense, I have specially prepared a set of garments for the netherworld, along with wealth and other articles, to be reverently burned and offered here to the honored soul.

I humbly pray that you will graciously accept them. Having lightly groomed and carefully adorned yourself, having adjusted your robes and fastened your cap and sash, you may then draw near to the Buddha-dharma and receive its noble causes.
Within our Buddhist teachings, there is the practice of transforming garments and silks.
Mantra: I reverently recite this.
Namo samantabuddhānām vairocanavikurvitasahe (three times). Having completed the ritual bathing and being fully attired, the soul shall rest upon the divine banner;
the filial attendant, with utmost reverence and devotion, kneels in prostration.

The great assembly proceeds forward with sincere hearts, while the honored souls follow behind with devoted intent. They hasten to the site of practice to personally receive the offerings for their deliverance.
There, they loftily raise the music of the Dharma and move the tide-like resonance of the teachings. With reverent composure and single-mindedness, they take refuge in the Triple Gem.
Just now, relying upon the power of all Buddhas and depending on secret mantras, we have summoned the deceased, [Name], at this doorway;

may their true soul and correct spirit descend and arrive in person. They have constantly heard the great names and sacred titles of the Triple Gem and all Buddhas, who are the good friends and fields of merit for all sentient beings.
If one can take refuge and turn toward them, immeasurable sins will be extinguished, and furthermore, immeasurable [merit] will be increased.
Merit. Nevertheless, though it be so, gaze up upon the Compassionate Honored One, cast off worldly toil, and listen as I recite. O deceased one, listen with a sincere heart;
listen and receive with a sincere heart. (Recite with a drawn-out tone until "參佛," at which point state the aforementioned details.)
With each prostration and bow, one pays homage to immeasurable Buddhas; from the place where one bows to the Buddhas, one bows to True Suchness (*tathatā*).

Universally bowing to True Suchness throughout the entire Dharma-realm—(the assembly joins in)—all karmic obstacles as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are completely eliminated, and in every lifetime one shall constantly practice the Bodhisattva path.

(Chant together: With two prostrations and two bows, I pay homage to the subtle and wondrous Dharma. From the place where the Dharma is honored, I bow to the jeweled casket. I universally bow to the jeweled caskets throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
May all karmic obstacles as numerous as the sands of the Ganges be completely eliminated. In every lifetime, may I constantly practice the Bodhisattva path.
Perform three prostrations and three bows to the Arhat Saṃgha; from the place where you bow to the Saṃgha, bow to the Śrāvakas. Bow universally to the Śrāvakas throughout the Dharma-realm.
(Chorus: May all karmic obstacles as numerous as the sands of the Ganges be completely eliminated, and may they always practice the Bodhisattva path in every lifetime.
Tonight I have passed by [the home of] such-and-such a person. Having completed my prostrations and worship of the Triple Gem, all my karmic obscurations are entirely extinguished.
I only pray that with this body and mind, I may benefit sentient beings and seek liberation. (Chant: *Namo buddhāya dharmāya saṃghāya namo ratnatrayāya*.

Respectfully addressed to the deceased, [Name]: Having completed the prostrations before the Triple Gem, I now humbly request that you follow my lead in bowing and circumambulating once to pay homage to the myriad spirits.
Thereafter, return to the spirit seat to listen to the Dharma and hear the sutras. From this moment forth, reform your past ways and cultivate the future;
do not again mistake the head for its reflection. Firmly uphold the precepts, meditative concentration, and wisdom; sever and cease greed, anger, and delusion; and abandon the mundane.
While still in the body, they have realized the Dharma-body; having transcended the human path, they have returned to the Buddha-path.

Serve with diligent filial piety, following me as I lead them forward (bowing to the deceased as one enters from the right to attend the Sage on the left; then entering again from the left to attend the Sage on the right; thereafter, return to the place of the spirit).
The honored soul having descended, the pure spirit returns to its numinous state; as the Teaching possesses the *dhāraṇī*, it is employed to extend consolation.
(Recite the Consolation *Dhāraṇī* three times.)
Sitting serenely in meditative absorption, he received the offerings for the funeral rites; listening to the Buddha’s Brahma-voice, he was instantly transcended to the lofty peaks of the Pure Land.
*Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Yuan on High Peak, Compiled by Ji Xian*, Scroll Seven.
*Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Yuan on High Peak, Compiled by Ji Xian*, Scroll Eight.
Regarding the ritual texts for the *hu* (offering) established within the various gates of Buddhist practice:

I have humbly heard that as soon as the celestial canopy was perfected, the myriad phenomena were distinguished; and when the ten thousand chariots first arose, all living beings were nurtured. Without departing from...
Within the three realms, one must necessarily transcend the six sense objects (*ṣaḍviṣaya*). The turmoil is like striking flint for fire; the striving is like the wheel of a well-drawing bucket.
By abandoning the root to pursue the branches, the shadows of affliction follow; by turning one's back on awakening and uniting with the dust, the path to Bodhi is severed.
Craving fame and profit is like one chasing a hare who fails to see Mount Tai; regarding what is right and what is wrong is like one catching a cicada who knows nothing of the yellow magpie.
Once the true cause is lost, false teachings arise; the three poisons remain deep and cannot be eliminated, and the six consciousnesses thereby fall into disorder.
One sinks into the sea of suffering and is submerged in the river of craving; driven by the restless nature of karma, there is nowhere one does not go.

To what can one be liberated amidst the six garments of worldly toil? Therefore, our Buddha, as the World-Honored Teacher, established the two provisional means of the sudden and the gradual to rescue those mired in the seven realms of existence and to transform the four modes of birth into the Way. Thus the Way was revealed and its name made manifest.
He unifies the three realms within his mind; when the mind is empty, the objective world ceases. He widely spreads the net of Dharma, opening the gates of conditioned merit and wisdom;
he directly enters the realm of signless *nirvāṇa* through the perfection of the marks of permanence.

He expounds the teachings of the Two Truths and the Three Vehicles to deliver all living beings, opening eight hundred and four thousand gates to specially gather all categories of sentient beings—how much more so those who drift aimlessly in this fleeting life!

The realms of the five aggregates are vast and boundless; there are many whose fox-like spirits and lingering souls have lost their ancestral sacrifices, and not a few who cling to grass and wood as departed ones.
Having failed to cultivate virtuous fruits while in the world and having created only evil causes during their lifetimes, they are thus caused to sink into oblivion with no means of liberation.
On this night, [insert name here] offers this petition, conceiving thoughts of compassion and giving rise to a heart of pity, specifically to provide—

The offerings of the Fragrant Accumulation [Buddha] have sanctified the site of the *bodhimaṇḍa*, and the ancient practice of providing for the hungry and the weak has served as a means to suitably transform them.
Is this not something known to all? Indeed, it is due to great fortune. Now, the sound of the Dharma resounds greatly and the chanting of the *brahman* hymns rises on high.

We entreat the orphaned spirits to descend upon this Dharma assembly. (Enter; perform the ritual of sprinkling water for purification. We have heard that within the earth there are prisons called the hells. These hells are not uniform, but consist of many varieties:
the eight cold and eight hot hells, the eighteen layers, the thirty-six locations where one dies and is reborn ten thousand times.
In all of these, beings suffer no end as they starve upon swallowing glowing iron and thirst upon drinking molten copper. There is no end to their suffering.
At that time, their punishment lasts for long kalpas. Take, for example, the eighteen lords of hell;

all because of a single moment of error, they hear nothing but bitter suffering for many years and do not encounter joy for eternal kalpas. There are a thousand varieties of instruments of torment, and not a single kind word is heard.
Sword-trees stand in dense rows along the paths, and fiery cities blaze fiercely on all four sides. This suffering is beyond description.

Cease your lamentations. Let us not speak yet of the unbearable heat of the furnace coals; rather, it is because the kalpas are so long and vast that the gates of the bird-entrance are difficult to open and the dark paths are impassable.
Were it not for the true mantras of our Buddha, how could the gates of hell be shattered?
Now, I entreat the Tripitaka Master to ring his golden bell and perform the empowerment for you with the Hell-Shattering Dhāraṇī. Thus he spoke in verse: (Gāthā)
The Buddhas bestow compassion and descend with the nectar of immortality;
their majestic power and swift, wondrous mantras can cause even the Avīci hell-beings to be shattered like dust until all is empty space.
*Namaḥ aṣṭāśatike samyaksambuddha-koṭibhyaḥ tadyathā...*
Oṃ jina jina vāśe dṛdhi dṛdhi hūṃ hūṃ. The empowerment of the *dhāraṇī* for breaking the earth is hereby completed.

It is hoped that the gates and locks of the hells shall be shattered, the boiling cauldrons and glowing coals extinguished, the hell-wardens shall show compassion, and the kings and officials shall grant amnesty. Hereafter, I rely upon this...
The great assembly together raises the *chao-yin* chant to proclaim the sacred name. (Chant: "Great Sage who Leads Souls, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. (Chant:
"The host of the vegetarian feast, the patron of the feast, and all those present in the ritual arena, bow their heads in prostration and pay homage.

With single-minded devotion, we invite all the hosts of spirits and deities from the infinite billions of worlds within the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system, throughout the realm of empty space and the entire dharma-realm. Ha!"

Liti-mother, the Ghost King Jiao-mian, the Brahman Seers, the hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and all sentient beings suffering in the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions;
those in the watery abodes, mountain forests, and the human realm’s shadowy boundaries;

those who died untimely deaths or evil deaths, and orphaned souls without a protector—may you all, by the power of the Buddha, descend together to this place of practice. At this very hour of this night, may you receive these offerings.
I have humbly heard that since the initial division of Chaos and the first opening of Yin and Yang, there have been rulers and ministers, fathers and sons.

For those scholars who cultivate the arts of peace and learning, what is the point of losing heart at their lamp-lit windows? For those who stabilize the state and secure the nation, how can they bear to die in the service of the King?
Whether they belong among the nine schools of thought or dwell within the gates of the Three Teachings, [they all share this same fate].
The Way has its periods of obstruction and penetration; nature and disposition have their categories of folly and wisdom.

Whether one is a merchant or a peddler, a farmer or a craftsman, a devotee of go or backgammon, or a member of the troupe of musicians and performers—whether one’s singing voice is winding and melodic, the sleeves of one’s dance fluttering, or one’s face adorned with painted brows and red cheeks;
whether one lies upon green fields or yellow sands; whether one peddles the arts of Mr. Junping or hangs out the mat of Lü Yang—[all these are paths].
The hooks of this world; the lifelong arts of the furnace-blower and the sorcerer’s incantations. Some study medicine but remain obscure, wasting their lives in idle days.
Others transmit technical skills that they have not mastered, needlessly traversing rivers and roads to lose their consciousness.
Some act as "gentlemen above the beams," practicing the villainy of the roadside; they seize the wealth of others to invite calamity, and recklessly offend the Jade [Emperor].

They are executed according to their crimes; they commit suicide by mutilating themselves, hanging themselves, throwing themselves into fire, or leaping from cliffs; they perish due to the hardships of childbirth; they fall through a succession of perils and calamities;

they suffer the harm of malevolent poisons, insects, and snakes; they are dragged down by the curses of those with whom they have grudges; they lose their bodies to poverty and illness, or meet death during famines;
some fail to survive on boats or carts, while others perish when bridges or roads collapse; [and there are those who lose] their parents' capital...
Having abandoned their duties, they dwell in seclusion; separated from wives, children, and kin, they suffer in the darkness of misery.

My words are too few to be inscribed upon the horse’s tail, and my heart’s thoughts—who can convey them as light as a goose feather? Mists and dew lock the thousand mountains; smoke and clouds shroud the ten thousand waters.
Some, during times of chaos, are slain without cause in the midst of war, their bodies mangled; others encounter flooding floods and drift away, unaware of the abyss.
One dies prematurely, losing the integrity of loyalty and diligence, and becomes a member of a seditious faction. Wandering idly among others, one rarely meets a true connoisseur;
leaving home and squandering one’s livelihood, one seldom encounters those who look back with favor. Though food is fragrant when cooked in a deep village hearth, few hear of its savory taste;
when the songs and dances end upon the great earth, none obtain a drop of its grace. Suddenly, the limit of one's lifespan has been reached.
Upon his arrival, Jier Changquan suddenly departed. Amidst the clusters of red smartweed, the gulls and birds dwell; yet they cannot truly be called neighbors.
Beneath the green willows, dewdrops hang suspended like tears, increasing the falling rain. At night, people hear wailing and crying; in clear skies, who recognizes their tracks?
Because life persists, there is but empty pretense among friends; once the world has ended, there is utterly no trace of old acquaintances. Corpses lie strewn across the wilds.
Their bones are buried amidst the wild weeds; while alive, they pursued only fleeting pleasures, yet after death, they ultimately invite only suffering.
In foreign lands and distant realms, where waters are far and mountains remote, even their names and surnames are unknown—how then could they receive offerings on festival days?
For a thousand ages, the bright moon atop the mountain merely casts its light upon solitary souls; through the four seasons, the pure wind through the trees only stirs against their remains.

The resentful spirit, that night, briefly departed from the realm of darkness to attend the ritual altar. There, it received the teachings and words of the Buddhas and partook of the offerings presented with sincere devotion.
Thus, it was liberated from the deviant path and transcended to the pure realm of transformation, where it may now wander freely within the spheres of humans and devas.

Within the gateway of Prajñā, one should strive to bring matters to ultimate completion. Furthermore, there are those from all the realms of hell, drawn by the power of the sinful karma they created in the past;
they enter that iron city and embrace the copper pillars, amidst the dismal gloom of the Ash River and the freezing severity of the ice-filled trenches.
Though King Yama may not be partial, how could his jailers be free from cruelty? They drive one up the sword-tree and force one toward the fire-pit;
strength is exhausted in the flaming furnace and the spirit dissolves in the boiling cauldron. Because of what one created in the past, who can now take its place?

Arriving here in tens of thousands and hundreds of thousands, one departs for great kalpas and small kalpas, encountering the depths of misery and suffering through every hardship. Since such was one’s life...

They were known as close relatives, yet after death, there has been no news of them; their path to the underworld only increases our longing, and their presence in the human world is forever severed from our remembrance.

This night, relying on the compassionate light of the Buddha, they have come to this Dharma assembly. Furthermore, there is a multitude of beings from the realm of hungry ghosts; their retribution is even more pitiable.
Their facial bones are jagged and protruding, and their skeletal remains are broken and disjointed; when they encounter water, fire erupts from within their hearts.
Upon rising, smoke rises from his tongue whenever he encounters food. He dwells perpetually amidst filth and impurity, forever remaining beneath the realm of darkness.
Compared to the various ghostly realms, this is the most base and lowly. It is solely because of the delusion of the single mind that karma extends through the three periods of time.
The nine grades of superior, middling, and inferior are each distinct; the two paths of light and heavy karma result in diverse retributions.

We humbly pray that you will briefly leave the realm of the Ganges and hasten to this banquet of accumulated offerings. May those who are weary and emaciated bathe in the fragrant waters so that their appearance is suddenly transformed;
may they partake of the flavor of precious delicacies as the Dharma-food, casting hunger and thirst forever aside. This night, we take refuge in the Buddha.
Their majestic radiance hastens to attend this Dharma assembly. Furthermore, there are all those from the realm of animals—beings of various species drawn by the karmic debts of their transgressions.
Their hooves are pierced yet they are still sent to plow the clouds; their backs are raw with sores yet they are still driven to carry heavy loads.

Worms breed within their scales and shells; fire cauterizes their festering wounds. When they are to be slaughtered, their heads and horns are severed; when they are flayed, their feathers and fur fall away. Truly, by virtue of this...
Throughout many lifetimes and kalpas, through intentional and unintentional acts, my mouth failed to restrain itself from the four transgressions and my mind was ever imbued with the three poisons.
Having fallen into this net of karma as a beast, I range among the myriad species of fluttering birds in the heavens and the thousand swarms of crawling creatures on earth.
Whether swimming in deep pools, I still fear the net; whether dwelling in mountain forests, I yet remain anxious.

In this shooting and casting [of lot], whether it be a massive form or a minute shape, none shall be excluded. We pray that you may ascend the gate of non-obstruction and turn the light back upon itself to reflect;
hasten to this assembly tonight to return to the root and restore the source. This applies to all solitary spirits of the three paths, the six realms, and the five castes.
May all who do not obscure their true mind descend upon this Dharma assembly. The foregoing was the praise and invocation in the language of Tang; next follows the empowerment through secret mantras.
Now, I request the Tripitaka Master to ring the golden bell and empower the universal summoning. There is a *dhāraṇī* which says:

The assembly of five clans of *pīlī* spirits and orphaned souls, dwelling long in the dark paths and suffering from hunger and emaciation, now receive this vegetarian feast bestowed by the Buddha’s decree;
emerging briefly from the wheel of suffering, they give rise to joy. Namo Pūrvakalpatātaparyāya.
Oṃ sarvasattvān ākarṣaya svāhā. Having shaken the golden bell above, I summon you, the hosts of spirits.

Now, as you emerge from the hells and arrive here through the paths of karma, upon first hearing the sound of the gongs and cymbals, you will surely feel a sense of alarm and trepidation. I now request you three...
I shake the golden bell; through my empowerment, may you be freed from fear. There is a dhāraṇī which says:
(Gāthā) Having long dwelt in the hells and other realms of great suffering, Upon first hearing the joy of the Dharma, one might be terrified and alarmed.
But by the inconceivable power of the secret Yoga, One immediately attains peace and joins this Dharma assembly.
Oṃ cchokta cchokra cchokhre māhe cchokhre araje tārā svāhā. The Buddha regards sentient beings as if they were his own infant children.
Having already harbored such thoughts of compassion, how could he possibly lack a heart of protection?
Now I request the Tripitaka Master to ring the golden bell and, for your sake, bestow the empowerment of the *Sarvabuddhamaitrīrakṣā-dhāraṇī*.
It is said (in verse):
The Great Vows of Compassion of the Tathāgatas throughout the dust-motes of all lands, Perpetually extend skillful means to protect all sentient beings.
Proclaiming the secret and wondrous mantras, they enable all who hear them to partake in benefit and bliss.
Oṃ muccha mudri vara roca haṃ. This is the name of the Pure Land, the support of the Dharma-body and Reward-body;
it is called the Jewel Pavilion where humans and devas ascend, where colorful banners flutter and sway.
The incense shavings swirl in fragrant clouds. To ascend the jeweled pavilions and crystal towers, one must rely upon the sublime teachings of Vairocana.
Now, I request the Tripiṭaka Master to ring the golden bell and bestow empowerment upon this divine banner. The Dhāraṇī for Guiding the Way says:
(Gāthā) The precious towers and sacred pavilions are most high and vast; The colored banners flutter lightly in the glow of the lamps.
As soon as Vairocana expounded it, all the sages heard it;
it is that upon which those traveling the path above rely. Oṃ mūni dārimuṇaye tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddha-kūṭānām tadyathā oṃ kramaṃ kramaṃ sarvabhāvapadaṃ.
*Rājan maṃ niṣ sārvva svāhā*.
Having completed the consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of each of the aforementioned mantras, I now summon you, the hosts of spirits.

Now, you who have long dwelt in the realm of hungry ghosts (*preta-gati*), each possessing your own karmic retribution, have this night at this very hour descended here, sustained by the light from the Buddha’s ūrṇā-kośa.
The Site of Enlightenment. We accept these offerings out of concern that you have long been bound within the three miserable realms and that the field of your bodies is impure.
This evening, we have prepared fragrant water for you to bathe in, so as to purify the field of your bodies. We now wish to welcome you into this fragrant bath.
May the assembly reverently offer incense and flowers in invitation. (Recite) the Mantra for Transforming Robes.
Namo buddhāya. Namo dharmāya. Namo saṃghāya. (Recite three times. Namo buddhāya.
May you, from this very night until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi, vow to offer this body and mind to the Buddha as his constant disciples. May you never fall into the realm of hell.
Do you not see those within the realm of the hells? Having seen them, you must give rise to compassion. The ox-headed Dharma-wardens guard their physical forms;
grasping halberds and tridents, they are ever wrathful. They rush toward the mountains of blades and climb the trees of swords;
in a single day, they undergo thousands of deaths and births. Such bitter sufferings are of hundreds of thousands of kinds; only the Buddha alone can deliver them.

Namo dharmāya. May you all, from this very night until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi, vow to offer this body and mind to the Dharma and remain forever its disciples. May you never fall into the realm of hungry ghosts.
Have you not seen those within the realm of hungry ghosts? Having seen them, you must give rise to compassion. Their heads are like Mount Hua, their bellies like mountains;
their necks are as thin as needles, unable to hold even a drop of water. Driven by the winds of karma, they stand by the riverbanks;
when they wish to drink, the water turns into pus. Such are their myriad sufferings, numbering in the hundreds of thousands; only Bodhidharma can deliver them.

Namo Saṃghāya. May you, from this very night until the attainment of unsurpassed bodhi, vow to offer this body and mind to the Saṃgha to serve as their disciples forever. May you never fall into the realm of animals.
You have already seen those in the realm of animals; having seen them, you must give rise to compassion. Bearing saddles and wearing iron bits, they are ridden by men;
with horns upon their heads and hair upon their backs, they repay debts from former lives. Their hooves are pierced and their jaws are broken as they traverse long roads;
though they possess mouths, they never know how to speak. Such bitter sufferings are manifold, numbering in the hundreds and thousands; only Saṃghāya can deliver them.
(Chant: We take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
It is said that within the three realms, beings rise and fall; through the four modes of birth, they drift and wander. Some dwell in the realm of Yama, while others reside in the hells (*naraka*).
There they endure suffering eternally and are perpetually entangled in agony. They do not behold sweet nectar, nor do they encounter fine garments. This is all due to...
Due to the causes of unwholesome deeds, you have consequently invited the retribution of the ten evils.
Now I wish to welcome you all into the *dōjō* (place of practice) to receive offerings. However, having just left hell, your entire bodies are foul and rank;
the women lack sufficient clothing, and the men lack crowns and sashes. Since you are thus disarrayed and unfit for the company of the holy and wise, you must not be pressed forward.
This defiled body of Laṅkā shall immediately enter the pure assembly of the maṇḍala. Tonight, the patron of the feast has given rise to a vast and expansive mind;
he has established two bathing halls for men and women at this site, with two basins of fragrant water.

From within the general offerings, one set of garments each for men and women has been extracted. First, having performed the incense-offering and cremation before the bathing halls, dispatch the dhāraṇī-holders...

Purifying the Body. There is a dhāraṇī which says:

This concludes the proclamation of the holy names of the Seven Jewels Tathāgatas, including Amitābha Tathāgata. Hereafter, the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination shall also be expounded;
you should listen attentively. As for the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination, it is as follows: ignorance is the condition for...

Volitional formations arise. With volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise; with the six sense bases as condition, contact arises;

with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, clinging arises; with clinging as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises; and with birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise.

With the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease. With the cessation of volitional formations, consciousness ceases. With the cessation of consciousness, name-and-form ceases. With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense bases cease.
With the cessation of the six sense bases, contact ceases. With the cessation of contact, feeling ceases. With the cessation of feeling, craving ceases.

With the cessation of craving, grasping ceases. With the cessation of grasping, existence ceases. With the cessation of existence, birth ceases. With the cessation of birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and despair cease.
This is the Dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination. Now that you have heard it, you ought to bring it to ultimate realization.

Generally, food is used to sustain the body, while the Dharma-food nourishes the spirit. Now, as the offerings are arrayed with fragrant scents and the seats are assigned according to rank, how much more so when, through the power of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), the meager is transformed into abundance to become unimpeded Dharma-food?

May you all partake to your heart's content until fully satiated, giving rise to a mind of joy, harmonizing your roots of goodness, and refraining from mutual disturbance. I pray that all may receive this offering through universal compassion. Thereafter...
May each and every one of you give rise to the bodhicitta, leave behind all miserable realms of existence, and reach the fruit of Buddhahood from which there is never again regression.

Those who first attain the Way vow to deliver one another. Considering that blessings vary in quality, ranks differ in height, capacities for power are not the same, and their names are distinct, may you all partake of this food of the Dharma;
may it moisten the field of your bodies and inspire hearts of joy, so that you may obtain full satisfaction.

Abiding in impartial conduct, may you give rise to the bodhicitta and cultivate a spirit of mutual blessing and reception. May you obtain the benefits of the Buddha and the Sangha, and with mutual reverence, may each fulfill their own karmic conditions.

Exert yourselves with diligent cultivation and quickly attain liberation. (Next, the offering of burned paper money: Indeed, gathering and dispersing are impermanent;
coming and going have no fixed destination. Things meet when conditions are formed and part when their purpose is fulfilled. Like a whirling wind...
For the duration of this entire day, may the torrential rain not fall until the morning has passed. This evening, you shall ascend the path of the deities to attend this Dharma assembly;
there you shall partake of the fragrant offerings of the donors and listen to the esoteric words of the Tathāgata.
It is my hope that all you deities will give rise to diligence in your hearts, sever all doubt, emerge from the river of affliction and craving, and reach the further shore of Bodhi. Instantly—
Having clarified the ultimate truth and realized the Supreme Vehicle, you shall return to deliver all sentient beings, leading them equally to the path of enlightenment.
Now, as our stay has been long and our lingering here has been many, we pray that you will travel upon the true path and each return to your own abode. We prostrate to the various deities;
may you remain in good health. Then he spoke the *pansong* (farewell) *dhāraṇī*: 1. Oṃ mārajara-mukha-jiyau-muḥ.
