The Ritual Text for Scattering Flowers on Various Occasions of Buddhist Practice:

It is said that when the wind is calm and the whistling of the bamboos has ceased, and the constellations have shifted as the night deepens, this is precisely the time when the sages and worthies descend to look upon us, and when ordinary beings [should offer their prayers].

At the moment of surrendering in faith, the ritual site was as pure as ice, and fellow practitioners gathered like clouds. It was fitting to scatter celestial flowers and reverently present the Buddha-treasures.

As for these flowers: they were planted through roots of goodness and nurtured within the ground of the mind. Their growth did not depend on the warmth of spring, and their blooming and fading had no concern with the workings of nature.
Plucked from amidst a multitude of petals upon golden platters, their cold beauty was free from dust; they were cut from light silk—*xiǎnqiāo*.
From the tips of these jade-like fingers, a fragrant scent pervades the world; its artistry surpasses that of the earth and its subtlety eclipses the craftsmanship of heaven.
When Śakra scatters them, every leaf is *tathatā*; when Bodhidharma transmits them, every branch is *prajñā*.

Poets with clever minds cannot compose verses for them, and painters with skilled brushes find it difficult to capture them on paper. Now, as they are picked up at random from the hand, they may be scattered right here on the spot.
I offer this to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. May it universally sustain all the myriad spirits of heaven, earth, and water.
We now reverently pass the flower and recite the verse: Verse:
When spring arrives, the hundred flowers are called kings; After the rain, the eastern hedge is exceptionally fragrant.
Hidden in waxen hues by the cold, clear waters, It claims the autumn light within the moon of this Sahā world.
Once it bloomed in a thousand stems at Wuling, Now it unfolds ten-foot fragrance atop Mount Taihua.
A singular, numinous sprout, not of the Beiyuan variety, It comes entirely from this place to aid its propagation.
The security guards are exquisite beauties whose ingenuity rivals the works of Heaven; they have fashioned extraordinary flowers of diverse forms.
Now, before the Sage, they reverently present them as offerings, further praying for blessings, longevity, and eternal abundance.
A virtuous lady of exquisite skill has grasped the divine mystery; She has cut and fashioned fragrant blossoms with extraordinary artistry.
Holding them before the Buddha, she makes her most earnest plea: May she be granted an auspicious dream of the bear and the tiger.

Returning vows and reflecting on kindness, may all aspirations be fulfilled and the heart’s wishes perfected; Cutting the bonds of worldly ties and fashioning red silk, I offer this to the Dharma assembly;
May your compassion descend and accept me, so that from now on, blessings and prosperity may extend forever.
This flower that protects the fetus requires no planting or nurturing; Without rain and without wind, it blooms of its own accord.
I offer it to the Golden Immortal to seek blessings and merit, Praying that the womb and the fetus shall forever be free from calamity.
The Begging for Skill is a flower, neither false nor real; held in the palm of the hand, it is a springtime of another kind.
What vow is there in offering this to the Dharma King? The exquisite craftsmanship of the mind is entrusted to the person here.
In years of repenting for my hair, not even a single strand has changed according to my heart’s wish;
Deeply fearing the karmic causes encountered during my lifetime, I trim this extraordinary flower to seek purification. May these cloud-like tresses remain lush and ever-springing.

Prayers for sericulture and agriculture are the foremost priority in the world; To raise silkworms and achieve tenfold success in the harvest, one must rely on the power of the Buddhas through the offering of flowers.
May all be auspicious and as wished for—this is the essence of the silk thread.
The offerings for the deceased are neither peach nor plum, yet they are naturally fresh; their purity is like a lotus blooming amidst fire.
This night, at this very hour, I personally present them to the Buddha, praying that the lingering souls may be swiftly reborn in heaven.
This flower offered for the deceased is not like other flowers; Planted and nurtured within the mind-ground, it is a creation of the Great Artist.
Scattered toward humans and devas to assist the departed soul, May they be reborn early among the purple lotuses of the nine grades.
In former days, I reverently followed the Way and held flowers to offer to Dīpaṃkara; The fruit of unsurpassed Bodhi was spontaneously perfected.
This night, before the banquet, I personally presented them to the Buddha, Praying that I may quickly awaken to the nature within the sky of the mind.

Regarding this great causal nexus of the rite for releasing living beings, one must strictly avoid stirring up waves where there is no wind. How could the teachings of the Three Vehicles not serve to connect with sentient beings and benefit their lives?
They open the gate of the skillful means of all Buddhas and broaden the path of compassion throughout the three realms. At times they manifest as the lamp of the mind to dispel darkness.

In the darkness, may the rain of Dharma descend to moisten the parched and withered, capable of transforming the great earth into pure gold and enabling all sentient beings to attain perfect enlightenment.
I earnestly contemplate how even the black toads and earthworms wear the radiant halo upon their heads, and how the ants, mosquitoes, and insects bear the *svastika* upon their chests.

The various birds—doves, thrushes, and others—do not forfeit their status as the "Seven-Called" species; tortoises, turtles, snakes, and dragonflies all possess the potential for the Six Supernatural Powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).
Ten thousand devaputras were originally fish, and five thousand noble monks once belonged to the herd of deer. Bees and ants observe the righteousness of ruler and subject;
tigers and leopards share the benevolence of father and son. Even snails understand how to protect the scriptures, and even mynahs still know [the Dharma].

Recite the Buddha’s name. Therefore, a sutra says: "All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature. Furthermore, it is taught that even those currently in the realm of animals were once human beings in past kalpas.

Their minds were clouded and dull, their faculties were ignorant and crude; they did not believe in the precepts, concentration, and wisdom, and they constantly disparaged the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.
Buried within the four elements and six sense organs, they committed the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes. Relying on wealth and status...
They deceive the virtuous and good; they use their power and arrogance to suppress the lowly. When craving beauty, they falsely display their elegance;
when addicted to wine, they act with unrestrained contempt. Seeing another's property, they strive to claim it as their own; killing living beings, they pray for long life.
Whether incurring debts of life or wealth, or engaging in false speech and frivolous talk, their curses are as venomous as swords and blades, and their practice of jealousy is such that—

Harmful as jackals and wolves, they deceive the sages and the worthy while flatter the superiors and prey upon the subordinates. They see only the pleasures before their eyes, yet how could they know of their own future sinking into misery?
When the meager merit of a single lifetime suddenly ends, the karmic conditions of former days follow immediately.

Only after long kalpas have one finally left the hells, yet this time one loses the human body, being reborn either with feathers and wings, or clad in scales and shells, or else born by transformation.
Whether dwelling in moonlit groves, misty ridges, or being governed by the Dragon Courts of the Water Realm, you offer your flesh to sustain others and repay your debts with your very lives.
While alive, you are subjected to hacking and chopping, cast upon the butcher’s block; to undergo such calamity is truly pitiable.
On this day, [Name] humbly acts on behalf of [Matter], mindful that you, a creature of this kind, are about to be led to the place of execution. He does not begrudge his family wealth to ransom you.
I command you to release them so they may return; let them then reform their past ways and cultivate themselves for the future.

I shall further extol them, granting them full liberty to transcend birth and escape death, transforming the cauldrons of boiling water and flames into a realm of cool serenity, and shifting the ovens of roasting and steaming into a land of peace and joy.
May they abandon the four modes of birth to realize non-arising, and leave the six realms of existence to return to the Great Way. Furthermore, I fear that once you have lost this human body...
The stage of the nature-ground (dharmatā-bhūmi) is difficult to clarify. Upon first hearing the great names of the Triple Gem, one may fearfully experience a single-minded alarm.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the *Dhāraṇī for Eliminating Fear*. I shall recite it for you. You spirits of various kinds, listen with a focused mind;
listen and receive it with a focused mind.
Namo khakite khara-khaki-lu hali mahālu-hali arada ra-cara-saha (three times).
The recitation of the mantra for being free from fear is now complete.
Visualize that you are freed from all fears and have attained right concentration.
Mind. Now, for the sake of requesting the Buddha to act as our great witness, you all should with sincere resolve together give rise to a mind of refuge and orientation.
(Chant: Disciples [Name] and others, together with those present at this ritual site, prostrate themselves in humble salutation.
Thus, I have finished respectfully requesting all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to act as great witnesses for you.

Furthermore, I shall now perform repentance on behalf of you, all sentient beings, for the defilements of sins from many lifetimes and the grievances and transgressions accumulated over many kalpas. Now, as for repentance:
it is to serve as parents for others, as eyes for others, and as guides for others. One must not dare to conceal the karmic offenses already committed, nor [the ones yet to be committed].

Repent your transgressions and do not commit them again. All you spirits and beings of the six realms, the gates to which are deep and the paths to the three miserable destinies are far, have fortunately encountered this holy assembly and joyfully met with virtuous conditions.
As soon as you hear this proclaimed before the Buddha, you should listen with an open heart; abandon all frivolous discourse and sever your perverse thoughts.
Each of you should vow to take refuge and seek swift liberation. If you let this night pass by, it will be lost for all future days.
It is difficult to encounter. You may take refuge with sincere devotion and listen with a focused mind.
(Chant: All classes of spirits and those assembled at this ritual site, from time immemorial until this present life—
From the time of this present life until this very night, I have committed unwholesome deeds of body—killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct;
unwholesome deeds of speech—slander and false speech; and unwholesome deeds of mind—covetousness, anger, and wrong views.

I have consumed alcohol and meat, distressed and disturbed sentient beings, lacked faith in the Buddhist scriptures, failed to be filial toward my parents, and did not give rise to compassion or practice skillful means. My own...
I have committed such offenses as performing [evil deeds], inciting others to do so, and rejoicing in seeing or hearing them performed. These and other transgressions are immeasurable and boundless.
This very night, at this very moment, before the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, I openly confess and repent. May all sins be extinguished. (Recite three times.)
The confession for you all has now been completed. I shall further recite for you the Dharani for the Definitive Destruction of Evil Karma;
listen with a focused mind and receive it with a focused mind.
Oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya sarvagrahabhūtān satyena samaye hūṃ (three times).
The above recitation of the *Dhāraṇī for the Definitive Destruction of Evil Karma* for the sake of all classes of spirits and beings is hereby completed. All.
I consider that you may still have karmic enemies; because your bonds of karma are firm and you have not yet attained liberation, you have incurred this retribution.
According to my Buddha, the Tathāgata, there is the *Vairaṇirghātana-dhāraṇī* (Dhāraṇī for Resolving Karmic Knots and Hostilities). I shall now recite it for you.
You should listen with a sincere mind and receive it with a sincere mind.
Oṃ samtrā khatrā svāhā. The recitation of the *Dhāraṇī for Untying the Knots of Enmity* for you, all you classes of spirits and beings, is now complete.
Furthermore, there is the *Dhāraṇī for Purifying the Three Karmas*. I shall now recite it for you; join your palms and listen with a sincere mind and focused attention.
Listen with a sincere heart. Sarva bhāṣitum sarva dharmāḥ sarva bhāṣitum haṃ.

This is the first time it has been proclaimed. There is a second time as well; you should join your palms and listen with a sincere mind, receiving [the teaching] with a sincere mind (the mantra is the same as before).
This is the second time it has been proclaimed. When the sound ceases at the third repetition, it is precisely when you turn your backs on awakening and unite with the sensory dust;
at that moment, you should listen with a sincere heart and receive it with a sincere heart. (The mantra is the same as before.)
This is the third time this has been proclaimed. Upon hearing the sound of this mantra, you shall immediately perceive the elimination of karma and the purification of the mind;
you shall behold your original face and awaken to the Supreme Vehicle (Upari-yāna). Now, for your sake, I shall further utter the Four Great Vows.
All Bodhisattvas have realized their minds through these, and the Tathāgatas of the ten directions have attained Buddhahood through them. You should resolve [to follow them].
Listen attentively with a focused mind and receive this teaching.
(Chant: I vow to sever the boundless afflictions; I vow to deliver the boundless sentient beings;
I vow to study the boundless Dharma-gates; I vow to realize the boundless Buddha-way.
I have now finished reciting the Four Great Vows for you, all you classes of spirits and beings.
According to the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*, the Elder’s Son Jalavāhana preached the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination to ten thousand fish;
thereafter, he invoked the name of the Tathāgata Ratnaśrī. Those ten thousand fish died on that very same day and were reborn in a celestial palace. For the sake of these ten...
The benefit for the thousand devaputras is not small; I shall now proclaim it for you as well. Listen with a focused mind, listen with a focused mind and receive it:

ignorance conditions volitional formations; volitional formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form; name-and-form conditions the six sense bases; the six sense bases condition...
Contact. Conditioned by contact is feeling. Conditioned by feeling is craving. Conditioned by craving is clinging. Conditioned by clinging is existence. Conditioned by existence is birth.

Conditioned by birth arise old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and despair. With the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease. With the cessation of volitional formations, consciousness ceases.
With the cessation of consciousness, name-and-form ceases. With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense bases cease. With the cessation of the six sense bases, contact ceases. Contact ceases...
Feeling ceases. With the cessation of feeling, craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases. With the cessation of clinging, existence ceases.
With the cessation of existence, birth ceases. With the cessation of birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and despair cease.
This is the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination. Now, for your sake, I shall further proclaim the names of the Tathāgatas of the Seven Jewels.
You should listen with a focused mind and receive it with a focused mind.
(Namo) Homage to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna; Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava;
Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇa; Homage to the Tathāgata Vipulakāya;
Homage to the Tathāgata Abhayadatta; Homage to the Tathāgata Amṛtāgrarāja.
Namo Amitābha Tathāgata (recite each three times).
Thus far, for the sake of you various classes of spirits and beings, I have recited the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination as well as the names of the Seven Jewel Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, there are the names of the Triple Gem which are difficult to encounter and difficult to hear; were they but once to pass through the faculty of hearing...
The sins as numerous as the sands of the Ganges shall be extinguished. You should listen with a sincere mind and receive this teaching with a sincere mind.
(Chant: Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namo Saṃghāya (three times each).
I have just now proclaimed "Buddhāya" for you, all you spirits and others, repeatedly declaring that this is the Buddha;

once it enters your ears, you shall not fall into the realm of hell-beings. I have proclaimed "Dharmāya," which is the Dharma; once it enters your ears, you shall not fall into the realm of hungry ghosts.
I have proclaimed "Saṃghāya," which is the Saṃgha; once it enters your ears, you shall not fall into the realm of animals.
(Chant: I take refuge in the Buddha, the Unsurpassed Honored One; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One Free from Desire;
I take refuge in the Sangha, the Honored One Among the Multitude. (Recite each verse three times.
From this day forward, I shall call upon the Buddha as my teacher, call upon the Dharma as my teacher, and call upon the Sangha as my teacher. Never again shall I take refuge in anything else.
Māras and heterodox teachers, we only pray that the Tathāgata will accept and protect us out of compassion (recite three times).
(Chant: Having completed the taking of refuge in the Buddha; having completed the taking of refuge in the Dharma; having completed the taking of refuge in the Saṅgha (each recited three times).
Thus far, for you various classes of spirits and beings, I have proclaimed the names of the Triple Gem; this constitutes the precept of the Three Refuges.
Furthermore, there is the Samaya Precept. This precept has been taught by all Buddhas of the past, will be taught by all Buddhas of the future, and is now being taught by all Buddhas of the present.
Its merit is immeasurable and inconceivable; a single hearing of it through the faculty of the ear extinguishes sins as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
You should listen with a sincere mind and receive it with a sincere mind.

Oṃ samaya-sattva (three times). Thus far, for you spirits and others, we have requested the Buddhas to bear witness, repented of the roots of transgression, made the Four Great Vows, and received the Three Refuges and Precepts.
May these precepts be fully perfected; may each of you vow to transcend the physical body of saṃsāra and suddenly awaken to the Dharma-body. [Karma and its fruits...]

They shall instead attain the fruit of Buddhahood; they will forever be liberated from the three miserable realms and remain far removed from the six paths of existence. They will clearly understand the ancestral style of the Ultimate Vehicle and realize the *anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*.
Together with the assembly at the site of enlightenment, they shall all obtain the True Cause, and with their minds pervading the Dharma-realm, they shall ascend together to Perfect Awakening.
Dwelling in the world like empty space, Like a lotus flower unsullied by water,
With a mind pure and transcending all, I bow my head in homage to the Unsurpassed Honored One.
*Text for Dispatching the Boat (Rite for Sending Off the Deities of the Plague Division)*
I look up and address the Sage of the Celestial Capital: the numinous efficacy of the Epidemic Division is manifold and its sovereign authority vast. The hosts of ghosts assemble in great numbers;
the Epidemic Soldiers receive the talismans of the Purple Microcosm Golden Gate and uphold the edicts of the Most High Jade Sovereign.

They traverse the world to inspect human affairs, extirpating evil intentions and manifesting virtuous deeds. They spread their majestic wind so that the pestilence winds blow fiercely, shifting between joy and wrath.
In a mere moment, he fans forth a murderous aura and a fierce, virulent stench rises and falls within a single instant. His spiritual powers are responsive;
his transformations are inexhaustible. He manifests a thousand forms and assumes a hundredfold moods:

when encountering a man of good character, he joins his palms and raises his fists in greeting, bestowing auspiciousness and blessings; when meeting one with an evil heart, he gives rise to resentment and wrath, raining down calamities and misfortunes.

Disaster. We humbly pray that Your Majesty shall mount the jade carriage and stride with divine majesty upon the pearl-ornamented altar. Unfurling the crimson banners, may you lead the pestilence-soldiers from behind;
grasping white blades, may you station the fierce generals in front. May you transform pestilential vapors into auspicious mists and convert pestilential winds into propitious breezes.
In accordance with the bequeathed words of our Buddha, may all attend this dharma assembly on this auspicious night. With sincere devotion, the lay devotee presents this offering. I.
The second circuit of divine wine: human flowers and fruits express worldly earnestness; the Dharma-food and silver coins display the precious regard of ordinary sentiments.
The second circuit of divine wine is presented. The droplets of a commoner’s outflows may be measured, yet the divine sages are unfathomable;

with the dull eyes of ignorance, it is difficult to expect satiety. The third circuit of divine wine is presented. With single-minded prayer and entreaty, the three prostrations are concluded. At this point—
On this very day, [Name] has cultivated a sublime assembly and prepared a dharma feast. He has specially provided a flower boat to present a ceremonial offering.
This vessel was constructed by master craftsmen and adorned with exquisite artistry; it is a phoenix galley and dragon boat, featuring a tiger’s head and a leopard’s tail.

Within, it carries a thousand years' worth of provisions; without, it spreads across ten thousand qing of surging waves. One may roam at will across the four seas and reach the five lakes according to one's heart’s desire.
By bestowing grace and conferring blessings, misfortune is transformed into auspiciousness; through protection and the granting of rest, calamity is changed into good fortune.
Epidemics are gathered in and poisons are withdrawn, all ascending upon the dragon boat. As the drums beat and the banners unfurl, each returns to its original path.
(Chant: The Great Sage, Bodhisattva Huanxizang. (Verse:
The ghost-kings and their retinues patrol the five directions; A hundred monsters and spirits bring calamity and demonic affliction.
Incense seals lead and welcome the assembly of worthy spirits; Flower-boats ferry across the oars of the gods of decay.
Red banners flash along with the river waves; Painted drums resound in harmony with the ocean tides.
The Sage gathers in pestilence and collects all toxins; The young men ply their oars in total freedom.

Chapter on the Vows of Various Families.

We pray that the sacred source of the imperial lineage may expand its blessings, and that the precious reign may prolong its prosperity. May the common people forever rejoice in the era of Yao, and may all within the realm always behold the sun of Shun.
Furthermore, the imperial wind sweeps vast and far-reaching; the sovereign way is lofty and majestic. The myriad regions sing of eternal years, and the four seas pray for boundless longevity.
Furthermore, may the Venerable One surely attain renown; may the Venerable One surely attain long life. May you forever accord with the endurance of earth and heaven:
eight thousand years as spring, and eight thousand years as autumn. How many times shall the rivers clear and the seas be tranquil?
Furthermore, he has eternally governed the Golden Wheel and constantly regulated the Jade Candle; his Way transcends that of the Three Augusts, and his merit surpasses that of the Five Emperors.
Moreover—
The Emperor’s life-span is as vast as Heaven; he wields the sovereign authority of supreme honor and prosperity. His reign extends ever further, and he enjoys the blessings of tranquility and peace.
Officials...
May these vast crags forever assist the longevity of the Southern Mountains; may the two tiers of the Taijie forever support the majesty of the Northern Pole.
We further pray that you shall become an immortal for a thousand years and remain a venerable elder at the three courts throughout eternity.

Furthermore, they tread upon jade and ascend the golden throne; holding the balance and occupying the central axis, they assist the Son of Heaven during an era of Great Peace and bring stability to the people throughout the realm.
Moreover,
As a high minister holding the central axis of government and as a senior official directly governing the people, you serve as a model of virtue for those above and a protector for the people below.

Your imperial favor increases ever more, never ceasing as you maintain the responsibility of the balance of state. With imperial edicts frequently descending, we await your promotion to the essential offices of the pivot of power.
Furthermore, as the constellation Tai (Jupiter) shines directly upon him, his blessed ground becomes even more profound. At the Ministry of Personnel, he is selected for his eminent reputation;
at the Board of Civil Office, he is honored with an appointment to a vacant post. He celebrates the joy of his parents, and his fame spreads far throughout the Three Dynasties.
Furthermore,

as his official standing grew increasingly prominent and his rank and emolument shifted upward with the times, he responded above to the grace bestowed by the Purple Emperor’s appointment and consoled below the expectations of all who looked up to him among the common people.
Furthermore,

having already been bathed in imperial grace, you have newly ascended the official registers. May you always act as parents to these people, and quickly become a pillar of support for the superior state.

Furthermore, the constellation of the Terrace shines brightly, and his rank and position have been honorably advanced. Looking upward, he receives the grace of the Holy Sovereign; looking downward, he satisfies the hopes of the common people.
Moreover,

May your lifespan be extended for all eternity, and may you enjoy blessings without end. With purple ribbons and golden fish insignia, may you always rejoice in companionship at the same brow, never aging;
with green robes and wooden tablets, we await the sight of them filling our eyes in orderly rows.

The civil officials and scholars are graced by the auspicious light of the stars; the constellation Kui shines its brilliance upon them. Those from humble dwellings exert themselves, seeing the day they achieve fame in a single examination;
they stride across the vast blue clouds while their parents are still in the prime of life.

Furthermore, his literary compositions have already achieved perfection in seven steps, and his learning is as vast as that accumulated over three winters. Under the autumn wind, the cassia blossoms shall soon be seen alongside him as he is recommended by the "eagle" (the imperial examination);
under the spring waves, the peach blossoms await as we look forward to his soaring high through the Dragon Gate.

Furthermore, the Star of Destiny shines directly upon you, and auspicious fortune descends. Within your breast lies the richness of embroidered brocade; from your brush flow characters like dragons and serpents.
In the examination halls, you rely on the assistance of the divine; your name shall be inscribed as high as the sun and moon.
Furthermore,

his literary style towers ten thousand feet high, and his brush sweeps away thousands of troops. Having already donned the indigo robe to honor his person, he now adds luster to his native village by wearing the brocade robes of official rank.

Furthermore, this mountain and these rivers concentrate spiritual essence; the Dipper and the Ladle harbor refined excellence. This year in the autumn examinations, his name was early recommended to the local lords;
next year at the Imperial Academy, he shall have his name inscribed high upon the "Swan Tower" in the capital.
Furthermore,

having achieved victory at the thorny gates of the examination hall and registered one's name upon the orchid tablets of the provincial academy, the eagle and falcon leave the dust and wind to spread their wings and display their prowess;
the dragon and serpent obtain the clouds and rain to make their horns and head protrude with majestic loftiness.
The Sangha secretly transmits the seal of the mind, continuing the ancestral lamp above, so that karmic obstructions may be extinguished in their time and the sprouts of goodness may grow daily,
acting as the eyes and ears of devas and humans, and forever serving as the pillars and beams of the Buddha-dharma.

Furthermore, may his roots of goodness increase, may demonic obstacles be eliminated, and may he master all the tenets and doctrines of our school. May he cultivate both merit and wisdom to become complete,
serving as the presiding spirit of the Dharma-gate and the pillar of the Brahma-realm.
Furthermore,

his physical body is firm and solid, and his eye of the Way is perfectly clear and bright; he constantly forms causes for joy throughout the ten directions and forever transcends the path of saṃsāra through ten thousand kalpas.
Furthermore, the ocean of his compassionate mind is vast, and the mountain of his Dharma-life is lofty. He rows the vessel of Prajñā and serves as the eyes for humans and devas.
Moreover,
Beneath his *kāṣāya*, he constantly cultivated the causes of purity; within the seal of virtue, he forever bore the grace of the Lord of Compassion.
Thus, the tradition of our school flourished ever more, and the moon of the precepts shone with increasing brilliance.
The foundation of the Way is firm; the temple of contemplation flourishes. The mind-transmission is subtle and spontaneous; the realization of the profound truth is clear and unclouded.
Furthermore,

with their fundamental natures and faculties pure and serene, they have perfected the fruits of the Way; they shall forever serve as the steps for crossing the sea of suffering and eternally act as the beams and pillars of the Dharma-gate.

Furthermore, as he attained sudden enlightenment into the profound mystery, his merit and virtue grew ever more sublime. By day, he soared like a phoenix or a crane, his power of the Way pure and lofty;
by night, he walked among the Dipper and Ox constellations, his nature-sky clear and transparent.

The husband tills the soil and the wife carries provisions; they sow in spring and weed in summer. They have no anxiety over drought or flooding, and enjoy the blessing of millet, grain, rice, and broomcorn millet.

Furthermore, they begin their labor in the east at the start of spring and look toward the harvest in the west at its conclusion; thus, no household worries about supporting eight members, and every door has the accumulation of a thousand granaries.
Moreover—

On the eastern ridges, the land is ploughed and broken; on the southern fields, the weeds are weeded and the seedlings tended. Pestilence and vermin are secretly eliminated, and rain and sunshine arrive according to the seasons.
Grains, millet, mulberry, and hemp flourish in abundance; cattle, sheep, chickens, and dogs multiply and spread.
His craftsmanship was as marvelous as the ingenuity of Heaven; his mental artistry was lofty and brilliant. His skill was uniquely unrivaled, and his learning ranked foremost among all.
Early on, he awaited the summons of the Celestial Edict and was graced by the benevolence of the Sage King.

Furthermore, his mental ingenuity fashioned marvels, and his manual arts were thoroughly mastered. Within his breast lay extraordinary and ingenious designs; upon the palms of his hands, he could manipulate the very workings of creation.
He constantly received the honored summons of high officials and enjoyed the radiant grace of the Emperor himself.

Merchants traveling between the provinces and capitals, sojourning in the imperial city, have no fear of bandits when journeying by land, nor do they face the perils of wind and waves when transporting goods by water.
May the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava assist their movements, and may the youth Jambhala protect their travels and storehouses.
Furthermore,

there is a proper way to generate wealth, and one’s subtle calculations leave nothing to chance. Why trouble yourself by repeatedly monopolizing the market, merely to see your own gateways turn into bustling markets?
Furthermore, it is convenient for commerce and trade is abundant. Whether by water transport or overland travel, one is spared the perils of treacherous precipices and wind and waves;
with pearls in abundance and jade piled high, there is no fear of housebreaking or banditry.

Public officials shall find peace and prosperity in the public halls; private residences shall be tranquil and secure. Those who serve as officers shall constantly obtain blessings and auspiciousness; those who act as administrators shall be free from all faults.
Noble persons shall provide protection, and the family way shall flourish and prosper.

Furthermore, auspicious stars shall shine upon them, and noble officials shall provide support. By serving the public, public affairs will be harmonious; by serving their superiors, the calamities of office shall be utterly extinguished.

The physician’s merit in saving the multitude is profound; his benefit in bringing life to others is vast. His surgical blade achieves the efficacy of a "ten-in-ten" success; his medical prescriptions transmit the excellence of three generations.
May the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja protect his practice and storehouse, and may the King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel assist his application.

Furthermore, the physicians claim that their mastery of medicine and the efficacy of their arts and practices— which achieve the merit of rescuing the precarious and restoring the ruined, and obtain the effect of bringing the dead back to life—
are entirely dependent upon the power of the Buddha and the great bestowal of his hidden grace (*guṇa*). This enables every person to dwell in a land of peace and joy, and causes those who are...
To ascend to the realm of health and tranquility,

the practitioner of arts and techniques attains spiritual communion. Through strategic planning and the pursuit of one's intent, they manipulate the stalks and arrange the symbols to discern good fortune, misfortune, regret, and caution before the signs have even manifested.
Previously, he cast stalks and tossed tortoise shells to divine fortune, misfortune, calamity, and auspiciousness regarding the future; furthermore,
his mastery of stellar destiny moved the high officials with his art, determining life and death without error and establishing standards for good and ill fortune.
Relying upon the Buddha’s grace, may the practice of the Way further flourish. May the star-fated destiny and the gates of sorcery and divination remain tranquil;
may the Dharma teachings spread, and with the protection of the shadowy armies, may there be daily peace and stability, sustained by divine power.
By maintaining this, one will experience constant peace and well-being from time to time.

Furthermore, the Dharma-gate will flourish, and the master’s arts will attain spiritual efficacy. Where divine talismans and seals are placed, malevolent spirits and demons will be struck with dread, and the dharma registers shall be opened.
At that time, demons and malevolent spirits vanished from sight. Though this was attributed to supernatural power, it was in truth due to the Buddha’s majesty.

The physical bodies of the masters and nuns became firm and stable; their observance of the precepts was upright and dignified. They cultivated the fruits of longevity through roots of goodness and caused the flowers of enlightenment to bloom within the ground of their hearts.
Avalokiteśvara bestows his protection; the Queen Mother of the West grants you equal years.

May the red complexion of the aged remain forever, never to be invaded by white hair. May the Jade Terrace record your age as one difficult to grow old, and may the Purple Registry inscribe your longevity.
His character is like this.

Furthermore, his body is like a mountain, firmly established and enduring; his longevity is equal to that of the Chinese parasol tree and the pine, remaining unchanged through the severest cold. His years and virtue—

The lineage is noble and flourishing; their descendants are numerous. Relying upon the protection of divine beings and sustained by the blessings of the dragons and devas, Mount Longevity remains firm and secure, lofty yet never in peril.
The ocean of merit is vast and deep, becoming ever more fathomless the more one probes it. May their long, white eyebrows endure for eternity.
She is an immortal of the Penglai and Fuzhou islands, difficult to age; with hair as white as cranes, she has long served as an elder in this sagely world’s era of great peace.
Her role as a matron is clearly manifest, and she constantly observes the way of a wife. Her face is like a peach in the second month, and her brows rival the willows of the third spring.
In longevity, she rivals Magu; in age, she equals the Queen Mother of the West.
Furthermore, her celestial nature is pure and tranquil, and her mind is harmonious and gentle. May the Queen Mother’s peaches of immortality grant her eternal life for a thousand autumns. O Guanyin!
The willows sweep away the calamities of the four seasons.

The life-force of the child is made firm; their natural disposition is intelligent and clear. Their nourishment and food are harmoniously regulated; malevolent spirits are forever eradicated. From childhood, they are cherished like a pearl in the palm.
This is a rare auspicious omen, bringing great honor to the national treasure.
Furthermore, there is peace and security by day, and no cause for alarm or fear at night. His youthful nature is easily nurtured, and his innate disposition is blessed with great intelligence.
Within the palace, the two attendants have constantly received secret blessings; the fifteen kinds of ghosts mentioned in the sutra shall never again cause harm.

Furthermore, the child has been pure and auspicious, with milk and food being well-balanced. The Treasury of Conduct is protected by the youth Sudhana, and auspiciousness descends from the Tathāgata Śrī.
May there be blessings and protection. May it bring benefit and prosperity to your parents, bringing glory to your lineage and causing the Way of every household to flourish ever more.
May the family reputation grow ever more eminent, so that the fragrance of the orchids and lilies upon the steps of the Xie family shall be perpetually diffused. Confucius...
In his household, the teachings of the Odes and Rites were grandly propagated through his influence;
furthermore, his family shared in the auspiciousness of the Duke, inheriting the glory of the Shi clan. Year after year, their crops and silkworms yielded full harvests, and their livestock thrived.

Advancing in merit month after month, both public and private affairs were guided toward auspiciousness; waterways and land routes flourished with success. At the gate, the sound of bustling activity resounded;
among one’s offspring, the reputation for excellence spread far and wide.

Furthermore, the thunder shall deliver blessings from the Five Heavens, and the lightning shall drive away the calamities of the nine untimely deaths. A life-span of a thousand fathoms shall tower over heaven and earth;

a single stream of merit shall extend through the sun and moon. Within the station of husband and wife, there shall forever be no fear of mutual harm or suppression; within the position of children and descendants—
May you always preserve the celebration of family unity.

We pray for your longevity, equal to Mount Tai in its stability, and your blessings, as vast as the ocean. May you sing the poem of the Southern Mountain that never falters, and chant the verses of the Pan Water that defy aging.

This hymn further proclaims that longevity and auspiciousness are bestowed by Heaven, and merit and virtue flourish daily. May the golden script of the precious talisman eternally inscribe the characters for long life upon the Isle of the Immortals (Yingzhou).
May the flourishing years of Penglai Island extend forever;
may the span of your life be as immeasurable and boundless as the sands of the Ganges; and may the foundation of your merit be as firm as the foundation of heaven and earth.
It has become increasingly firm. We look up to the Imperial Enlightenment for a great bestowal of vast blessings.

May prayers for felicity lead to ever-present tranquility and brilliance; having attained such abundance and prosperity, may our gates welcome the auspiciousness of the *jianjian* (simple and pure) and our households receive the continuous flow of the *mianmian* (unending).
The harvests were abundant, and there was ample illumination. Nothing was unsuitable.
Furthermore, auspiciousness gathered in profusion, and pestilence vanished in secret. Every undertaking accorded with one’s heart, and every movement unfolded in a thousand ways.
Your wishes have been fulfilled.

Furthermore, a thousand auspicious signs converge like clouds, and a hundred blessings increase like a river. May your mountain of longevity be as high as Mount Hua, and your ocean of merit equal the vastness of the deep blue sea.
Its depths are profound.

Furthermore, among the five blessings, the first is longevity. With a thousand granaries and ten thousand wagons, the splendor of the Xu and Shi families spreads its influence like a fragrant breeze, drawing all toward it.
The noble mansions of the Jia family—once the wealth and glory of the Jin and Zhang clans—dissolve into a thousand gates through the power of the Buddha.

Averting calamities brings forth blessings like rising clouds; disasters are swept away like lightning. Whether entering or departing, one attains the great harmony of earth and heaven; whether active or retired, there is no obstruction from mountain or river.

The darkness of ignorance is dispelled; fire and thieves are both extinguished. Both public and private interests are benefited. Once the vow-mind has been revealed, the sacred intention shall be maintained.

Furthermore, celestial calamities and terrestrial misfortunes shall not reach their person; the lunar afflictions and annual declines shall not strike their life-force. As for those fateful portents of misfortune—

It transforms misfortune into good fortune; it changes the dimness of the stars into brilliance. When one moves, the multitude of sages provide support; when one dwells at rest, the myriad spirits offer protection.
There is celebration amidst the shifts of cold and warmth, and one gazes upon their own conduct with no cause for anxiety.

Furthermore, at that time, the Way was clear and the realm was peaceful; the state was prosperous and the people were at ease. The three luminaries were complete, the cold and heat were balanced, the five grains ripened, and the populace flourished.
Everywhere there was the joy of ascending the terraces, and every person indulged in the leisurely wandering of drumming their full bellies. Merchants stored their wares in the markets...
Things are abundant and wealth is plentiful; scholars cultivate culture, achieving merit and fulfilling their ambitions. May travelers and artisans prosper and flourish.
Men till the fields and women tend the mulberry trees, so that there is surplus grain and surplus cloth. Prisoners shall find eternal rest, and pestilence shall vanish entirely.
Fire and bandits remain hidden; villages and neighborhoods enjoy tranquility. (The universal wish of the four classes of people:

May all who receive this protection be free from illness, ensuring their well-being and peace. May the hundred parts of the body be spared the fear of withering, and may the four elements attain lightness and ease.

Its joy is such that taking medicine is like the flavor of pouring *amṛta* (clarified butter) over one’s tongue; eating and drinking is like the bliss of *dhyāna* and celestial delicacies. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, there is no obstruction or anxiety;
in every movement, whether entering or leaving, rising or resting, one is always peaceful and always joyful.

Furthermore, as the sun of wisdom shines its light, the clouds of calamity dissolve and roll away. Auspicious luminaries assist our every movement and repose, while malefic stars leave no stain upon our conduct or concealment.
Moreover, we rely on Avalokiteśvara, Savior from Suffering, to clear away all miseries, and depend upon the Bodhisattva Who Eliminates Calamities to forever sweep them clean.
Other calamities shall cease.

Furthermore, chronic illnesses will depart from the body; auspicious luminaries will preside over the palaces; destiny and fortune will be enjoyed, and the vital breaths and the horse-energies will naturally harmonize; the stars and constellations will move in accordance with the seasons.
The dragon of the body becomes ever more vigorous. The Buddha bestows the sword of wisdom to excise the source of illness; the Sage grants the divine elixir to eliminate suffering and affliction.
The tree of life soars with its verdant hue; the mountain of longevity increases its towering peaks.

Furthermore, at times when calamities have been extinguished and dispersed, and the lunar afflictions have been cleared away; when malevolent stars recede and auspicious stars arrive, when baleful vapors vanish and harmonious energy gathers;
when the Medicine King Bodhisattva balances the five viscera with his medicines to bring peace, and the Poison-Averting Vajra dispels a hundred poisons—
Though situated in impurity, it is pure;
the precious pearl within the womb has not yet emerged, and the five petals hold their fragrance. Fearing that the month of birth is approaching, one relies upon the holy sages for protection.
On the day of birth, it was as if wandering through a garden of joy; at the time of sitting upon the grass, it was like climbing a tree of sorrowlessness (*aśoka*).

Furthermore, ten months were spent in lightness and ease, and one hour was protected without difficulty. The birth was supervised by the Holy Mother, who internally dispelled [obstacles] and partially relieved [the burden].

May the transgressions [of this child] be cleared away. May the protective spirits of the newborn bestow great blessings of auspiciousness. With the dream of the bear and the cubs harmonized, and the solitary arrow displayed at the gate, may the omen of the early birth of a male child be realized.
May he succeed as a descendant who carries on the ancestral tradition.

The silkworms were protected so that the spring cocoons ripened in great abundance; the summer silk was double its usual yield. When the silk was reeled, it became snow-white threads; the fields of Han could not rival the quantity of cocoons produced.
As for the cutting and sewing of spring garments, who among those of the Zhou could sing of "having no clothes"?

Furthermore, the cocoons are as bright as frost and the silk is piled like mountains. The Bodhisattva Ma-ming (Aśvaghoṣa) can transform the few into many, and the King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra-rāja) can manifest existence from non-existence.
There shall not be even a hair’s breadth of loss; we pray that ten times the amount may be fully harvested.
The seedlings are protected once the fields have been sown; the crops flourish just as they emerge. There is no longer fear of drought or flooding, nor the harm of weeds or locusts.
The people of the lower realm perceive the omen of the dreaming fish, while the heavens respond with the auspicious sign of the inverted Dipper.
Furthermore, the rice seedlings grow in competition, while weeds and tares do not arise; there is no anxiety regarding floods or droughts, and locusts and moths are forever stilled.

Since the commencement of spring cultivation, the green waves across the thousand villages have reached the heavens; soon we shall see the harvest of autumn, when yellow clouds of grain will densely cover the earth for ten thousand acres. In every household—
With the joy of filling granaries, people sing songs of contentment like those who beat the earth with wooden blocks;
cattle and sheep are well-nourished and robust, while dogs and swine multiply and flourish. There is no longer any fear of pestilence, and the scourge of theft and robbery is forever severed.
Furthermore, the five mother hens and two mother pigs did not miss their breeding seasons; the three dogs and four sheep each fulfilled their natures.
Thus, all living beings multiplied and flourished, and every creature thrived in abundance.
When the ox is kept, it is released in the morning at the Peach Forest; by day it grazes on the grasslands. When crossing dangerous terrain, it suffers no injury;
when plowing, it performs with strength and vigor. It is always seen to live long, never suffering harm.
Furthermore, pestilence was swept away, allowing all to live out their full lives. They roamed the fields in herds by morning and returned to their pens in groups by evening.
There were hymns of longing for the sacrificial animals as they arrived; in times of harmony, there was no toil even for the lowing of a single breath.

Furthermore, as those oxen approach, my sacrificial animals are already prepared— abundant, thriving, neither sickly nor diseased. They descend to drink, sometimes lying down and sometimes moving about.

To avert the calamity of fire, the planet Venus conceals its brilliance and the Fire God Zhurong retreats from his path; thus, misfortune is transformed into auspiciousness and scorching affliction is turned into refreshing coolness.
Relying upon the compassionate breeze, the phantom flames are silently extinguished.

To avert the calamities of water and fire, we rely upon the power of the Buddha to inspire the arising of compassion. May the waters follow the course of the ravines and flow peacefully; may the flames subside within the hollows of the *li* trigram.

Thus the two rivers, swelling with green tides, shall safely carry their boats, fulfilling the merit of irrigating all things; and the smoke from ten thousand households shall find relief as they move their hearths and shift their fuel.
This brings about such benefits. That the sufferings of the realms of burning, drowning, and drifting have been extinguished is entirely due to the excellent conditions of these propitiatory rites.

Thieves and bandits are driven away, their tracks vanish; petty pilferers hide their traces. There is no longer the anxiety of dogs barking in the night, nor the distress of chickens being stolen by moonlight.
Outer gates need not be closed; one may rest on high pillows without anxiety.

Furthermore, doors are constantly left unbarred, and abandoned items are picked up along deserted roads. There are no farmers raising poles upon the ridges, nor any who would dare to toy with the waters of the Huangchi River.
The soldiers are like infants; the sound of the night watch-drums has fallen silent. The people rejoice as if upon a spring terrace.
May the fulfillment of vows be like the moon appearing in a clear pool, and may the completion of the offerings be like a sound echoing through a valley. To all the myriad spirits...
May this be examined and approved. This is the *vidyā* of the Seal of the Triple Gem.

Furthermore, having already received your secret grace, how could I dare to betray our original covenant? I respectfully exhaust my sincerity on this day to specifically repay the kindness shown previously.
Furthermore,

upon the ledgers of the Six Ministries and within the registers of the Three Realms, I pray that you may grant me the name of "one whose beginning has been extinguished" and bestow upon me the inscription of "one whose end is filled. May I cultivate this in advance.

Fortunately, having obtained a human body, one dwells within consciousness to cultivate the principles of self-refinement. Having been granted a place in the mundane world, one ought to clarify the causes for transcending it.
If one did not adorn oneself in previous lives, what will be sown for future retribution? Therefore, one should pre-prepare meritorious fruits and extensively establish bridges and ferries.
Relying upon these auspicious conditions for action, one will surely obtain future blessings.
Furthermore, when cold comes, one must seek a fur coat before the cold has arrived; when thirsty, one must dig a well before the thirst has set in.
By performing good deeds in this present life, may auspicious blessings descend in future days.

It is my universal wish that the Emperor’s sagely longevity may equal that of Heaven, and that the rank and status of his civil and military officials may daily increase. May the myriad nations come like ships upon the ladder of the seas.

Capping and girding the hundred tribes of the barbarians, he blended the common people into the benevolent heavens; he led those in the eight frontiers to the realm of longevity. The seasons were harmonized like the jade candle, and the years accorded with the golden harvests.
In winter there was no excessive heat, and in summer no hidden cold; the wind did not whistle through the branches, and the rain did not break the clods of earth.

A hundred joys arise together from the governance of the state. The four classes of people each find fulfillment in their livelihoods. Those who cultivate the Way of Confucius have their names inscribed upon the Goose Pagoda;
those who master the arts and crafts await imperial summons at the Golden Gate. Merchants travel abroad and store their wares in the markets, enjoying the abundance of gold, knives, and coins;
they dig wells and plow fields, accumulating harvests that fill granaries and barns. Silk and mulberry cultivation flourish tenfold, such that both profit and virtue are fully realized.

May there be longevity, wealth, and well-being; may they flourish, prosper, and reach venerable age. May every household receive a thousand auspicious signs and a hundred blessings; may no family suffer the nine untimely deaths or the three calamities.

May all people rejoice in ascending into the spring of life; may dogs not be heard barking in the night. May the beacon fires vanish from distant frontiers, and the grass flourish within the circular enclosures.
May those with feathers, fur, scales, and shells all attain their natural lives and extensions; may all things that move or grow, fly or hide, reach the pinnacle of fulfillment.
May they flourish and multiply, reaching upward to the Peak of Existence and extending downward to the boundless realms. May all sentient beings alike ascend to the other shore.

*The Recorded Sayings of Master Xian, Compiled by Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gaofeng, Volume Ten.* *The Recorded Sayings of Master Xian, Compiled by Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gaofeng, Volume Eleven.*
General Prayer for the Gate of Fragmented Speech:
General Prayer for the Entire Section Above, Offering Blessings to the Present Emperor—His Way Surpasses that of Kings Yao and Shun; His Ministers in Office—Their Virtue Excels that of Gao Yao.

In the ranks of Kui, the mists were swept away as the dust of Hu was cleared, and spears and halberds were entirely laid low. When the moon sank over the beacon fires at the borders, the civilizing tracks became uniform everywhere.
All people rejoiced upon the spring terrace; there was no commoner who did not ascend to the realm of longevity. Thus, neighboring villages enjoyed peace and stability.
Families dwell in tranquility and peace; they are spared from the calamities of floods and mountains, and constantly encounter the harmony of earth and heaven.

Men dig wells and till fields, each secure in their livelihood; they suckle at the breast and drum their bellies, all rejoicing in their innate nature. Merchants sing their songs in the marketplaces as goods abound and wealth increases;
scholars cultivate their studies as their merit is realized and their ambitions fulfilled. In the spring, silkworms and mulberry trees flourish, and every household reels white silk.
The silkworms have yielded their cocoons; where the autumn harvest ripens, yellow clouds of grain ears are reaped everywhere. At night, there are none who must cover their beams for lack of food;

at times, one hears children singing as they strike the *rang* blocks. Oxen and sheep grow robust across the thousand mountains; roosters and dogs can be heard barking and crowing throughout the four borders.
Prisoners find eternal rest, and pestilence vanishes in secret. All aspirations are fulfilled, and boundless merit and blessings are accomplished.

As an official, he served his post without affliction and administered affairs with divine skill. People longed for him as the people of Shao did for Lord Bo and his sweet-tasting pear trees; the world vied with one another to emulate Duke Guo and his bamboo horses.
Early on, he was granted a salary of a thousand *zhong*, and he received the honor of the imperial decree on a one-foot-long tablet. May he enjoy a long and enduring life.
Having entered official service and been promoted through the ranks,

those who cultivate literature unfurl the scrolls and tablets at their Han-dynasty windows, while the poetry and books fill their shelves like those of the Yecheng library. I pray that you may be the first to ascend the three tiers of the Yu Gate.
Ascending, I pray that this single branch of the *gui* tree may be broken early, so that a hundred blessings may flourish and extend, and a thousand calamities be forever extinguished.

As for those who practice the martial way, the six chapters clarify the path of the leopard; with a three-foot blade, they caress the Dragon Spring. Thus, the achievements of Sun Zi and Wu Qi become ever more refined, while those of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing...
His fame and merit were realized early; drawing his bow and charging in pursuit, he achieved the feat of piercing a willow leaf at a hundred paces.
Returning in glory clothed in brocade, he celebrated the joy of his parents with the filial play of colorful silks. As for the management of the household...
The masters of principle possess a Way; their subtle calculations leave nothing unaccounted for. Their estates are as lofty as mountains, like those of Wang Kai;
their wealth flows like spring water, like that of Tao Zhu. As they grow old, the fragrance of the cassia blossoms even more manifest, further revealing the hidden virtues of the Dou family;
the orchids stand tall and jade-like, flourishing the illustrious reputation of the Xie household.

Serving public officials as clerks and serving the authorities, one shall receive abundant stipends. Attracting wealth and encountering the noble, one’s person shall find security. When cases are concluded, they shall be free from error or discrepancy;
when reviewing the affairs of officials, they shall be met with approval and compliance. May there always be the beauty of preservation and integrity, forever free from fault or transgression.
May there be no cause for anxiety. May the domestic way flourish and prosper; may the public sphere be pure and auspicious.

For those devoted to agriculture, they dare not complain of the frequent watering of the fields; fire-hoeing must indeed be endured as toil. With a single plow amidst the spring rains by the river, one shall reap a thousandfold in autumn.

Clouds gather over the ridges of the fields; the great harvests are always bountiful. The lofty granaries are increasingly filled with stores of grain. Dogs do not bark in the night, and officials do not knock at the gates.
As for those who raise silkworms—
Śakra secretly supported him, and Aśvaghoṣa silently aided him; he gathered every last leaf from five mu of empty space, and spun fine threads from a thousand looms.
Thus, silks and fabrics became abundant, and wealth and property flourished.
The artisan is by nature clear-headed and discerning; his mental craftsmanship is exquisite. Within his breast he possesses his own models, and from his hands he frequently produces ingenious works.
His movements always abide in auspicious places, and his efforts often encounter noble patrons. He thus doubles his daily earnings and, as he travels, meets with good fortune.
By the decree of the Celestial Writs,

merchants may trade and exchange as they wish; setting out on their journeys, they gather immense wealth, managing their operations according to their own intent, and obtaining double or triple profit in the markets where they store their goods.
The profits thereof were such that coins flowed upon the ground and wealth overflowed at midday. The family’s hereditary occupation grew increasingly noble, and its reputation shone with brilliance.

Those who practiced medicine transmitted secret formulas—both those already known and those previously unknown—to treat chronic illnesses that were otherwise difficult to cure. Their merit in saving human lives was exceedingly vast, providing relief to all.
May the Way of the World increasingly flourish; may the King of the Treasury of Merit constantly and secretly support every movement and step;
and may the Bodhisattva of Peace and Bliss further augment auspicious omens. As for the selection of the date: [text follows].
The water patterns clearly reveal the profundity of the school’s essence; the mountain formations provide deep insight into the mysterious mechanism.

His breast encompasses the artistry of creation, and his calculations derive the subtleties of the stars and constellations. He constantly meets with noble patrons who support him, and is frequently invited by wealthy households.
Wealth, food, and clothing come to him as he wishes and desires; prosperity, honor, and splendor follow his plans and expectations.
The fisherman holds several feet of silk line in his hand; clad in a single rain cape, he lets his life unfold amidst mist and rain. The fish of the river are delicious and easily sought;
the waters of the Xiang are clear enough to draw from. May his longevity be as enduring as the hills and ridges; may his blessings be as deep as the rivers and seas.

The one who opened the wine shop was Ma Xiangru, who washed the vessels; the one who stood by the hearth was Zhuo Wenjun. Guests who paid with coins came constantly, while those who stole their drinks had already departed.
Profits were gathered ten-thousandfold, and wishes were fulfilled in a thousand ways.

For those who open a shop, a hundred deities shall provide protection and ten thousand spirits shall sustain them. The business shall flourish eternally like the gate of Mengchang, and wealth and resources shall enter the storehouse constantly as if into the treasury of Wang Kai.
Legal troubles and verbal disputes shall vanish moment by moment, while fortune, rank, and auspiciousness shall follow in their wake.
The day arrived.

As one who slaughters animals for a butcher, my carving of flesh was certainly no match for the skill of Fang Shuo; yet, wielding the blade, I have presumptuously studied the art of Cook Ding. The karmic retribution for the sin of killing is as solid as ice.
It vanishes. Wealth sufficient to moisten a mansion accumulates like mountains;

yet for the gambler, clever calculations follow the mind as he seizes riches and fulfills his desires. He merely needs to perceive the opportune moment to shout in triumph, and in the end, he must surely gain the hand and fill his pockets with coins.

From the moment you cast this divination once, you shall naturally obtain a profit of one million. You will not be entangled in official litigation, nor will you be encroached upon by thieves or bandits.
Whether in action or repose, your conduct will dispel unforeseen calamities, and in every movement, you will receive newly arriving blessings.

For one who acts as a boatman, wielding the oar and managing the rudder, there will forever be no fear of waves; when encountering perils or approaching sandbanks, they shall always be protected by dragons and deities.
Whenever traveling upon the vast blue waters, it is as if proceeding safely across level ground; every undertaking will be successful, and every step will be auspicious.
Benefiting and delivering others;

as practitioners of the monastic path, may you be protected by devas and nāgas externally, while your pure conduct (*brahmacarya*) remains clear internally. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, may you be sustained by a hundred blessings throughout spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
In winter, a thousand calamities are utterly extinguished.

Those who serve as Daoist adepts wear star-patterned caps and descend from their mountain grottoes; draped in rosy robes, they emerge from the misty heights. Within six cases, the winds and thunder conceal a precious sword; in a single flask, the heavens...
The earth nurtures the numinous elixir, and blessings arrive in profusion; may their lifespan be as enduring as that of the *chūn* tree.

Those who have become nuns knit their brows like green willow leaves, dwelling within the gateway of myriad wonders; their cheeks reflect the crimson of peach blossoms, as they strive in the teachings of spontaneity.
Unconditioned and profoundly penetrating, he diligently practices the Great Way. He widely upholds the pure precepts and prolongs the lifespan of the immortals.

As a master of sorcery, he rescues beings from the suffering of the four hundred and four diseases; his efficacy is such that he succeeds one hundred percent of the time. His numinous talismans lock and sever the gates of the ghosts.
The curtain is closed. The ceremonial cap and sash are spread open to reveal the human world. The Three Primordial Honored Sages constantly bestow great auspiciousness;
the officials and soldiers of the various divisions diligently provide protection and defense day after day.

The physiognomist’s art for interpreting destiny is sublime and ancient; his skill is so refined that it moves all who behold it. In discussing auspiciousness and misfortune, he exhausts the profound principles of the five planets and the five elements;

in discerning nobility and meanness, he possesses the marvelous efficacy of hitting the mark a hundred times out of a hundred. There is no need to seek out Feng Junping in Western Shu. Is this not so?

Awaiting the time to travel south of the Yangtze to seek Guo Pu, one laughs and roams amidst the sun and moon within the *huzhong* (the alchemical crucible), dwelling at ease amidst the mists and clouds beyond the mundane world.
The broker maintains a mind of integrity and weighs goods with impartiality; he gathers merchants from the four quarters and unites the transactions of two households.

They possess abundant wealth and goods, relying solely on their eloquence that flows like a cascading river. Carriages and boats converge from all directions, and their gates are often seen so crowded as to form a marketplace.
As for the courtesans—
The life of a wandering monk advances daily; the livelihood of a pleasure-seeker is full of elegance. In the morning he accompanies the wealthy and extravagant of the four seas;
in the evening he keeps company with the youths of the Five Tombs. Amidst clusters of fine silks and brocades, he secretly dispels slander and official disputes;
amidst the sounds of strings and pipes, he constantly acquires gold, pearls, jade, and gems.
Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Gaofeng Longquan Monastery, Compiled by Ji Xian, Scroll Eleven;
Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Gaofeng Longquan Monastery, Compiled by Ji Xian, Scroll Twelve;
Memorial Service for Chen Yi (General Liturgy for Praising the Spirit).
In summary, the entire span of a hundred years of life is but a single *kṣaṇa*. How could this illusory body composed of the four elements endure for long?

Having departed from the mundane world, the fragrant soul is now distant and its destination unknown; having returned to the gates of the spring, the passing spirit is vast and lost—where does it go? Its voice and countenance...
I may not behold you; my flesh and bones are left only with grief. To extend the merit of this offering and unveiling, one must rely upon the power of your compassion.

Furthermore, even the Master, a Sage, was seen in his dream at the two pillars before his final rest; and even the Great Being Bodhidharma was heard to have returned to the West with but a single shoe.
The Dharma-body cannot avoid coming and going; how could this illusory form be free from birth and death? Having departed upon the dark path, where shall the passing soul find its refuge?
One must rely on the merit of ritual offerings and deliverance to point directly toward the path of transcendence. (Below, one may proceed to describe the specific Buddhist rites performed.
Furthermore:
Alas for this mundane world, a cycle of a hundred-year dream and illusion! The Buddhas, in their great compassion, reveal the True Vehicle to deliver sentient beings.

I humbly reflect that the deceased [Name], in his personal conduct, was frugal and modest, while in his labors, he was diligent and industrious. In his dealings with others and his treatment of people, he was fundamentally humble and harmonious without exception;
in serving his elders and caring for the vulnerable, he exhausted himself in filial piety and righteousness without fail. Just as he looked forward to reaching the height of Mount Shou, suddenly—

Sighing at the passing of the surging waves, [he] above leaves behind his gray hair, failing to provide warmth and clarity in the hall of the *xuán* (mother), and below abandons his orphans, wailing bitterly in the thatched mourning chamber.
Wishing to solemnize the offerings to the ancestors, he resorts to the cultivation of incense and meditation. (As before) Furthermore:
Earth, water, fire, and wind are truly but dreams within a dream. Who knows that beyond this body of birth, aging, sickness, and death, there exists another body?

If one seeks to reach the other shore and transcend the cycle of rebirth, one must exert effort within this very realm. We respectfully venerate the spirit of [Name]: by nature long-suffering and generous, with a lineage as brilliant as the earth itself.
When he first established his household, he was renowned for such abundance that the grain rotted in the storehouses and the coins decayed in the chests. As for his conduct...

In his native village, he enjoyed the beauty of kinship with the benevolent and harmony with his neighbors. Fortune rested upon his person, such that he partook in longevity, tranquility, and well-being.

Prosperity flowed to his descendants, such that virtue, conduct, and righteousness were fully realized. Having received the "crane's recommendation," his five successive examinations were not in vain;
pointing toward the Dragon Gate, his single leap was imminent. Just as it was said his life would be as firm as the *chun* tree, who would have expected the dew on the leeks?
Suddenly the dawn has broken; hundreds of thousands of matters have all become empty. Eighty-two years were but a dream. The care of the three cauldrons could not be fulfilled;
the regrets in the nine springs increase in vain. Unable to detain the twin wheels [of time], we look down upon the arrival of the seventh day.

I present this offering to my grandparents and ancestors, who were sovereigns of virtue at their own gates; as a filial descendant receiving blessings, how could I dare forget the kindness of my own flesh and blood?

Coinciding with this anniversary of their passing, I look up in devotion to the Awakened Sovereign. I humbly reflect that [Name] was diligent and frugal in managing the household and instructed his children in the Odes and Documents.

Brothers share no words of discord; friends exhort one another toward the path of goodness. May you personally enjoy the pleasures of your fields and gardens, while together promoting the benevolence of your village.

Having already achieved the merit of founding a family and establishing a career during your lifetime, you should now harbor the intention of honoring the conclusion of life and remembering those long departed [on their memorial anniversaries].

In offering this memorial for my father, I am moved to sigh upon ascending the heights, giving rise to a resolve of laborious reflection. Though I entrust my lamentations to the "Liao-e" (Sweet Flag and Mugwort) verses, I find it difficult to fully express my sincere plea of grief.
Although I have exhausted the heart of a filial son, I cannot repay the virtue of Heaven. I humbly reflect that my father, [Name], was of profound and heavy merit in his creation and nurturing of me.
The kindness of his upbringing was profound; it was our original hope that he would be nurtured for a full hundred years. Who would have thought he would suddenly pass away from a single illness?

For five or seven days after his death, the toil of his labor was remembered with gratitude, making it clear how great was the debt owed to him who gave us life. Having no means to repay him, we are suddenly moved by the lamentation of being left without a protector.

Only a son of the Buddha can fulfill the way of a filial son. Borrowing upon Your Holiness’s sacred compassion to offer a small tribute to my fatherly love, I pray that You will grant the grace of forgiving his transgressions and directly point out the path to rebirth in the Pure Land.
I grieve that [Name], who formerly dwelt in the mundane world, has only just reached sixty-two years of age.
Now, returning to the spring palace, thirty-five days have already passed.

Furthermore, as youth approaches its twilight, I grieve that the time for my venerable father’s return to long life has come; yet the vermilion summer has suddenly arrived, when a filial son ought to repay his debt of gratitude.
On this day, wishing to offer the soul for deliverance and liberation, one must rely upon the compassion of our Buddha.

We respectfully contemplate that [Name] dwelt in the human realm for seventy-eight years and has cast off the illusory dust of the world for thirty-five days. Desiring to repay the virtue of their life-giving and nurturing, we employ the merit of this memorial service for their offering.

Since my father passed away during the minor anniversary (*xiǎoxiáng*), I have had no one to rely upon; I constantly cherish the sorrow of the "Ascending the Hill" (*zhǐhù*) poem. Having the Buddha as my refuge, I have long since made the vow to save all beings.

I further reflect that [so-and-so] maintained a mind of equanimity and conducted himself with gentleness and kindness. As he was a person who practiced the ten wholesome deeds (*daśakuśala*), he ought to enjoy [the fruits of his merit].
A lifespan of a hundred years—how could one have expected that a single illness would so suddenly send you back to the Nine Springs? Your soul wanders afar, seeking no place of return;

the path ahead is vast and desolate, with no turning back. If you wish to point the way toward the auspicious clouds of the Minor Anniversary (xiaoxiang), you must rely upon the exemplary standards of the Great Awakened One.
For three years she wept blood upon the funeral mats, deeply grieving for the resolve of Zi-lao; for seven days she abstained from drink, profoundly honoring the heart of Zeng-zen.

She moved the sincerity of Wang Xiu to cease his farming and that of Du to suspend his duties; her hidden virtue evoked the sighs of her neighbors. Although the events of antiquity and the present may differ...
Though their status differs, the affection between mother and child is no different. I grieve deeply for [Name], who dwelt in this Jambudvīpa world manifesting in a female form;
internally she fulfilled the duties of a mother, and externally she brought harmony to her kin. Her kindness in nurturing was profound, and her virtue in her toils was complete.
In these years of long life, one never forgets the joy of filial service; yet who would have thought that the quietude of the mother’s chamber would so suddenly give rise to heartache?

A hundred days since the mother’s passing, the moon over the mother’s hall is cold, leaving behind only the traces of the wooden effigy. Clouds of sorrow gather at the orchid-steps as the grief for the neighbor’s parting suddenly arises.
With deep sorrow, I reflect that ten months have passed without her return; thus, I rely upon the nine grades of merit to perform posthumous cultivation on her behalf.

I humbly consider that my mother possessed a long-standing virtuous heart and was never deficient in noble conduct. She maintained a gentle and refined character, eminently manifesting the decorum of the inner chambers; she responded to all circumstances with circumspection, perfectly fulfilling the duties of a wife.
One son has reached old age, and two daughters have found worthy husbands; while the world admired the glory of their official ranks, her own kin were suddenly—
I have heard that we shall part forever; the severing of the loom from days past can no longer be witnessed, and the playful filial offerings of this morning cannot now be made.
Without relying upon the Pure Land to transcend this life, how could the deceased soul be delivered?

Regarding the minor anniversary (*xiǎoxiáng*) of my mother’s passing: because she labored so hard to give birth to me, I have suddenly been moved by thoughts of her being no longer with me. The Buddha is able to save beings through skillful means;

I respectfully offer this small token of gratitude. I humbly reflect that [the deceased] possessed noble conduct marked by serenity and a pure, mature heart; it is fortunate that a successor has been born.
O four sons, your allotted lifespans should have reached a full hundred years; how could it be that beyond the age of fifty, you must suddenly part for a thousand autumns?
In an instant, we grieve at the separation of a full year; our sorrowful tears fall like rain.
Having no means to repay the kindness of your upbringing, there is only the Buddha who shows the path to rebirth.
It has been one hundred days since my late father passed away;
