six or seven months have gone by, yet he has not returned from his journey. As I reflect back on my grandmother’s passing, six or seven months have likewise elapsed since she joined him.

Desiring to offer sustenance for their dual souls, it is fitting to cultivate the Nine Grades of Merit. May you first respond as the Lord of Transformation and simultaneously serve as the King of Equality; we look to you to open this path.
The gateways of skillful means each point toward the path of transcendence.
When a daughter recommends her mother or a husband recommends his wife,
the daughter’s grief is but a laborious carving of wood, and the husband’s remembrance is but an empty recollection of the sorrow over the overturned basin.
To cause both souls to be delivered together, one must rely on the Three Jewels for empowerment. This filial daughter (Name) grieves deeply for her deceased mother (Surname);
and this husband (Name) humbly acts on behalf of his deceased wife (Surname). In one case, the righteousness [of filial duty] was profound as toward one's own flesh-and-blood parent;

in the other, the kindness was deep as toward one bound by the marriage vow. Originally, these were joys of being kin within a household; who would have expected that we would share the same path of birth and death?

For the six or seven generations of ancestors and the four or seven generations of mothers—whether mother or child, they have successively returned to their final end—we recite the names of the Buddha and the sutras to rely upon for their deliverance.

Thus, we direct the collective resolve of the assembly to reverently offer this memorial for these two souls: we expound the ritual protocols of the Great Sage Manjushri and perform the precious repentance of Avalokitesvara, universally responding to the needs of the three thousand worlds.
The assembly of sages of the trichiliocosm, together with the kings of the underworld from the four, seven, six, and seven generations, have been honored in requital.

Three grandsons have successively offered offerings for their grandmother, paternal aunt, and maternal grandmother, who have returned to their final rest one after another; the eldest grandson and the second grandson join in lamentation to offer prayers for their deliverance.
We, [Name] and others, reverently commemorate our grandmother [Name] and our paternal aunt [Name].

As we approach the first month of the lunar year, barely two days having passed since their passing, we find ourselves unable to bear that the spirits of these two noble ladies have together returned to the dark soil of the Nine Springs.

For my late mother and my wife, during the first seven days [of mourning], the clouds darken over the Hall of the Mother (Xuántáng), where I could not fulfill my will to serve her countenance; the wind laments in the Chamber of Orchids (Lánshì), suddenly causing grief for our lifelong bond.
Although the paths of the aged and the young differ, birth and extinction ultimately return to the same way. I reverently contemplate my deceased mother, [Lady] (Surname).
He enjoyed a worldly lifespan of seventy-five years; his deceased wife (Lady surnamed *Mǒ*) reached the age of thirty-two.
Before two days had passed since her passing, we have shared this eternal parting from the Great Thousandfold World.
As the first seven-day memorial period approaches, we must rely upon the sacred teachings of the Three Vehicles to cultivate the sublime spirits of these two souls.
When the wife of Duke Gong was recommended for marriage, people admired her vow of lifelong fidelity; throughout the generations of Zhou women, the sound of her virtuous wailing was renowned.

Her soul has flown away upon the misty waves of the Xiang River, and her dreams have ended with the clouds and rain of the Terrace of Chu. I humbly reflect that my deceased husband governed his household.
Living in harmony and treating others with gentleness and kindness, she had hoped to fulfill the joy of "an old woman sharing her life with a gentleman.

Yet, who would have expected that she would give rise to the lament of the "heavenly people" who have no one to turn to? Though one gazes upward to Heaven, what benefit can be found? One can only look toward the stone to stir grief.
Desiring to repay the grace of those who tied her hair for her, she shall rely upon the fruit of offering lamps.

Furthermore, when we two families were joined in marriage, our original hope was that she would serve with the diligence of sweeping and dusting; yet, separated in an instant for a thousand autumns, it is difficult to expect her to fulfill the trust of offering the *ping* and *fan* herbs.
I reflect deeply upon my deceased husband (Name): he was fair in his conduct toward himself, loyal and generous in his dealings with others, and harmonious within his own kin.

Outwardly, he brought harmony to his local community; we all believed that he would enjoy the joy of aging together for a hundred years. Yet, who could have anticipated that he would part ways midway?

When his wife was interred at the Orchid Terrace (Lantai), the place fell silent and only gave rise to the sorrow of dancing before a mirror; when the Phoenix Pavilion (Fengge) was locked away from incense, there arose the lament of beating upon a basin.

I humbly reflect upon my deceased wife (so-and-so). From early on she was diligent in the way of a wife and naturally maintained the decorum of the inner chambers. It was our hope that we would grow old together for a hundred years; who would have thought she would suddenly end her life through a single illness?
That she could not reach the age where brows meet in harmony is a source of grief, and that our hair has been tied together in marriage in vain brings but sorrow.

As the clouds return to the immortal isles, the evening smoke is cold; as flowers fall at the spring terrace, the days are long. To cause her noble spirit to transcend, one must rely upon wondrous conditions; thus, may the Buddhist hymns be raised high.
The melodic strains continue the performance of the severed lute strings; the incense smoke from the burner dissipates as it mingles with the rising mist of sorrow.

Furthermore, for a hundred years you were destined to grow old together, pledging the bond of hair-tying; yet the four elements have suddenly become void, and you hastily give rise to the lamentation of beating the basin.

I reflect with utmost sorrow that my deceased wife was ever devoted to the path of a virtuous wife and fully perfected the decorum of the inner chambers. She was complete in both filial piety and righteousness, and her kin were all harmonious.

Her brothers were like *jijiling* birds upon the high mountains, bound by the duty of mutual aid in times of urgency and distress; yet suddenly, like wild geese amidst the clouds, they have been struck by the grief of her passing.

I reverently reflect that [my deceased elder brother/younger brother], though sharing the Way with me as fellow human beings, was bound to me by ties as close as those of kinship. Just as we were about to harmonize in our shared essence, you suddenly returned to the Truth.
The grounds where we once roamed in the bamboo grove give rise to sorrow; beneath the shade of the *dànlì* tree, I am moved to sigh in grief.

The fragrant orchid offered for my son has withered upon the jade steps; deep, somber mists of grief obscure the void. The phoenix enters the crimson heavens; silent winds of sorrow swirl across the earth.
I humbly reflect that my deceased son (Name), a filial son capable of upholding the family and a fine talent for managing the household affairs, was originally expected to promote loyalty.

In this house of filial piety, it was hoped that the legacy of the *jī* and *qiú* would be fully inherited; who would have known that through a single illness, there would be a final parting for a thousand autumns?

The eldest son drowned, a wound to the heart as he was the one to uphold the ancestral vessel—never expecting to lose the oars in midstream. By the Buddha’s vow to deliver all beings, may I point the way for you to board the raft upon the celestial stream.

The Path of the Immortals. I humbly reflect that my deceased son studied diligently at Longmen yet failed to penetrate its depths; he personally beheld the Jiao River only to pass through it in an instant.

One night, when the watch was deep, he finally emulated the youth who crossed the Xiang; for a thousand autumns, his parting has become a source of regret, turning him into a "Banished Immortal" who grasps at the moon.
Where the sounds of the echoing rapids rise, they augment my lamentation; when the swift waves splash, they add to my silent tears.
The orchid offered at the Xie courtyard has withered; in the end, all is empty. The clouds of the Chu gorges have dispersed; one knows not where they have gone.

I humbly reflect that my deceased daughter’s virtuous heart was pure and mature, and her noble conduct was harmonious and refined. Who would have expected that the onset of a single illness would so suddenly bring about a parting for a hundred years?
I have relied upon the Buddha’s fruition to offer a small measure of praise for his journey to the realm of immortals.
My uncles, moved by a heart of grief and pained by the loss of their kinsman, find no refuge in their sincerity; they therefore rely upon the power of the Buddha Vehicle.

I humbly reflect that my late uncles were blessed with the accumulated merits of generations, their excellence emerging from a single lineage—my late father’s worthy scions (referring to the elder uncle as *zouzi* and the younger as *jizi*).
They were the very branches of my own father’s kinship, and I had expected them to enjoy long lives; how could I have anticipated that they would meet their end at the age of one hundred?

Sisters, by the natural order of kinship, we shared the same birth and were joined as branches of one tree. Yet worldly affairs return to emptiness; it is unavoidable that we must pass from life to death.

I humbly reflect that although our deceased elder sister and younger sister were both nurtured by the same parents, they each departed to wed their respective husbands. Like the *dìhuá* (fraternal blossoms),...
I had presumed that within this succession of illustrious kin, the ranks of the geese would suddenly be broken by the pain of parting.

Now, with clouds of sorrow hanging over you, you grieve bitterly for the collapse of Mount Tai; with tears flowing in ceaseless streams, you overflow with lamentation for your son-in-law at the eastern couch.

Though you were as pure as ice and as lustrous as jade, you could not escape the cycle of death and rebirth. I humbly reflect that you, my lord, were endowed with a magnanimous virtue and bestowed your grace equally upon those within and without your household.
I privately rejoiced at the good fortune of our entire family, having been able to extend the affection due to a "half-son" to you.
Yet, I did not expect that the four elements of the body would become empty, and that such a separation for a thousand autumns would so suddenly come to pass.

The clouds of sorrow darken the night as the mother-in-law grieves over her daughter-in-law’s sudden passing; tears fall like rain in the new autumn as she cannot bear to face the sighs rising from the gate.
Having parted forever for a thousand autumns, what reliance remains for this half-child? To ensure that her spirit may ascend, we rely upon the power of virtuous causes.
I offer this memorial for my late mother-in-law, [Name]. She gave birth to sons who were filial, their reputations already renowned in the northern hall;

she raised daughters with noble families, her love especially honored in the eastern courtyard. It was thought she would enjoy a hundred years of life, yet who would have expected her end through a single illness?
At dawn, the mountains grow dark as clouds of sorrow disperse; at night, the ravines stretch vast as rushing waters flow away.
The son-in-law’s grief knots within his household as the one upon the eastern couch has suddenly passed away; tears fall from his sleeves in the bitter pain of losing his only child.
Were it not for the virtuous conditions beyond the mundane world, there would be no means to offer prayers for this honored guest of the family. I humbly reflect that the deceased son-in-law, [Name]:

The worthy Xian flourished during a prosperous age; his lineage emerged from a distinguished family. Internally, he brought harmony to the joy of his parents; externally, he enjoyed the reputation of his neighborhood.

It was said that he was deeply devoted to the duty of kinship and constantly cultivated the rituals of respect. Yet, one could not have expected that Heaven would not bless such humility, suddenly causing him to be the first to return to the earth.

Furthermore, at the gateway of destiny, there was hope for the chance to harmonize with the "sparrow-in-the-center" omen; yet, lacking reliance on favorable winds and fire, I have suddenly lost the prospect of transforming into a dragon.
Desiring to extend an offering for their deliverance, I humbly rely upon your compassion.

When Shang died, his carriage went forth and never returned; Confucius lamented the sighing of flowing waters as they departed and did not come back. When Zhuang Zhou lost his wife, he gave rise to a cry of grief for her departure from home.
Life and death are the ultimate limit of destiny; whether one acts or remains still is not something humans can control. I reflect upon the solitary and upright nature of such-and-such a person.
In his heart, he harbored the ambition to travel the four quarters; like a spirited horse yoked to its carriage, he possessed the intent to gallop a thousand li.
He constantly employed boats and carts to facilitate the exchange of goods and wealth, seeking the profits of long-distance trade and taxation to provide for the enrichment of his household.

Yet, before his noble aspirations could be fulfilled, one did not expect that his allotted years would be so short. His wandering soul now drifts into the distant, dark paths of the Nine Springs—where has it gone?

Long has he departed; his spirit wanders in vast obscurity across ten thousand miles, longing for his kin yet unable to return. We reverently cultivate the Pure Land to assist him on his journey beyond.
As for the Sangha’s dedication to their own Master (reciting the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*):
how could Śākyamuni Buddha have avoided manifesting his passing at the Twin Trees? And how could the Great Master Bodhidharma have escaped returning west to the Pamirs?
Although the Dharmakāya is fundamentally without birth or extinction, how could the debt of gratitude for [your mother’s] milk be neglected?
To increase the wondrous radiance of Prajñā, one must rely upon the Great Teaching of the Avataṃsaka. I reverently contemplate our late Master, the Great Virtuous One:
your majestic appearance was like that of Maitreya descending to be born; your lucid Chan mechanism was as if Xuansha had never left the mountain pass. Longshan...
Venerable Patriarch, Master of the Yan-shui lineage: your preceptual conduct vied with the frost and moon for brilliance, and your Brahma-voice thundered alongside the wind and rain.

Suddenly, one morning, you attained a profound realization; shaking out your sleeves, you departed. The robe has already been transmitted to the man at the mountain pass; your backache became instead the companion of those beyond the mundane world.
Today being the thirty-fifth day, how shall we repay our debt to the teacher? We shall employ this to open one hundred and twenty cases.
Accompanying [the deceased] for a short while upon the path of clouds;
I humbly pray that this offering for the departed may bring universal benefit to the family.

The dust of worldly toil is cleansed away, vast and expansive like clouds dispersing to reveal a clear sky; karmic obstructions are suddenly eliminated, as sudden and complete as ice melting and snow dissolving.

One realizes the mind and reaches the source, stilling the intellect and forgetting all conditions. Amidst coming and going, one awakens to the absence of coming and going; amidst birth and death, one awakens to the absence of birth and death.
Severing all delusion and falsehood, one proceeds directly toward true emptiness. Having shattered the three poisons, one realizes the three [emptinesses].

Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Having subdued the six thieves, one cultivates the six pāramitās and the six divine functions. Only by thoroughly understanding the laws of arising and ceasing does one clearly realize the non-existence of self and person.
Never departing from the forest of Bodhisattvas, one dwells eternally within the Flower Treasury Ocean.
Furthermore, the Immortals of the Numerical Path will frequently come to welcome you back to the Purple Palace; three-colored auspicious clouds will lead you out beyond the mundane world.
Casting off the five hindrances and utterly transcending the six sense-objects, you shall be born in the palace of Maitreya and enter early into the assembly at the Dragon Flower Tree.
Furthermore, within the Golden Palace, one constantly beholds the body of purple-gold; at times, amidst the hearts of red lotus flowers, one hears the verses on suffering and emptiness.
Moreover,
Upon the sea of the four modes of birth, they lowered the sails of ignorance; at the shore of the three types of awakening, they severed the ropes of delusion.

Departing from the world-system of Sahā, they were reborn in the celestial palace of Tuṣita. There, they frequently beheld the jade-like radiance [of the Buddha] face-to-face and daily heard the wondrous Dharma with their ears.
To realize clearly that mind itself is Buddha, to suddenly comprehend that which is neither thought nor emptiness, to attain the Prajñāpāramitā,
and to achieve unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, the boundless ocean of afflictions is completely dried up, and the immeasurable flowers of wisdom blossom forth in vast abundance.
Moreover,
Above, they pass through seven layers of nets; below, they ride upon thousand-petaled lotuses. Floating and drifting, they are born in the Tuṣita Heaven;
in great numbers, they walk through the Maṇi palaces. There they behold the golden countenance face-to-face and listen to the sound of the Dharma with their own ears.
Furthermore, at the ten-thousand-fathom depth of the Jade Pond, the golden wind stirs and lotuses bloom upon them; within the thousand-tiered jeweled pavilions, as the pearl curtains are rolled back,
the Buddha appears amidst the clouds.
Furthermore, one strolls leisurely upon jeweled horses within the jeweled pavilions and jeweled canopies; one traverses fragrant clouds over fragrant lands and fragrant cities, experiencing joy.
Moreover,

Beneath the shimmering lattice of jewel nets and amidst the ethereal drifting of celestial flowers, one pays homage to the Compassionate Honored One who possesses the Ten Epithets and awakens to the wondrous principle of the One Vehicle.
Furthermore,
At the moment Subhūti snapped his fingers, he recognized the gate of the thousand sages; when Mahākāśyapa broke into a smile, he suddenly awakened to the principle of the one true reality.
Furthermore,
In the Hall of Universal Radiance, they turn the mundane mind into the Buddha-mind; within the Palace of Bodhi, they transform the fleshly eye into the wisdom-eye.

At every step, red lotuses bloom beneath their feet; gracefully, green canopies rise in the air. Casting off the defilements of the three outflows, they give birth to the pure ground of the ten adornments.
Entering within the jeweled crown, they sit upon the lion throne; hearing this once, they attain great enlightenment.
Through these causes and conditions, one realizes the ultimate principle of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*).
Furthermore, true luminosity illuminates it; the Dharma-eye ascends to the summit of Mount Sumeru and pierces through the four continents. Thus, one awakens to the state of perfect clarity. True...
The mind turns toward the interior of a single atom and sits there contemplating the three realms.

Furthermore, the true mind is sovereign and the dharma-nature is carefree; without entering the three vehicles, one directly ascends to perfect enlightenment, realizing that there is nothing to be realized.
The Dharma of non-attainment; the gate of realizing that there is nothing to be realized. Life after life, they don the Tathāgata’s robe of patience;
age after age, they dwell within the jewels of the Buddhas’ compassion.

Furthermore, as the clouds of obstruction disperse, the moon of Bodhi appears; as the ocean of karma dries up, the mountain of merit rises high. One does not enter into heterodox schools, but constantly gives rise to right mindfulness.

Furthermore, within the ponds of the seven treasures, all karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions, and afflictive obstructions are completely cleansed; upon the nine lotus pedestals, one constantly hears wondrous sounds,
Brahma-sounds, and ocean-tide sounds.
Furthermore, they shatter the mountains of affliction and tear asunder the net of craving and desire. Mental doubts are instantly resolved like the untying of a hundred-fold flowered turban;
the stains of transgression silently vanish like the dispersal of a heap of sand by the eight winds.

The ten evils and five heinous crimes of women are all melted away like ice; the three poisons and seven afflictions are entirely purified through repentance. The five outflows are transformed into the state of no-outflow, and the six sense faculties are changed into wholesome roots.
By relying on the merit of this dedication for the deceased through the One Vehicle, one points toward the path of rebirth in the nine grades of the Pure Land.
May you joyfully follow the jade maidens to welcome and sweep the immortal mountains of Mount Penglai; may you long accompany Lady Heng’er to return directly to the moon palace of the lunar mansion.

May Guanyin of the Eastern Sea personally bestow her prediction upon you; may you vow to practice together with the Dragon Girl of the South. Swiftly emerge from the path of delusion and quickly ascend to the garden of enlightenment.
Furthermore,
when the fruits of karma wither and the flowers of transgression fade away, one shall ascend to the seashore to pay homage to the countenance of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
and forever attend upon Lady Māyā by the side of the Snow Mountains.
The two souls of Vairocana within the Flower Treasury World follow one another at every step; the lotus pedestals of the Pure Land are available to all who have faith.
Need one be constrained by age—whether old or young? Let them be called by the same name and share the same title. Pair upon pair of phoenixes and cranes return to the azure heavens. The Phoenix...
May we return in pairs to the Treasure Cave; may we join our hairpins and advance together, riding upon the vessel of Prajñā;
may we walk hand in hand and arrive simultaneously at the other shore of Pāra. Furthermore:
Riding together upon the causes of conditioned action, each points toward the path of rebirth. Upon the red lotus pedestals, you shall follow one another step by step;
before the jade-green steps, you will surely find one another at every turn. May all nine grades ascend together to the highest grade; may those of the three vehicles realize the supreme vehicle.
Turning back to receive guidance, they ascend to the heavenly realms; joining hands in carefree leisure, they return to the Buddha-land.

Furthermore, the kind mother with her thick eyebrows has long since followed the Buddha-mother back to the celestial palace; the lovely lady from the phoenix bed shall now accompany Dà'ér (Xiǎo'é) to the moon palace.
Two wisps of colored clouds lightly support her feet, and a pair of jeweled nets adorn her body. Having already formed [karmic bonds] during her life...
Regarding their family members who have passed away, may they all ascend together to the Buddha-land.

Those who drowned and died without relying on the Sage’s grace find it difficult to escape the perilous straits of delusion; may the sweeping waves of the seven-day memorial rites wash away [the defilements] of the great trichiliocosm.

The ocean of sins and defilements is transformed into an ocean of merit; the dragon palace is changed into a celestial palace. Roaming freely through the Milky Way, one is spared the suffering of sinking into the abyss for ten thousand kalpas;
finding joy upon the star-bridge, one is free from the anxiety of emerging from or entering the three evil paths. I pray that you will grant me passage upon your compassionate boat.
May they swiftly ascend to the other shore.

Furthermore, as the waves of the river of craving are vast, may they look forward to ascending high to the far bank; as the sea of suffering is deep, may they rely upon the compassionate vessel for universal deliverance.
Furthermore,

without lingering in the middle stream, one immediately ascends to the other shore. One pays homage to the compassionate aspect of the Water Treasury and hears the subtle and wondrous sound of the ocean tide.

Furthermore, having cleansed the mind to attain profound insight, he immersed himself in the depths of the sages' domain. Pointing toward the Buddha as his ultimate Brahmin, he departed from the mundane sea of floating and sinking.

Mounting the backs of the white whales and giant fish of Li Bai, he sought out the stars of the Ox and Dipper followed by Zhang Qian. With a pure breeze beneath both armpits, he laughed and roamed among the Three Mountains.
On this island of *páng*, where a stream flows through a *táohuán* (Peach Blossom Spring) that has remained serene for a thousand ages,
there was the holy monk Āluó who welcomed and guided the Bodhisattva Shuizàng.

Dedicate this monastic body to achieve the ultimate goal on the Right Path, treading step by step upon the distant heavens. With the heart’s aspiration to realize the source of delusion, go forth and ride upon the emerald carriage.
Entering the stage of the four dhyānas and possessing the emptiness of the single nature, one gazes from the midst of the high and vast lion throne.
The Fragrant Blossoms of Nāgārjuna. One Illumination of Perfect Enlightenment; Sudden Awakening to the True and Constant.
*The Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gao Peak*, Volume Twelve.
*The Recorded Sayings of Master Yin of Longquan Monastery at Gao Peak*, Volume Thirteen.
In the Dharma-discourse on Nirvana, the expression of grief:
Last autumn, one night, wind and thunder arose; they roared through the earth, rushed across the sky, and tossed the seas and mountains. They startled the ancient elders of many years.
A chisel! He leveledly snapped off the horn of the Azure Dragon in mid-air. From afar, across a thousand li, the news of his passing has returned;

the grief shakes the entire forest, and all are struck with consternation. While the funeral rites for the late Master were still resounding through the heavens, it was extinguished upon reaching this blind donkey.
(He then lets out a long sigh of profound sorrow.)
Furthermore, for thirty years he was the foremost practitioner on the sea. With such a sudden departure, who would not feel sorrow?
Nevertheless, one must know that Master [So-and-so] has never been born and never died; he has never gone and never come.
At this very moment—pointing to the shrine—he said: "In this way, I was born of the same lineage as Xuefeng, yet I do not die of the same lineage as Xuefeng.
If you wish to know the final word, let us clearly request the entire assembly to raise their voices together: 'Alas! Alas!'"
(Furthermore, for both monastics and laity):
Having wandered through this dusty world for years, a single point of radiant splendor is inherently natural. Do not be surprised that my return is so swift;

you must believe there is another heaven within the alchemical vessel. My soul has transcended to the Pure Realm, and though you all linger here in sorrowful attachment, it is as they say: [Text continues]
Coming and going are fundamentally unimpeded; yet how can one deny that they are clearly present before one’s eyes?
When the time arrives, there is no need for concealment or avoidance—weeping for the heavens within the heavens (Alas, alas).
The coffin is opened;

atop the mountain of the five aggregates lies a single expanse of emptiness. Though we walk and enter together, we do not meet. From this point on, having turned the pivot, one pierces the celestial aperture;
with a direct flip of the body, one is unimpeded everywhere. [Master] (Name), though you come and go within the sea of birth and death, you have attained perfect stillness.

Within the realm of true purity, there is fundamentally no arising or ceasing. To move is to give rise to the root of birth and death; to be still is to sink into the land of delusion and intoxication.

If both movement and stillness are extinguished together, one falls into a void of non-existence. If both movement and stillness are gathered together, one is already deceived regarding Buddha-nature.
How can one deliberate upon the single point of transcending movement and stillness right now? Taking one step out the door, I shall explain it for you: pick it up!
The eyebrows leave no trace; everyone, take heed and exert yourselves together!
Thus, with every step, a pure breeze arises. (Also for Elder Puming.)
Laozi Xiansha of Puming was a neighbor to [the Master]. He resided at the monastery for thirty-four years and lived to the age of seventy-one.
Parting during the summer retreat, he traveled home against the heat; a monk who has completed his affairs knows the beginning and the end.
Pushing out his meditation cushion, the bright moon is in the sky; lifting up his alms-bag, the clear breeze fills the room. His straw sandals are tightly bound and his cassock is freshly laundered.
He proceeds to the cremation site to fulfill the ritual requirements. (Speaking in a loud voice: "Venerable Puming, now is the very time.
Please depart from the abbot’s quarters. (Tapping the coffin once: "Arise!"
Hanging in the true void, formless—what name can it have? With five colors, the body beyond bodies is depicted; the spirit of the entire canon is hidden herein.

A petition for the renovation of the bell tower with glazed tiles:
This tower stands a hundred feet high, majestically surmounting the ravines and reaching toward the heavens. Its single toll of the bell can cause those who hear its sound to awaken to the Way.
As time has passed, the structural timbers and roof tiles have fallen into ruin; to restore the old as if it were new, we rely upon compassion and the joy of giving.
The "Memorandum on Transforming Rice and Opening the Path" states:

Having made vows over billions of kalpas to be free from all obstacles, now turn back and awaken with vigor. Do not shrink from shaving your head; you must enter together with Danxia.
This is the Great Dharma Gate. Do not let the Jewel Moon emerge alone from the stage of the Single Head; O Bodhisattvas who love the Dharma, you should all together form bonds of joyful affinity.
You scholars who have transcended the mundane shall now manifest the mark of perfection.

When officials and commoners are transformed by the Dharma-gate of the *duṇḍa* (ordination certificate) and the *shū* (petition), the four gates open and the six powers penetrate, allowing them to freely brandish their arms. Yet, caught within the net of worldly entanglements—thousandfold and ten-thousandfold knots—is it not easy to extricate oneself?
As many days and months passed, he suddenly realized that yesterday was wrong and today is right. Venerable Da-mu immediately took leave of his mother and [departed] with incense...

Petition for the Ordination of a Daoist Nun:
Illusory life has lost its way; may we awaken from the delusions of the patriarchs. Seeking the source of our original nature, may we return to the single truth within quiescence.
Since we are already like willow catkins clinging to the mud, we shall strive to become lotuses that do not adhere to the water. We rejoice to have encountered this sacred grace.
One may thus attain the marks of a Buddha. If the Great Layman’s brush-tip were to produce even a single stroke, it would resonate like jade and gold;

In the Śītavana Grove, the World-Honored One held up his robes to show them to the merchants; before Mount Shaoshi, Bodhidharma, the direct successor of the Dharma, transmitted them personally.
Although the Way is a mere inch and remains untainted, what prevents a single thread from connecting? If you wish to obtain the three robes, let us join our hands together.
In the Preface to the Hundred-Patch Robe:

This is not merely intended to inspire awe among the worldly; it is truly meant to serve as a magnificent sight for the Dharma-gate.

Refine it out! Those who are impatient, look!

Let each extend a hand to jointly establish the supreme cause of Prajñā, and with a sincere heart, together form the virtuous assembly of the Avataṃsaka.
Preface to the Commentary on the Vajra Assembly:
In the past, the Buddha-dharma was entrusted to kings and ministers; now, to revitalize the ancestral tradition, it must be sustained by lay practitioners and elders.
May we together possess the vajra-eye and jointly form the karmic conditions for Prajñā-pāramitā. This shall not only lead us to transcend the beginningless cycle of saṃsāra, but furthermore—
Accomplishing such immense merit, the True Persons are truly extraordinary; may each of you take up this responsibility.
This preface for the *Ullambana* Assembly is inscribed:
the golden wind whistles as it is the season when the Earth Deity pardons transgressions; the jade moon is full, marking the time when the Venerable One rescues his kin.

On this day, having fortunately encountered such a season, why not form a bond of karmic affinity? Thus, we have gathered virtuous people from the district of Hua to jointly establish this superior assembly of the *urņapātra* (lotus bowl).
This not only resolves the public case of ten million years, but shall also trace the spirits of the five hundred kalpas.
May each of you please take up this responsibility; how could there be any room for discrimination?

Section on Self-Explanatory Statements.

The Master himself recounted the causes for the virtues of the Bhikṣu Yeshi: his life was assigned to the Bingshen year; he resided in the Yiwu month; on the day of Guiyou and at the hour of Guihai, he entered the womb in the Bingxu year.
His birth year, Geng, was marked by many obstacles. Having planted the roots of virtue in his youth, he was fortunate enough to dwell in the Central Kingdom, receiving the grace of his father.
In her birth and upbringing, she was moved by the protective embrace of Heaven and Earth. At the age of ten, her father passed away prematurely;

she observed the mourning rites for five winters, yet her compassionate mother abandoned her to remarry. Having endured every form of solitude and hardship, how could she not feel sorrow and lamentation?
She vowed to renounce the secular world and leave her kin, aspiring to leave the household life and return to the Buddha. Thus, she joyfully entered the Gate of Emptiness.
Before two autumns had passed since ascending the stellar cycle [of the monastic order], the bell of the chamber of the Dharma Master tolled;

it was an untimely tragedy to be parted from my late teacher for the first time. Not even a full year had elapsed since the master’s parinirvāṇa, when my noble and virtuous mother suddenly returned to the gates of the spring source.

Calamities and misfortunes converged at once, manifesting ten thousand forms of extreme suffering and heart-rending grief. I lament that sixty sexagenary cycles have already passed in this Jambudvīpa world.
At twenty-nine years of age, I have carried my aspirations in vain; through the passing seasons, I have borne my days and months to no purpose.
Having failed to seek the Eastern Passage for myself, I must instead fulfill my parents' wish for them to return to the West.

Unable to avoid casting off my body to wander aimlessly, I have traced my humble footsteps from my native home to Lingjiang and Qujiang, briefly halted at Wengyuan, and returned again to Shiyi and Baoyi. I have traversed every forest monastery, yet have not yet encountered one with the clear eye.
The Master took up his staff and returned, seeking a place to settle and dwell. Wandering at ease, he traveled toward that land;
while climbing a high mountain for a view, he recognized the dilapidated remains of an ancient temple and site of practice, where the plaque inscribed with "Lóngquán" (Dragon Spring) had faded away.

Thorns and briars surrounded it on all sides, the walls and fences had collapsed, and weeds grew upon the steps. On both sides, the thatched halls and shrines were leaning, their tiles covered by creeping vines.
One must tuck in one’s feet when walking along the path; one must bow deeply upon entering through the low gate. When inquiring of the neighbors, they all knew the facts:
that for a long time there had been no monks, and that all the permanent assets had been seized by the government offices.

Only the Dharma Hall remained; who would care whether the two rains drenched the Buddha images? Observing the surroundings closely, it appears quite remote from the secular world. Since the mountains and waters come before the monastery gates, how could they have been abandoned for so long?
Moved by the spiritual resonance of the dragon deities, the monastery spontaneously began its restoration. When first establishing the layout, I was only twenty-five years old;
by the time the foundations were completed, I had reached thirty. Having received imperial silk brocade decrees from the court, I applied my mind and strength to contribute wealth and goods.

Borrowing as circumstances required, the expenses did not fall short of a thousand strings of cash. Exhausting my efforts in the search for resources, I have fortunately fulfilled my original aspiration from beginning to end.
A single vow. Amidst ten trials and nine hardships, ten thousand sufferings and a thousand pains, I relied upon the power of the Buddha for support therein;
I am glad that my karmic affinity with the Sangha was secured there. That year, by fortunate chance, I received the transmission of the Patriarch’s formless three robes;

the following year, through good fortune, I was appointed by the Prefectural Office to concurrently manage the lotus fields and communal merits of two locations, serving as the abbot of Longquan at this monastery. Thus have I traveled back and forth.
For several years, he has engaged in this cycle, adjudicating three public cases. His past debts have been cleared, totaling five hundred *suo*;
his karmic ties to the *kāṣāya* have been formed with two or three individuals. All of this is due to his diligent labor year after year;

it is entirely through following conditions with frugality that he has dug wells and opened ponds to facilitate irrigation, constructed bridges and leveled roads for the convenience of passersby, and expanded his estates to receive guests from the ten directions. Flowers...

The remaining fruits were offered throughout the three realms. The foundation was laid and the entire temple was completed; the halls and buildings were renovated, resplendent with gold and green glaze.
The sacred countenances were re-carved and adorned with brilliant colors, and banners and flowers were arrayed as offerings.

I burn incense and light candles in worship and reliance, to repay the four debts of gratitude above and to support the three realms of existence below. Let it not be said that the Way-gate lacks efficacy;
I fear only that the human heart is not steadfast. Having reached my fortieth year, I rejoice that my life’s aspirations have been fulfilled.

With a mind clarified of myriad anxieties, I dwell in peace according to my karmic conditions: I sew fine cotton and coarse cloth robes as time permits, and pass each day with a bowl of gruel and wild vegetables.

If you wish to seek the discourse on non-arising, you must extend your years for a long time. Simply ensure that the ground of your mind is level and even, and you may be certain that the dragons and devas will provide protection.
This is the inscription for the founding and construction of the mountain monastery.

At Ryūsen-in on Kōfūzan, I have observed that this temple has long lacked an abbot. The halls and buildings are collapsing, the gates and corridors are in ruins, and upon a single glance, the rafters and beams are all decayed.
Thorns and brambles grow everywhere around it; having stood for many years, its dilapidation grows ever more severe. Fortunately—

The three-bay Dharma Hall still remains; alas, the monastery gates are entirely destitute of anything. Those who see it feel sorrow in their hearts, and those who hear of it raise sighs of lamentation.
(De-in) received an official dispatch from the Prefectural Office appointing him to sweep and maintain the grounds, and he accepted the donor’s formal invitation to serve as the abbot.
Although it is said that there have been periods of decline and revival, how could one simply sit by and watch its rise and fall?

Therefore, with a resolute mind and all-out effort, we sought to reform the old and establish the new. Thus, drawing upon the resources of our robes and alms bowls, we extensively procured timber and gathered craftsmen to rebuild the monastery grounds.
We constructed a Dharma Hall of nine bays and five bays, and established a dormitory of seven...
The five-bay central hall was likewise completed, reaching up to the construction of the triple gate.
Furthermore, the two corridors were renovated, seventy-three Buddha statues were gilded and sculpted within the hall, and eighty-four sacred images were painted upon the walls.
Forty-nine scrolls of the *Sūtra of Merit for Responding to Conditions* were enshrined, and twelve sections of the true exegesis of the *Tripiṭaka* were designated.
He fashioned vessels to accommodate those who came and went, planted flowers and fruits to present as offerings, constructed bridges and roads, and dug wells and ponds.
He increased the sources of taxation by more than six hundred, to provide for the permanent endowment of the monastery forever, without decay throughout the ages.

The total expenditure exceeded three thousand *guan*. From the outset, this was not accomplished through the collective efforts of the assembly; rather, by the grace of its successful completion, I have sought to extend my celebratory repentance.

I have commissioned my fellow practitioners to establish two assemblies for the Water-Land ritual—one for the netherworld and one for the living—and have arranged a great vegetarian feast to make offerings to the myriad spirits of Heaven, Earth, and the Water Treasury.
By gathering these roots of goodness, I may slightly fulfill my long-held aspiration and look upward to offer prayers for [the deceased].
May this one person be blessed with boundless longevity; may the rank and emolument of the officials increase; may the long life and auspiciousness of the donors be extended.

Furthermore, we hope that the mountain gate (the Sangha) will flourish ever more, and that the conduct of the monks shall remain forever peaceful. May all share equally in this grace, as the heavens and the human realm look on with brilliant discernment.
Year, Month, and Day. Respectfully recorded.
